# DISEÑO FINAL — GPT-2 vs CodeLlama-7B en RepoBench-Python `cross_file_first` (design-only)

**Etiqueta global:** esto es un diseño. **No se ha ejecutado ningún experimento y no hay ningún valor de rendimiento en este documento.** Solo hay parámetros de diseño, reglas de decisión y bandas de coste *estimadas analíticamente* (etiquetadas como tales). Etiqueta en cada punto: **[HECHO]** (verificado aquí con comandos), **[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]** (RepoBench/RepoCoder/modelos, no verificable sin datos ni red), **[PARÁMETRO]** (decisión de diseño congelada).

---

## 1) Pregunta y endpoint primario pre-registrados

**Pregunta.** Con la misma información de contexto cross-file, ¿en qué se diferencia el completado de una línea de código (RepoBench-Python, spec `cross_file_first` propia, §2) entre un modelo pequeño no especializado (GPT-2-124M base) y un modelo de código de 7B (CodeLlama-7B base), y cuánta de la diferencia atribuible a "modelo grande" desaparece al neutralizar la asimetría de ventana de contexto?

**Endpoint primario (único, pre-registrado).** **Edit Similarity (ES) media** sobre los N=500 ejemplos de la semilla 13, condición **C1**, **k=1**, zero-shot, greedy temp=0, contraste pareado por ejemplo CodeLlama-7B − GPT-2-124M.
- **Hipótesis confirmatoria única:** ΔES = ES(CodeLlama) − ES(GPT-2) > 0 (criterio en §7).
- Semillas 42 y 7 = **réplicas de robustez** (no confirmatorias). k=0/3/5, C2, contexto aleatorio y few-shot = **secundarios/exploratorios**.
- Endpoint secundario de apoyo en la misma celda: **EM normalizado** pareado (base del test exacto de McNemar).

**Qué NO se afirma.** Ningún valor numérico de ES/EM; ninguna comparabilidad con las tablas publicadas de RepoCoder (§2.4); ninguna afirmación general sobre "modelos pequeños vs grandes" (un lenguaje, un split, dos modelos).

---

## 2) Definiciones operativas (con etiqueta en cada punto)

### 2.1 Spec propia de `cross_file_first` — **[PARÁMETRO] + [SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**
Definición congelada por el researcher, no verificable contra la fuente (**[HECHO]**: sin datos RepoBench y sin red en este entorno):
- Tarea **next-line completion** del split **cross-file** de RepoBench-Python: dado `file_path` y el prefijo `pre_code` (todo lo anterior al cursor), generar la continuación de la línea de referencia.
- Contexto cross-file: **k=1** = **primer fichero del ranking de contexto** (ranking congelado, §2.5).
- Recorte del fichero de contexto: **primeras M=128 líneas**.
- Presupuesto C1: **1024 tokens del tokenizer GPT-2** total, **≈924 contexto / 100 reservados a generación**.

**Lecturas alternativas descartadas** (cada una cambiaría el experimento):
1. "first" = primer fichero del repo por **orden alfabético** de ruta (no usa ranking).
2. "first" = **primera instancia/split** del test (convertiría el rótulo en un muestreo, no en una condición de contexto).
3. "first" = **nombre de config concreta del repo original** (p. ej. config HF `cross_file_first`) con su propia plantilla/campos (posiblemente `next_file_path` + varios ficheros). Descartada **por inaccesible, no por improbable**: es la alternativa de mayor riesgo para la validez externa.
4. "first" = primer fragmento **por tokens** del fichero recuperado en vez del primer **fichero** (mezclaría dos ejes de recorte).

### 2.2 Ensamblado del prompt (idéntico para ambos modelos) — **[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]** plantilla + **[PARÁMETRO]** reglas
Plantilla estilo RepoCoder (texto exacto a congelar en `template.py` versionado; la redacción es supuesta):

```
{HEADER: "You are an intelligent code editor. ... Files that may be helpful for your incoming completion:"}
[Context file 1 = ranking[0]]
<primeras 128 líneas del fichero>

Next statement:
<pre_code del fichero objetivo>
```

**Recorte en C1 (orden de prioridad, mismo algoritmo para ambos):**
1. Reservar 100 tokens de generación + tokens fijos de plantilla (medidos en calibración).
2. Incluir el fichero de contexto (primeras 128 líneas o lo que quepa, cortando **desde el final**).
3. Añadir `pre_code` completo.
4. Si desborda 1024 tokens GPT-2: recortar **primero el fichero de contexto** (desde el final) y solo después `pre_code` **desde la cabecera**, preservando **siempre la última línea incompleta** de `pre_code` (el prefijo de completado nunca se toca).
5. El presupuesto se mide siempre con el **tokenizer de GPT-2** como vara común.

**Consecuencia declarada:** en C1 el prompt es **byte a byte idéntico** para ambos modelos (**[PARÁMETRO]** auditado con `sha256(prompt_text)` por ejemplo y aserción de igualdad). Como los tokenizadores difieren (GPT-2 BPE 50257 vs Llama 32000, **[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**), CodeLlama tendrá menos tokens y **no sufrirá truncado en C1**; se reportan ambos conteos como covariable descriptiva.

**Post-procesado** (**[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**, protocolo RepoBench): cortar la generación en el primer `\n`, quitar whitespace final; EM/ES se calculan sobre ese span. Decodificación greedy `do_sample=False`, `max_new_tokens=100`.

### 2.3 C1 vs C2 — **[PARÁMETRO]**
- **C1 (presupuesto compartido, primaria):** contenido idéntico, tope 1024 tokens GPT-2. Responde *"¿con la MISMA información gana el modelo de código?"*.
- **C2 (ventana nativa, secundaria):** mismo ensamblado y orden, presupuesto elevado a la ventana del modelo (**4096** para CodeLlama, para acotar prefill; M del fichero de contexto sube de 128 a 1024 líneas y entran más ficheros del ranking que quepan). Responde *"¿cuánto añade explotar la ventana nativa?"*.
- **Identidad estructural:** para GPT-2 **C2 ≡ C1 por construcción** (ventana dura 1024 por posicionales aprendidas, **[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**). Por tanto **C2−C1 es una cantidad definida solo para CodeLlama** y se interpreta como coste/beneficio de la ventana, no como comparación entre modelos.
- **Sesgo declarado:** en C1 CodeLlama queda deliberadamente infra-utilizado (<15% de su ventana); se reporta el % de ventana usada por modelo en cada corrida.

### 2.4 Nota obligatoria de no-comparabilidad
> **NOTA.** `cross_file_first` es una **spec propia de este estudio** (k=1 fichero de contexto, recorte a 128 líneas, presupuesto 1024 tokens GPT-2 en C1), definida sin acceso a los datos ni al código de RepoBench/RepoCoder. Por tanto **los números de este experimento NO son comparables con las tablas publicadas de RepoCoder/RepoBench** y no deben citarse como réplica; solo son comparables **entre los brazos internos** del experimento.

### 2.5 Retrieval congelado por adelantado — **[PARÁMETRO] + [SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**
Antes de generar la primera salida se materializa `retrieval_lock.jsonl` (por ejemplo: lista ordenada de ficheros de contexto + hash de contenido). Fuente por orden de preferencia: (a) campos de retrieval ya presentes en los datos de RepoBench si existen; (b) **BM25 determinista** reimplementado y ejecutado una sola vez. **[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]**: no sé si la versión publicada usa ground-truth o un retriever aprendido; afecta a la calidad del fichero "first" (amenaza §6.6). El mismo lock alimenta C1, C2, todos los k y ambos modelos; aserción automática de que el ranking no cambia entre condiciones.

### 2.6 Few-shot (solo sensibilidad) — **[PARÁMETRO]**
Zero-shot primario. Sensibilidad 1-shot y 3-shot en C1/k=1 con ejemplos idénticos, mismo orden, mismo texto, seleccionados con semilla fija **fuera** del test. Regla de recorte idéntica para ambos y orden de sacrificio fijo: **primero ejemplos (del último al primero), luego fichero de contexto, luego `pre_code` por cabecera**. En GPT-2 el few-shot es concatenación en bruto, sin marcas de rol ni formato instruct.

---

## 3) Brazos, controles y ablaciones

### 3.1 Brazos de modelo
| Brazo | Modelo | Rol | Etiqueta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | GPT-2-124M **base**, por continuación | sujeto pequeño | [SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]: base, no instruct, ventana 1024 |
| **M2** | CodeLlama-7B **base** (no instruct) por continuación, greedy temp=0 | sujeto de código | gated; sustitución pre-escrita en §5.3 |

Sin brazo instruct y **sin brazo RepoCoder** (decisión del researcher: los checkpoints RepoCoder son retrieval-augmented, cambiarían la identidad del modelo y desviarían la pregunta); se menciona **solo como trabajo futuro**.

### 3.2 Parrilla y tiers
| Tier | Condición | k | Modelos | N | Semillas | Rol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 confirmatorio** | C1 zero-shot | 1 | M1, M2 | 500 | 13, 42, 7 | endpoint primario |
| T2 | C1 | 0 | M1, M2 | 500 | 13 | línea base sin contexto |
| T2 | C1 | 3, 5 | M1, M2 | 500 | 13 | pendiente de contexto |
| T2 | C2 | 1, 5 | M2 (M1: C2≡C1) | 500 | 13 | efecto de ventana |
| T2 | C1 **contexto aleatorio** | 1 | M1, M2 | 500 | 13 | control de especificidad |
| T3 (si el presupuesto §5 lo permite) | C1 1-shot / 3-shot | 1 | M1, M2 | 200 | 13 | sensibilidad few-shot |

**Control de contexto aleatorio (crítico):** mismo nº de ficheros, mismo recorte, mismo presupuesto, pero el fichero de contexto es **otro fichero del mismo repo** con semilla fija y sin relación con la posición del cursor (si el repo tiene <2 ficheros, se toma un fichero de otro repo del mismo dominio). Separa "ganó por información útil" de "ganó por más tokens".

**k>1 en C1:** el presupuesto restante se reparte de forma determinista y equitativa entre ficheros (primeras líneas, orden del ranking); se registran las **líneas efectivas entrantes por fichero** (en C1, k=5 implica ficheros muy truncados y debe ser visible).

### 3.3 Separar "fallo de formato" de "no usa el contexto" — **[PARÁMETRO]**
Métricas de formato por ejemplo (independientes de la corrección semántica):
- `f_no_newline`: no corta en `\n` dentro de `max_new_tokens` (no acata next-line).
- `f_repeat_pre`: copia/continúa el final de `pre_code` (solape ≥15 caracteres o ≥3 tokens).
- `f_empty` / `f_maxlen`: salida vacía / agota los 100 tokens (proxy de no-parada).
- `f_trunc_prompt`: el prompt sufrió recorte por presupuesto.
- `f_ast`: `pre_code` + salida no parsea con `ast.parse` (ni tras dedent).

**Matriz diagnóstica 2×2 pre-especificada** (usa el contexto / no la usa × formato OK / formato roto), con dos contrastes distintos:
- **Acatamiento** = 1 − tasa(`f_no_newline` ∪ `f_repeat_pre` ∪ `f_empty`), reportado **por modelo y por k**; la tasa en **k=0** separa "no entiende la tarea" de "le pierde el presupuesto de 1024".
- **Uso del contexto:** *ganancia* = ES(k=1 real) − ES(k=0); *especificidad* = ES(k=1 real) − ES(k=1 aleatorio). "Usa el contexto" exige **ambos** > 0 con IC bootstrap pareado excluyendo 0. Ganar solo en el primero ⇒ aprovechó **más tokens**, no la **relación cross-file**.
- **Subconjunto de formato compartido** (solo ejemplos donde AMBOS acatan): se reporta **explícitamente como descriptivo y con sesgo de selección (collider)**, nunca como endpoint primario.

---

## 4) Muestra, semillas y plan de análisis

**Muestra.** **N=500** del split Python cross-file, **estratificado** por: (a) nº de ficheros candidatos del repo (1, 2–5, >5); (b) longitud de `pre_code` (terciles); (c) si el fichero de contexto coincide con el propio `file_path` (sí/no → control de contaminación in-file). Muestreo sin reemplazo, determinista por semilla.

**Semillas y determinismo.** **13 confirmatoria; 42 y 7 réplicas disjuntas.** Con greedy temp=0 la generación es determinista: las semillas afectan solo a la selección del subconjunto y al orden de lotes. Riesgo declarado: *batch-invariance* en CPU puede alterar el último bit → **tamaño de lote fijo** + **test de determinismo** (50 ejemplos repetidos con lote distinto; se exige 100% de salidas idénticas; si falla, se declara y se fija lote=1).

**Análisis pareado** (mismos ejemplos en ambos modelos → pareado, no dos muestras):
- **EM (raw y normalizado):** tablas discordantes b/c → **McNemar exacto** + OR con IC95% + **tasa de discordancia** (b+c)/N.
- **ES y métricas continuas:** **bootstrap pareado, 1000 remuestreos sobre ejemplos** (semilla del bootstrap fijada, p. ej. 20261022), IC percentil 95%, re-muestreando el ejemplo entero (todos sus brazos juntos, para que los contrastes de pendientes queden bien pareados).
- **Tamaños de efecto obligatorios junto a cada p-valor:** ΔES absoluto con IC; **d_z pareada** con corrección de Hedges; ΔEM con IC; **pendientes de contexto** ES(k)−ES(k=0) por modelo y su **diferencia de diferencias** (interacción modelo × k) con IC bootstrap pareado — estadístico central de H2.
- **Precisión planeada (aritmética, no medida):** MDE ≈ 2,8·σ_d/√N para α=0,05 dos colas y ~80% de poder; con N=500 y **σ_d supuesta** en banda 0,18–0,30 → MDE en banda **~0,02–0,04** en ES. Se **recalcula con σ_d estimada en la calibración N=20**; si el MDE supera 0,10, el estudio se declara descriptivo (§5.2).
- **Multiplicidad:** familia confirmatoria pequeña (H1 + EM de apoyo) corregida con **Holm**; todo lo demás etiquetado como exploratorio y reportado sin corrección, con la etiqueta visible.
- **Reporte por subconjunto:** cada resultado por semilla + pooled (media y rango 13/42/7); si el signo no se mantiene en las tres, se marca como inestable.
- **Scorer:** factible con stdlib (**[HECHO]**, prototipo ejecutado en `/tmp/proto/scorer.py`: Levenshtein O(n·m), ES=1−lev/max(len), EM raw y normalizado, `ast.parse` con reintento tras dedent). Sus salidas son comprobaciones sintéticas de plumbing con entradas fabricadas a mano (`ES=1.0` en coincidencia exacta, `ES=0.231` en una transposición falsa inventada, `AST_ok True/False`), **no** salidas de modelo.

**Artefactos congelados/registrados:** `config.yaml` (plantilla versionada, presupuestos, seeds), `template.py`, `retrieval_lock.jsonl`, `subsample_{13,42,7}.jsonl`, `prompts_hash.jsonl`, JSONL de salidas (tokens de prompt por modelo, tokens generados, texto crudo), `scores.jsonl`, y manifest de sustitución de modelo (§5.3) con timestamp **anterior** a la primera generación.

---

## 5) Factibilidad honesta

### 5.1 Estado real del entorno — **[HECHO]**
Sin red (DNS caído, `curl` falla), sin GPU, sin `torch`/`transformers`/`datasets`/`numpy`/`editdistance`, sin pesos, sin datos, con **Python 3.14.4**. → **este nodo no puede ejecutar el diseño**: hay que aprovisionar un entorno con **Python 3.11/3.12 fijado** (3.14 es un riesgo real de wheels de torch/transformers), `transformers` fijado por versión y CPU-only.
Nodo observado: **224 cores, 2011 GB RAM (1937 disponibles), ~1 TB libres en tmpfs**, **Intel Xeon Platinum 8570** con **`avx512_bf16`, `avx512_vnni`, `amx`, `avx2`** (**[HECHO]** vía `/proc/cpuinfo`); esos flags hacen *plausible* la inferencia bf16 de 7B en CPU (**[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]** su magnitud), pero **no** son una medición de throughput.

### 5.2 Puerta obligatoria 0: micro-benchmark de calibración N=20
Antes de cualquier corrida confirmatoria, N=20 ejemplos (subconjunto de la semilla 13) por celda de T1+T2, midiendo por modelo×condición×k: tokens reales del prompt (ambos tokenizadores), **prefill tok/s**, **decode tok/s**, RSS máximo, y fracción con `f_trunc_prompt`. Es ingeniería, no un resultado del estudio.

**Regla de proyección y decisión pre-especificada:** `horas(celda) = N × (prompt_toks/prefill_tps + gen_toks/decode_tps)`
- ≤ **6 h** por celda y ≤ **24 h** de pared para todo T1 → se mantiene **N=500**.
- Si no: **N=200**. Si sigue > 6 h/celda: **N=100** y el estudio pasa a **exploratorio-descriptivo** con MDE recalculado, y así se escribe.
- **N nunca se reduce tras mirar ES/EM de ningún brazo**; la decisión usa solo métricas de throughput y queda registrada con timestamp.
- Palancas declaradas antes de bajar N: lote fijo multi-hilo con afinidad, **bf16 con AMX/AVX512-BF16**, o cuantización int8/int4 (si se cuantifica, **ambos** brazos en la misma precisión, porque cuantizar solo a M2 rompe el pareado).
- **C2-k=5 es la celda cara** (prefill dominado): si no cabe, se recorta **primero C2-k5, luego T3, y nunca T1**; si T1 y C2 no caben juntos, se ejecuta T1 y C2 queda como trabajo futuro declarado, no como "no hubo efecto".

### 5.3 Criterio de sustitución de M2, escrito ANTES de correr
Si al aprovisionar (antes de la primera generación) CodeLlama-7B no está disponible bajo su licencia de investigación, sustituir por el primer candidato que cumpla el orden de desempate fijo: **(1)** pesos *base* no-instruct disponibles, **(2)** ≈7B parámetros, **(3)** ventana ≥ 4096 (necesaria para C2), **(4)** licencia usable sin gate para investigación, **(5)** pretraining explícito en código. Candidatos en orden: **DeepSeek-Coder-7B-Base**, luego **StarCoderBase-7B**. Reglas: sustitución aplicada a **todas** las celdas y semillas; registrada en el manifest con timestamp previo a la primera generación; **prohibido** sustituir tras calcular cualquier métrica; prohibido mezclar modelos entre C1 y C2; en el informe se usa el nombre real del modelo (si se sustituyó, se declara la pérdida de alineación con la literatura).

### 5.4 Coste esperado — **BANDAS ESTIMADAS, NO MEDIDAS**
Parámetros declarados: greedy, ~32 tokens generados de media (tope 100), prompt medio C1 ≈900 tokens, N=500 → ~0,42 M tokens-ejemplo por celda T1.
- **GPT-2-124M** (~0,5 GB fp32): **minutos** por celda; T1+T2 despreciable.
- **CodeLlama-7B en C1** (~4 GB int8/int4 o ~13 GB bf16): **varias horas por celda**, banda gruesa **~2–10 h** con N=500 en CPU; **C2/k=5** multiplica esa banda por el prefill de miles de tokens.
- **Huella total** (T1 3 semillas + T2 1 semilla + controles, ambos modelos ≈ decenas de celdas de N=500): **de ~1 a ~2+ días de CPU** en el peor caso; de ahí el tiering y la puerta de calibración.
- Explícito para evitar lecturas erróneas: **todas estas cifras son bandas analíticas con throughput supuesto**; la fuente autoritativa será §5.2.

---

## 6) Amenazas a la validez y limitaciones
1. **Ventana (confuso principal).** C1 neutraliza la ventana a costa de infra-usar a CodeLlama; C2−C1 solo está definido para CodeLlama (C2≡C1 en GPT-2). Ninguna condición elimina del todo el confuso; se reportan ambas y se interpreta la brecha.
2. **Tokenizer asimétrico.** Mismo texto, distinto recuento. Acotar por tokens GPT-2 da holgura a CodeLlama; además GPT-2 comprime peor el código, así que "1024 tokens" ≈ **menos líneas de código real** para GPT-2 → se reportan líneas_effectivas_entrantes por modelo para hacer visible la asimetría residual.
3. **ES sensible a estilo:** un modelo verbose puntúa mal sin estar equivocado; por eso ES va con EM, AST y métricas de formato.
4. **GPT-2 puede fallar por acatamiento, no por contexto:** si su tasa de formato válido es muy baja, ES mide en parte "quién obedece el formato". Mitigación: matriz 2×2, k=0 como base, subconjunto de formato compartido (descriptivo, con su collider declarado).
5. **`cross_file_first` es spec propia** (§2.1/§2.4): no comparable con RepoCoder; riesgo máximo si la config real homónima tiene otra semántica (lectura descartada #3).
6. **Calidad del retrieval "first"** no verificada: si lo publicado usa ground-truth y nosotros BM25, el contexto es más débil y las pendientes k se aplanan para ambos (el pareado interno se mantiene; la magnitud absoluta, no).
7. **Tamaño del split no verificado** (**[SUPUESTO-DOMINIO]** ~4,5k ejemplos en Python cross-file next-line): si fuera mucho menor, N=500 dejaría de ser submuestra pequeña → se cuenta el nº real de filas antes de muestrear.
8. **Gated weights y reproducibilidad:** dependencia de licencia (§5.3, a costa de desalineación con la literatura) y de versión de `transformers` (fijada; riesgo agravado por Python 3.14 en el nodo actual).
9. **Greedy-only:** no hay varianza de muestreo de generación; las semillas cubren solo la varianza de submuestreo.
10. **Alcance:** un lenguaje, un split, un modelo pequeño (una familia, 124M) y un modelo de 7B. Escalado a GPT-2-medium/large y el brazo RepoCoder quedan como trabajo futuro.
11. **Determinismo numérico en CPU** (batch-invariance): lote fijo + test de determinismo, a posible costa de throughput.

---

## 7) Criterios de éxito/fallo pre-especificados (umbral de relevancia práctica Δ=0,05 en ES, a priori)

**H1 — "mejor con la misma información"** (C1, k=1, zero-shot, semilla 13)
- **Éxito:** ΔES > +0,05 **y** IC95% del bootstrap pareado con extremo inferior > 0 (Holm en la familia), con ΔEM normalizado positivo y McNemar p<0,05, **y** mismo signo en las réplicas 42 y 7.
- **Fallo:** IC incluye 0, o ΔES ≤ 0,05, o el signo no se replica.
- **Gate interpretativo (no éxito/fallo):** si la tasa de formato válido de GPT-2 es < 30%, el resultado de H1 **debe** encabezarse advirtiendo que mide en parte acatamiento de formato.

**H2 — "pendiente de contexto diferenciada"** (k ∈ {0,1,3,5} en C1, semilla 13)
- **Éxito (ambos componentes necesarios):** (a) **interacción** modelo×k (diferencia de diferencias de ES(k=5)−ES(k=0)) con IC95% excluyendo 0 a favor de CodeLlama; **y** (b) **especificidad**: en CodeLlama, ES(k=1 real) − ES(k=1 aleatorio) > 0 con IC excluyendo 0, mientras que en GPT-2 ese contraste tiene IC incluyendo 0.
- **Fallo:** pendientes superponibles. **Hallazgo válido, no fallo de experimento:** CodeLlama gana en k=5 vs k=0 pero **no** en real-vs-aleatorio ⇒ conclusión obligatoria "añadió tokens, no relación cross-file".
- **Fallo de diseño:** si en C1 k=3/k=5 quedan < ~10 líneas efectivas por fichero, el barrido no es interpretable y se reporta así (usando las líneas entrantes registradas, no a posteriori).

**H3 — "coste/beneficio de la ventana"** (C2 vs C1 en CodeLlama, k=1 y k=5)
- **Éxito:** ES(C2) − ES(C1) > 0 con IC95% excluyendo 0.
- **Nulo/fallo:** IC incluyendo 0 ⇒ la ventaja de la condición naive **no** proviene de la ventana, y la brecha H1 no es un artefacto de ventana (conclusión a favor de C1).
- **Obligatorio:** reportar C2−C1 como el número que separa "ventana" de "pretraining/arquitectura", junto al % de ventana usada por modelo, recordando que C2−C1 no está definido para GPT-2.

**H4 (descriptiva pre-especificada, sin criterio de éxito):** por modelo y k, reportar `f_no_newline`, `f_repeat_pre`, `f_empty`, `f_maxlen`, `f_ast`, longitud generada media y `f_trunc_prompt`; su función es hacer auditable la interpretación de H1–H3.

**Criterio global de ejecución válida.** El estudio es reportable si están T1 completo (3 semillas) + k=0 + contexto aleatorio + matriz de formato, todos con ICs y tamaños de efecto; retrieval congelado; prompts idénticos por hash en C1; y la nota de no-comparabilidad con RepoCoder presente. Si falta T1, **no hay resultado**, por muchas celdas secundarias que se hayan corrido.

【一、输入与环境核查（事实性结果）】

1. /workspace 仓库内容：
   - 仅含 1 个文件：task.json（491 B，JSON），内含任务 question/context 及 documents.track.md 字段。
   - 不存在任何 RepoBench 数据文件、代码、模型权重或评测脚本；无 JSONL 数据集可检视。track.md 未以独立文件存在于文件系统（全盘 find 无结果），其内容仅嵌入 task.json："Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."（设计型任务，不要求仓库与算力——已确认）。
   - 文件系统盘近乎写满（挂载点仅剩 ~11G 可用），对后续（若需）存放 7B 权重是关键约束（fp16 约 13.5GB 放不下，需 Q4 级量化约 3.9GB 或改用其他挂载点）。

2. 运行环境（实测事实）：
   - Python 3.14.4（/usr/bin/python3），pip 25.1.1 可用；
   - torch / transformers / datasets / accelerate / numpy 均未安装（全部 ModuleNotFoundError）；未安装任何东西；
   - network 已禁用：DNS 解析失败（socket.gaierror），无代理环境变量；
   - GPU：nvidia-smi 二进制存在但无任何 /dev/nvidia* 设备节点 → 无可加速卡；
   - CPU：nproc=224，与 cpu_affinity_count=224 一致；
   - 附加风险事实：Python 3.14 过新，主流 ML wheel（torch/transformers）对 3.14 的兼容支持存疑，即使有网络也可能装不上。

【二、拟定方法（高层轮廓，供审阅）】

1. 数据切分与输入构造：
   - 采用官方 RepoEval next-line completion、cross_file 检索设置、Python 测试集（论文报告 2,000 条测试样本；按语言过滤为 Python）。注意："cross_file_first" 这一确切设置在本地无任何材料可核实，拟定其操作化为"cross_file 设置下按官方顺序的前 N 条（如前 1,000/2,000 条）测试样本"或"首轮检索(first-pass retrieval)变体"，具体含义列为待您确认的核实项（见三）。
   - 输入构造（next-line）：prompt = [跨文件上下文块] + [目标文件光标前内容]，模型续写当前行直至换行符。跨文件上下文按官方格式将检索到的其他文件代码块前置拼接（每块带文件路径与行号注释头）。
   - 检索器：遵循官方默认（拟定 BM25，官方同时提供 SBERT 变体）；每样本从同仓库其他文件取 top-k 片段，按排名从高到低填装至提示预算。
   - 截断策略：统一 token 预算（拟定 max_prompt=1024，另做 {0(=self_only 对照), 512, 1024} 敏感性组）；优先保留光标前的本文件后缀，跨文件片段从低排名开始丢弃；两模型分词器不同，预算以各自 tokenizer 计。GPT-2 上下文上限 1024 是硬约束，CodeLlama-7b 远大于此——需在结果解释中显式处理该不对等（例如同报"各自最大可用预算"结果）。

2. 指标草案与解码：
   - 主指标：完全匹配（exact match，官方规范化后比较）与编辑相似度（官方 calculate_edit_similarity，Levenshtein 归一化）。此二者为 RepoEval next-line 官方协议指标。
   - 拟定不纳入 pass@k：官方 next-line 协议无执行评测工具，pass@k 属其他基准惯例；若纳入须作为非官方附加分析并明确标注（待您裁定）。
   - 解码：主设置贪心解码（消除采样方差，利于两模型可比性）；附加每组 n=5 低温采样估计样本级方差（官方脚本据我记忆使用某种 top-p 采样默认值——此为未核实记忆，列为核实项）。

3. 无执行条件下的论证组织方式：
   - 合理性论证：与 RepoBench/RepoEval 论文及排行榜公开数字对齐（若论文含 GPT-2 与 CodeLlama-7b 的 cross-file EM/编辑相似度，则给出预期区间与方向性假设：GPT-2 在跨文件设置下 EM 接近个位数百分比，CodeLlama-7b 高一个量级左右；具体数字全部标为"待核实来源值"）。
   - 对照组设计：(a) self_only（无跨文件上下文）vs cross_file，对每个模型分别测"跨文件上下文增益/损害"，区分"模型能力差"与"利用检索上下文能力差"；(b) 空上下文下限对照；(c) 讨论性对照：GPT-2 与 CodeLlama-7b 同时混淆了参数量(124M vs 7B)与代码域预训练两个因素，设计中须声明此混淆，并列出可选增补（Llama-2-7b 隔离代码预训练效应），标注为超预算可选项。
   - 可行性分析：CPU 推理估算（CodeLlama-7b 约 1–3 tok/s/流 × ~128 新 token × 2,000 条 → 单流数天量级；利用 224 核分片 32–64 路并行可压至数小时；GPT-2 分钟级）；存储约束（11G 剩余 → 量化权重）；Python 3.14 兼容性风险与离线无法装包的硬限制——结论是即便解除 design-only 限制，本机也仅能以 CPU+量化方式小样本试跑。

【三、假设与不确定之处（均标为假设，非既定事实）】

payload.answer:
# 实验设计：GPT-2 vs CodeLlama-7b 在 RepoBench Python cross_file_first 设置上的表现比较（仅设计，未运行任何实验）

## 1. 术语与假设声明

**操作化定义（单一、全程一致使用）**：本设计将任务所称 "cross_file_first" 操作化为：RepoEval **next-line completion** 任务、**Python** 语言子集、**cross_file（检索式跨文件上下文）**设置，按官方测试集的给定顺序取**前 N=1,000 条**样本（若快照过滤 Python 后不足 1,000 条，则取全量并在报告中记录实际条数）。这是一个**假设性操作化，而非已核实事实**——本地仓库（仅 task.json）与离线环境均无法核实该名称的官方含义。

**若 "cross_file_first" 实指 first-pass 检索变体，需改动的环节**：仅第 2 节的跨文件上下文**来源构造**（检索通道/首轮检索配置）需替换，替换后提示拼接、样本集、截断规则、指标、解码、统计检验全部不变；两档预算与 self/cross 配对逻辑与检索配置正交，无需改动。本设计不同时评估两套定义。

其余显式假设（非既定事实）：
- A1 数据快照版本：以取得时官方发布（RepoBench 仓库 / HF repoeval 数据集）为准，落地时**钉死 revision 并记录 SHA256**；本文所有论文数值引用均标"待核实"。
- A2 检查点：openai-community/gpt2（124M）与 codellama/CodeLlama-7B-hf，各自钉死 commit hash。
- A3 官方提示模板细节（跨文件块头格式如 `#path:start-end`）凭记忆拟定，落地时以官方脚本字段为准；若官方 prompt 字段已拼好则直接采用。
- A4 官方评测脚本的默认解码参数（是否 top-p 采样、温度值）**未核实，不凭记忆填写数值**；本设计主设定不依赖之。

## 2. 数据与提示构造

- **数据**：RepoEval next-line completion 测试集 → 过滤 language=Python → 按官方顺序取前 1,000 条。每条样本记录：样本 id、repo、文件、光标行号、真值目标行、本文件光标前内容、官方检索块字段。
- **提示结构**：`[跨文件上下文块（按检索排名从高到低依次填装）] + [光标前本文件内容]`，模型续写一行。
- **截断规则（按各模型自身 tokenizer 计 token）**：
  1. 目标预算 B（见第 3 节预算档）；
  2. 跨文件块按排名顺序填装，预算不足时**从最低排名块整块丢弃**；
  3. **光标前本文件内容始终优先保留**；若本文件内容单独超出预算，截去其头部、保留紧邻光标的尾部。
- **self_only 条件**：仅"光标前本文件内容（同一截断规则的同一后缀文本）"，无任何跨文件块。与 cross_file 条件构成严格配对对照。

## 3. 模型与解码

| 项 | GPT-2 | CodeLlama-7b |
|---|---|---|
| 检查点 | openai-community/gpt2, 124M（钉死 revision） | codellama/CodeLlama-7B-hf（钉死 revision） |
| 上下文硬上限 | 1,024 token | 16,384 token |
| 精度 | fp32 | GPU: bf16；CPU: fp32 |
| padding | 左填充 | 左填充 |

- **解码（主设定，固定要求）**：两模型统一**贪心（do_sample=False）**，遇第一个换行符 `\n` 停止，`max_new_tokens=128` 上限。贪心→确定性，无需随机种子；记录 torch/transformers 版本哈希保证可复现。
- **预算档**：
  - **A 档（主比较，公平档）**：两模型统一 B=1,024 token（各自 tokenizer 计；恰为 GPT-2 上限）。
  - **B 档（仅解释性补充）**：CodeLlama B=4,096；GPT-2 无 B 档（等于 A 档）。**主结论只允许建立在 A 档**，B 档仅用于解释"更长跨文件上下文是否帮助 CodeLlama"，不得与"哪个模型更强"混谈。
- **可选（资源允许节）**：n=5 低温采样仅用于样本级方差估计；温度值此处**故意不填数值**——官方脚本默认属未核实假设（A4），若执行则由研究者指定并记录。

## 4. 对照组矩阵（条件 × 模型 × 预算档）

| # | 条件 | 模型 | 预算档 | 样本 | 角色 | 级别 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | cross_file | GPT-2 | A (1024) | 1,000 | 主比较 | 主 |
| P2 | cross_file | CodeLlama-7b | A (1024) | 1,000 | 主比较 | 主 |
| P3 | self_only | GPT-2 | A (1024) | 1,000 | 增益配对(P1−P3) | 主 |
| P4 | self_only | CodeLlama-7b | A (1024) | 1,000 | 增益配对(P2−P4) | 主 |
| S1 | cross_file | CodeLlama-7b | B (4096) | 1,000 | 能力上限参考 | 次（解释性） |
| S2 | empty（无本文件内容） | 两模型 | A | 1,000 | 下限对照 | 次（可选） |
| O1 | cross_file + self_only | Llama-2-7b | A (1024) | 同 1,000 条 | 拆解"代码预训练"因素 | 预算外可选 |

- **跨文件增益（固定定义）**：增益(模型) = 平均编辑相似度(cross) − 平均编辑相似度(self)，同模型、同提示后缀文本、同贪心解码，仅切换跨文件块有无；按样本 id **逐条配对**计算差值，报告均值与配对 bootstrap 95% CI。
- O1 的预算内最小可行版本：同样本子集、同 A 档预算、同贪心解码、仅 P1'/P3' 两格——用于（若追加）将"GPT-2↔CodeLlama 差异"部分分解为规模与代码预训练，但见第 8 节归因约束。

## 5. 指标与统计检验

- **主指标（锁定两项）**：
  1. **EM**：续写行与真值行按官方规范化（strip 首尾空白）后完全匹配；
  2. **官方编辑相似度**：Levenshtein 归一化 1 − dist/max(len)，对齐官方 calculate_edit_similarity 定义（规范化细节以官方脚本为准，A3 级假设）。
- pass@k 不进入主分析，仅作一句扩展提及：若未来引入执行工具，可在同提示上扩展非官方 pass@k。
- **配对检验（按样本 id 配对）**：
  - EM 差值（模型间同题配对）：**McNemar 检验**；增益（条件间同题配对）同法。
  - 编辑相似度差值：**按样本 id 的配对 bootstrap**（10,000 次重采样，percentile 95% CI）+ Wilcoxon 符号秩检验为辅。
  - 主假设族仅 1–2 个对比，不做多重校正；次级/可选格标 exploratory。
- **统计功效（规划期近似，非测量）**：McNemar 正态近似下，α=0.05、80% 功效的最小可分辨 EM 差 ≈ 2.8·√(p_d/n)，p_d 为不一致对比例。设 p_d≈0.2（假设值）：n=1,000 → MDE≈4.0 个百分点；n=2,000 → ≈2.8 pp。编辑相似度：设配对差值 sd≈0.3（假设值），n=1,000 时差值 SE≈0.95pp。方向性假设预期两模型 EM 差距为数十个百分点量级（见第 6 节），远超 MDE，故 n=1,000 对主对比功效充足；对"跨文件增益"这类小效应（可能 <5pp），n=1,000 处于临界，若预算允许可扩至全量 2,000 条。

## 6. 预期方向性假设（全部为方向性预期；具体数字均标"待核实来源"，非已得结果）

- H1：CodeLlama-7b(A 档 cross) 的 EM 与编辑相似度**显著高于** GPT-2；方向预期：GPT-2 EM 为个位数百分比、CodeLlama 高一个量级（数量级参照 RepoBench 论文/RepoEval 排行榜公开数字——**待核实引用**）。
- H2：跨文件增益——CodeLlama 预期为正（能利用检索上下文），GPT-2 预期接近零或为负（小模型受长提示干扰）。
- H3：S1(B 档) ≥ S 无(A 档同模型)，即更长跨文件上下文对 CodeLlama 有帮助但非主结论依据。
- 以上任何数字在报告成文前不得表述为结果。

## 7. 可行性与预算（量级估计 + 敏感性，非测量事实）

- **计算量**：主网格 P1–P4 = 4×1,000 次生成，加 S1 共 5,000 次；每次 ≤128 新 token（预期均值 20–40，因换行早停）。时间公式 T = G·L/(R·r)，G=生成数、L=平均新 token、R=并发路数、r=单路 tok/s。
- **假设链（明示）**：r(CodeLlama, CPU, fp32) 取文献量级 0.5–3 tok/s（**未测量**）；R=32；L=30 → T ≈ 5,000×30/(32×[0.5–3]) ≈ **0.4–2.6 天**，对 r 有 6 倍敏感区间。GPT-2 各格合计分钟–小时级，可忽略。
- **目标执行环境（本设计的正式归宿）**：单张 ≥24GB GPU 上 bf16 推理 CodeLlama-7b，全网格数小时级；这是可移植的完整方案。
- **本机限制（非设计主体，仅试跑依据）**：即便解除 design-only 限制，本机因 (i) Python 3.14 下 torch/transformers wheel 兼容性存疑且离线无法装包、(ii) /workspace 挂载仅剩 ~11G（fp16 权重 13.5GB 放不下，须 Q4 量化 ~4GB 或换分区）、(iii) 无 GPU——**只能做极小样本冒烟试跑**（如 20 条 + 量化 GGUF），不足以产生任何正式结果。

## 8. 局限与后续可选项

- **归因约束（固定要求）**：GPT-2(124M, 通用预训练) vs CodeLlama-7b(7B, 代码预训练) 同时变动参数量与代码域预训练两因素。**结论只能表述为"两模型整体表现差异"**，不得归因于规模或代码预训练任一单一因素；如需归因，须追加 O1（Llama-2-7b，预算外可选项，最小可行版见第 4 节）。
- 其他局限：检索器与提示模板依赖官方字段（A3）；B 档仅解释性；贪心解码可能低估采样下的能力差异（A4 未核实官方默认）；方向性预期的论文数字引用待补页码/表号；"cross_file_first" 若证实为 first-pass 检索变体，仅第 2 节上下文来源需替换（第 1 节已述）。
- 产出物：逐样本 JSONL（预测、EM、编辑相似度、提示 token 数）+ 汇总表 + 版本锁定清单（数据 SHA256、模型 revision、库版本哈希）。

SCOPING PASS (no design committed, nothing run).

== 1) Inspection findings (verified in this environment) ==
Artifacts present: /workspace contains ONLY task.json (its "track.md" field states: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."). There are NO dataset files, NO RepoBench or CrossFileFirst splits, NO model weights, NO harness/eval scripts, NO cached completion files, NO config files anywhere on the filesystem (filesystem-wide find for *repobench*, *codellama*, *gpt-2*, *cross_file* returned zero hits; ~/.cache and ~/.cache/huggingface are absent/empty).
Runtime facts: Python 3.14.4 (notably very new — current torch/transformers wheels may not even support it). pip list shows NO ML/scientific stack: no torch, transformers, datasets, evaluate, numpy, scipy, pandas, sentencepiece, sacrebleu, nltk, accelerate (targeted grep across the full package list returned nothing; installed packages are OS/system tooling only). Hardware: CPU-only — nproc=224, ~2 TB RAM, no /dev/nvidia* devices, gpu_enabled=false. Network: DISABLED and confirmed (urllib to huggingface.co raises "Temporary failure in name resolution"; pip download fails).
Explicit statement: RepoBench Python 'cross_file_first' data and both model checkpoints (GPT-2, CodeLlama-7b) are ABSENT and CANNOT be obtained offline in this environment. Any execution would require a different environment with network access (or pre-staged data/weights) and an ML stack (torch/transformers) on a compatible Python (e.g., 3.10–3.12, not 3.14). The task itself is design-only per task.json, which is consistent.

== 2) Proposed approach outline (skeleton, pending your approval) ==
Models: "GPT-2" = openai-community/gpt2 (124M base causal LM, GPT-2 BPE tokenizer, native 1024-token context); optionally gpt2-large (774M) as a within-family scaling sensitivity arm. "CodeLlama-7b" = codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf (base code LM, 32k native context, SentencePiece tokenizer); optionally CodeLlama-7b-Instruct as a secondary arm if instruction variants are ruled in. Both run bf16/fp32; decoding is deterministic, so precision affects speed far more than ranking, but must be logged.
Unit of evaluation: RepoBench cross_file_first per the convention — one completion instance per target file, built from the FIRST file in the repository dependency/import graph that the target file depends on (cross-file prompt = first-dependency file content + target file prefix), ground truth = the following lines of the target file. Use the OFFICIAL pre-built RepoBench-P (v1.1) Python prompt files (cross_file_first split; clean/full variants) so dependency selection/retrieval is FIXED and IDENTICAL for both models; the comparison measures model quality, not retrieval quality.
Standardized decoding: greedy (do_sample=false), max_new_tokens=64 (RepoBench convention), RepoBench post-processing (cut generation at the first dedent/return to column 0), no repetition penalty, right-side prompt truncation to each model's context budget (see open question Q1).
Headline metrics on the FULL official Python cross_file_first test set (~1.7k line-level instances; if subsampled for cost, n>=625 for ~±4% MC error at 95%): (a) line-level Exact Match after RepoBench cleaning; (b) Edit Similarity (normalized Levenshtein); (c) codebleu/sacrebleu-BLEU as tertiary, with the caveat that corpus BLEU is unstable on short completions. Paired analysis: McNemar's test on per-instance EM between models; bootstrap CIs (10k resamples) on all metrics. Stratified reporting: by prompt-length bucket (<256 / 256–1k / >1k tokens) — where GPT-2's 1024 cap and truncation bite — by repository size, and a truncated-vs-untruncated decomposition separating "model weakness" from "context starvation." Compute cost (tokens/sec, wall-clock, FLOPs estimate) reported alongside. Since a parameter-matched comparison is impossible (no 7B GPT-2), the framing is explicitly "general-purpose small vs code-specialized mid-size," with scale-matched caveats as a written limitation, supported by the optional GPT-2-large arm to show within-family scaling direction.

== 3) Consequential assumptions/uncertainties for you to rule on ==
Q1. Context budget: hold both models to a common token budget (e.g., 1024 — equal input information, wastes CodeLlama's capacity), or let each use its native window (1024 vs 32k — "as-shipped")? My default: native as primary + shared-1024 secondary arm to isolate the context-length confound. Please rule.
Q2. Framing: accept that a parameter-matched comparison is impossible and treat this as "general small vs code-specialized mid-size" with mandatory scale caveats + optional GPT-2-large scaling arm? Or should a scale-proxy/per-parameter efficiency analysis be a headline component?
Q3. Compute-matched reporting: given the ~56x parameter gap (124M vs 7B), is per-token/per-FLOP normalized reporting REQUIRED as a headline section, or is a cost appendix sufficient?
Q4. Variants & precision: are CodeLlama Instruct/Python variants in scope (proposal: base-only primary, Instruct secondary)? Is precision/quantization (bf16 vs fp32 vs 8-bit) in scope, or fixed at bf16 for both? Note: this container's Python 3.14 likely cannot run torch at all; an execution-environment change is assumed if anything is ever run.
Q5. Retrieval/dependency selection: confirm that cross-file prompt construction is FIXED by the official pre-built RepoBench prompts (no re-implemented dependency selection), i.e., retrieval is explicitly out of the comparison.
Q6. Execution feasibility: given data/weights/network are absent here, confirm the deliverable is purely the design (per track.md); if a pilot is later desired, should I assume an alternate GPU-enabled networked environment, or drop pilot expectations entirely?

Inspection accepted and approach approved. Findings noted: no dataset/weights/harness present, no ML stack, network disabled, CPU-only, Python 3.14 — consistent with a design-only deliverable per track.md. Proceed to the final design. Rulings on your questions:

Q1 (context budget): Your default is approved, and it is the primary framing. Primary = each model at its native/deployable window (GPT-2 1024, CodeLlama-7b 32k, subject to a stated prompt-truncation cap so cost stays sane — declare the cap); secondary = shared 1024-token budget arm to isolate the context-length confound. Make the shared-budget arm a first-class section, not an afterthought: it is the only comparison that separates "worse model" from "context-starved model", and the truncated-vs-untruncated stratified decomposition you proposed is the mechanism. State explicitly which arm answers the question as asked (a deployed-capability comparison → native) and which answers the mechanism question (shared budget).

Q2 (framing): Accepted. This is explicitly a "general-purpose small vs code-specialized mid-size" capability contrast; a parameter-matched comparison is out of scope and you should say so as a limitation, not paper over it. Keep the GPT-2-large (774M) arm, but as a bounded within-family scaling sensitivity check (it may be reported on a stratified subsample, with the subsampling rule declared in advance), not as a headline result.

Q3 (compute): Middle ground. A cost/efficiency section is required in the body — wall-clock per instance, generated tokens, memory footprint, and a rough per-instance FLOP estimate for both models, plus EM-per-unit-cost — but a full compute-matched (iso-FLOP) analysis is out of scope for this question and belongs in limitations/future work. Rationale: the question asks how performance compares, and the ~56x scale gap makes iso-FLOP matching a different study.

Q4 (variants/precision): Primary = base checkpoints only (gpt2 124M, CodeLlama-7b-hf), both bf16, fixed and logged. Drop quantization as an experimental arm (note it as a logged constant with one sentence on expected non-effect under greedy decoding). Include CodeLlama-7b-Instruct ONLY if you can specify it without muddying the comparison: it is acceptable as a clearly separated secondary arm with the prompt-format difference spelled out (chat template vs raw continuation), and it must never be pooled with base results. Do not add CodeLlama-7b-Python as an arm — one extra code-specialized variant is enough scope creep; mention it as a design alternative not taken.

Q5 (retrieval): Confirmed as a requirement, not an assumption. Use the official pre-built RepoBench-P cross_file_first prompt files unmodified; no re-implemented dependency selection. Retrieval quality is explicitly out of the comparison and must be stated as a scope boundary. If the official clean/full split choice is ambiguous, pick one, justify it, and state the other as a robustness option.

Q6 (execution): Design-only, per track.md. Do not include pilot results or projected numbers, and do not describe a pilot as planned work in this environment. Include a short feasibility section that (a) states plainly that this container cannot execute the design (Python 3.14 vs the ML stack, no weights/data, no network, no GPU), (b) specifies the minimum execution environment the design would require (supported Python, GPU with enough VRAM for 7B bf16 inference, network or pre-staged artifacts), and (c) gives an honest inference-cost estimate for the full cross_file_first test set for both models so a reader can judge tractability.

- Rationale must explain each design choice in terms of what alternative it excludes.

Deliver the final design with: rationale, models/configurations, unit of evaluation and data provenance, decoding and post-processing protocol, metrics, analysis plan (primary, secondary context-budget arm, paired tests, stratifications), controls and held-constant factors, compute/feasibility section including the environment limitation above, and limitations/threats to validity. payload.answer:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing has been run and no outcomes are reported).

# 1. Question and claim structure
Primary question as asked: how do GPT-2 (124M) and CodeLlama-7B compare on RepoBench-P Python 'cross_file_first' completion, as deployed capability → answered by the NATIVE-context arm. Mechanism question (how much of any gap is "context starvation" vs model quality) → answered by the SHARED-1024-budget arm plus the truncated-vs-untruncated decomposition. Framing (per ruling Q2): an explicitly "general-purpose small vs code-specialized mid-size" capability contrast; a parameter-matched comparison is impossible (no 7B GPT-2, no 124M CodeLlama) and is a stated limitation, not adjusted away.

# 2. Data provenance and unit of evaluation
- Dataset: RepoBench-P v1.1, Python, cross-file setting with FIRST-DEPENDENCY prompts ("cross_file_first"), downloaded from the official RepoBench release (github.com/microsoft/RepoBench + HF). Official pre-built prompt files are used UNMODIFIED; no re-implemented dependency selection or retrieval. Retrieval quality is explicitly OUT of the comparison (scope boundary, per Q5).
- Split variant: primary = 'full' prompt variant (unmodified repository file contents), declared in advance, chosen because it is the faithful deployed condition and avoids a preprocessing step that could interact differently with the two models. The 'clean' variant is a pre-declared robustness replication (headline tables re-run on 'clean'; no cherry-picking — both reported). Exact cleaning semantics to be confirmed against the release README at data-staging time (data absent here).
- Unit: one completion instance per target file/line position as shipped: prompt = first-dependency file content + target-file prefix; reference = the following line(s) of the target file. Test set ≈1.7k line-level Python instances (design-time figure from the dataset card; exact count read from the staged split's metadata and recorded before any comparison).
- Instance alignment: both models evaluate the identical instance-ID list derived from the identical source prompt file. Rendered token sequences necessarily differ by tokenizer, but source text, ordering, IDs, and post-processing are identical.

# 3. Models and arms (per Q4 ruling)
| Arm | Model (HF checkpoint) | Role | Context budget | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | openai-community/gpt2 (124M base) | Primary "small general" | native 1024 (GPT-2 BPE) | full test set |
| B1 | codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf (base) | Primary "code mid-size" | native, capped at 8,192 tokens (declared) | full test set |
| B2 | CodeLlama-7b-hf | Shared-budget mechanism arm | 1,024 tokens (GPT-2-native-equivalent) | full test set |
| A2 | openai-community/gpt2-large (774M) | Bounded within-family scaling sensitivity | native 1024 | stratified subsample n=400 (rule in §6) |
| B3 | codellama/CodeLlama-7b-Instruct | Separated secondary arm | 8,192 cap | full test set; NEVER pooled with base arms |
Notes: (i) A1 doubles as the shared-budget GPT-2 run (native = 1024), stated openly; B2 is the budget-constrained CodeLlama. (ii) The 8,192 cap on B1/B3 is declared to bound prefill cost; the share of CodeLlama prompts exceeding 8,192 tokens is logged, and the cap is re-measured as a sensitivity if >20% of prompts are capped. (iii) Prompt format for B3: official Llama-2/CodeLlama chat template ([INST] with the RepoBench prompt verbatim as the user turn); base arms use raw continuation. Because prompt rendering differs, B3 is descriptive-only relative to A1/B1 and excluded from all paired confirmatory tests. (iv) CodeLlama-7b-Python is named as a design alternative NOT taken (one extra code-specialized variant is enough scope creep). (v) Precision fixed at bf16 for all arms, logged as a constant; quantization is dropped as an arm — under greedy decoding, modest quantization perturbs argmax ties only marginally and identically-in-kind across models, and it is a deployment rather than capability factor.

# 4. Decoding and post-processing protocol (fixed across arms)
- Decoding: greedy (do_sample=False, num_beams=1), max_new_tokens=64, no repetition/frequency penalty, no prefix caching differences (batched generation with per-sequence left padding; padding tokens masked).
- Truncation rule (declared): the target-file prefix (generation point) is ALWAYS preserved in full; if over budget, the first-dependency context portion is truncated from its interior, keeping the head (first k tokens) of the dependency file. Truncation event per (instance, arm) is logged as a boolean flag — this flag powers the §6 decomposition.
- Post-processing (RepoBench convention, identical for all arms): split generation to lines; keep line 1; keep subsequent lines only while they start with a whitespace character; stop at the first line whose first character is non-whitespace (dedent-to-column-0 cut); strip trailing whitespace. No model-specific post-processing.
- Determinism: greedy decoding, fixed model versions (git revisions recorded), single pass per instance. Generation failures: one retry in fp32; persistent failures marked "unavailable" with reason — never silently dropped (§6 missing-data rule).

# 5. Metric definitions (re-implementable)
Let p = post-processed model completion, r = reference completion (same line-keeping cut applied to nothing but the model output; references used as shipped), with per-line and whole-string comparisons on Unicode code points.
1. Exact Match (primary): EM(instance)=1 iff the line-sequence [l.strip() for l in p.splitlines()] equals that of r after stripping per line and after dropping trailing empty lines on both sides. Leading-indentation content is preserved up to strip() — i.e., EM is indentation-insensitive per line, matching the official RepoBench evaluation code, which strips before comparing (this convention is pinned by reading the official eval script at staging and recording it in the run manifest; if the official code compares without strip, that variant is adopted instead and noted).
2. Edit Similarity (co-primary): ES = 1 − Levenshtein(p′, r′) / max(len(p′), len(r′)), where p′, r′ are the stripped, newline-joined cleaned strings; convention: both empty → 1; exactly one empty → 0. Reported as instance-mean with CI.
3. CodeBLEU (tertiary only): the 'codebleu' PyPI implementation (Ren et al. 2020) with its Python tokenizer, corpus-level; fallback sacrebleu corpus BLEU with character tokenization and exponential smoothing if codebleu is unavailable on the execution stack. Reported with the standing caveat that corpus BLEU on ≤2-line completions is high-variance and n-gram-saturated; it is never used for claims or tests.
4. Cost metrics (§8): wall-clock per instance (prefill vs decode split), generated tokens, peak memory, per-instance FLOP estimate, EM-per-10^15-FLOPs.

# 6. Pre-registered analysis plan (all thresholds, families, and seeds fixed before any evaluation)
- Confirmatory family F1 (Holm–Bonferroni across exactly these four tests, α=0.05): (1) EM A1 vs B1, (2) ES A1 vs B1, (3) EM A1 vs B2, (4) ES A1 vs B2. EM differences tested with McNemar's test using the exact binomial test on discordant pairs over the intersected instance set; ES differences tested with the paired bootstrap below (no ad-hoc t-tests).
- Bootstrap: nonparametric instance-level resampling, B=10,000, percentile 95% CIs, seed 20261023 (single seed, fixed).
- Missing-data rule: primary analyses on the intersection of evaluable instances; counts and reasons per model reported; sensitivity analysis marks all unavailable instances as EM=0, ES=0 ("failure-as-wrong"); conclusions must agree across both views or be reported as divergent.
- Stratifications (descriptive unless named below): prompt-length buckets on a model-agnostic proxy — prompt character count thresholds {<1,200; 1,200–4,000; >4,000} chars (≈300/1,000 tokens); plus per-model truncation-flag decomposition (truncated vs not) applied to A1, B1, B2 — this is the declared mechanism analysis separating "worse model" from "context-starved model" (e.g., B1-vs-B2 gap within the untruncated stratum estimates pure-budget effect at matched content; within truncated instances, compare like-for-like where both were truncated). Repository-size and prompt-length strata beyond the named three are labeled exploratory/unadjusted. To prevent stratum fishing: only the three char-length buckets × EM for A1-vs-B1 receive Holm-adjusted "secondary confirmatory" status; all other cuts carry the label "exploratory, unadjusted for multiplicity."
- GPT-2-large subsampling rule (declared in advance): proportional stratified random sample, n=400, from the three char-length buckets, seed 20261023; reported descriptively as a within-family scaling sensitivity only; not pooled with A1.

# 7. Controls / factors held constant
Identical: instance set and order, source prompt text, dedent post-processing, max_new_tokens=64, greedy decoding, bf16, single reference per instance, same eval script for both models, same hardware class per pass (logged), fixed seeds for all resampling/subsampling. Intentionally varied: model checkpoint and its native tokenizer; context budget (the point of the arms); prompt rendering for B3 only (which is why B3 is descriptive-only).

# 8. Compute/efficiency section (in-body, per Q3)
Reported per arm: wall-clock per instance split into prefill/decode, total generated tokens, peak memory, per-instance FLOP estimate ≈ 2·P·(prompt+gen tokens) (forward-pass approximation, formula declared), and EM per 10^15 FLOPs. Design-time tractability estimate for the FULL ≈1,712-instance Python cross_file_first set: GPT-2 (≤1,088 tok): ≈2.7×10^11 FLOPs/instance → ≈5×10^14 FLOPs total — minutes-to-an-hour class on CPU/GPU. CodeLlama-7B at mean context ~3k (cap 8,192): ≈4×10^13 FLOPs/instance → ≈10^17 FLOPs total; on an A100-40/80GB (bf16, effective 50–150 TFLOP/s) roughly 1–8 h per full-set pass including decode-bound overhead (110k generated tokens/instance-set); CPU-only would be days — infeasible in practice. B2 (1,024-token cap) costs ~3–8× less per prefill than B1; B3 adds roughly one more full CodeLlama pass; A2 (n=400, 774M) is negligible. Full iso-FLOP / compute-matched curves are OUT of scope by ruling and appear in limitations.

# 9. Feasibility (per Q6)
(a) This container cannot execute the design: Python 3.14.4 with no torch/transformers wheels available, no ML stack at all (numpy absent), RepoBench data and both checkpoints absent, network disabled (DNS failures verified), CPU-only (no /dev/nvidia*). (b) Minimum execution environment: Python 3.10–3.12; torch ≥2.1 + transformers + the official RepoBench eval utilities; network or pre-staged artifacts (RepoBench-P v1.1 Python cross_file_first files; gpt2, gpt2-large, CodeLlama-7b-hf, CodeLlama-7b-Instruct); one GPU with ≥24 GB VRAM (7B bf16 ≈ 13.5 GB weights + KV cache ≈ 4 GB at 8,192 tokens ≈ 18 GB total; 40 GB comfortable). (c) Honest cost: §8 — full-set CodeLlama pass ≈ 1–8 GPU-hours, GPT-2 passes negligible; total all-arms run is single-digit GPU-days worst case, i.e., tractable for a real study but not in this container. No pilot is planned, claimed, or projected.

# 10. Limitations and threats to validity
1. Context asymmetry: native arm rewards CodeLlama's 32k window by design; the shared-budget arm bounds but does not eliminate the confound (tokenizer efficiency still differs at 1,024 tokens — GPT-2 BPE vs Llama SentencePiece pack the same prompt into different token counts, so "1,024 tokens" is not "1,024 tokens of content").
2. Tokenizer/vocabulary effects: EM operates on decoded strings, but indentation is whitespace-critical in Python; BPE 'Ġ'-merge vs SentencePiece whitespace handling and the dedent-stop rule can truncate the noisier 124M model's generations earlier than CodeLlama's — a scoring-path asymmetry mitigated only by the shared post-processing rule.
3. Not scale-matched: base-vs-base compares 124M general vs 7B code-specialized; the study cannot attribute the gap to code specialization vs scale (A2 offers only a weak within-GPT-2 direction check).
4. Single dataset/language: RepoBench-P Python only; generalization to other RepoBench languages, other units (cross_file_concat, intra_file), or other benchmarks is not covered.
5. Greedy decoding at 64 tokens is a known degeneration regime for a 124M model (repetition loops); EM/edit-similarity under greedy may understate GPT-2's sampling-quality capability. Held fixed for symmetry; flagged, not corrected.
6. Pretraining-contamination asymmetry: CodeLlama's GitHub-heavy pretraining may include RepoBench's repos, inflating verbatim recall; diagnostic (not corrective): report the rate of completions that match the reference verbatim beyond what prefix continuation predicts. Full mitigation impossible without held-out repo splits.
7. Prompt-quality noise: official prompts can contain near-leaks of the reference (dependency file containing the target line); spot-checked and reported as an overlap rate, since using prompts unmodified is a requirement.
8. The 8,192 cap on B1/B3 truncates a logged minority of prompts; if >20% capped, a 32k sensitivity is promised in advance.
9. 'full'-vs-'clean' choice: replication addresses it, but the primary is pre-committed either way.

# 11. Rationale — what each choice excludes
Official pre-built prompts → excludes retrieval-pipeline confounds. Native-window primary → excludes an artificial handicap on the 32k model for the deployed-capability claim; shared-1024 first-class arm → excludes "model vs context" conflation, the only design that does. Base-only primary → excludes prompt-format confounds (Instruct quarantined, never pooled). Greedy + fixed 64 tokens + shared dedent cut → excludes decoding/search asymmetry as an explanation. Paired McNemar + fixed-seed bootstrap + pre-declared Holm family → excludes analytic flexibility/fishing. Failure-as-wrong sensitivity + reported counts → excludes survivorship bias from silent drops. Full-test-set primary with one pre-declared subsample rule (A2) → excludes convenient subsampling. Required in-body cost table without iso-FLOP matching → answers "how does performance compare" without silently converting to a compute-efficiency study.

This is accepted as the final deliverable; no revision requested. The design answers both claims I scoped: the native-context arm (A1 vs B1) answers the deployed-capability question as asked, and the shared-1024 arm (B2) plus the truncation-flag decomposition is the mechanism analysis that separates "worse model" from "context-starved model". All six rulings are traceably implemented, and I checked them against the text rather than the summary.

Specifically satisfied:
- Rationale is choice-by-choice and written as exclusion of alternatives (§11), which is what I asked for rather than generic justification.
- Controls are explicit (§7), with the intentional-variations list making the confound structure legable: tokenizer, context budget, and B3's prompt rendering are the only free factors, and B3 is correctly quarantined from all paired confirmatory tests.
- The analysis plan (§6) is genuinely pre-registered: a closed Holm family of four, exact-binomial McNemar on paired EM, fixed-seed/fixed-B bootstrap, a declared missing-data rule with a failure-as-wrong sensitivity requiring convergence or an explicit divergence report, and a bounded strata policy that labels everything outside the three char-length buckets as exploratory and unadjusted. That is the anti-fishing control I required.
- Metric definitions (§5) are re-implementable, and CodeBLEU is correctly demoted to tertiary and excluded from claims/tests.
- Cost is an in-body section (§8) with a declared FLOP approximation formula and EM-per-unit-cost, and iso-FLOP matching is placed in limitations rather than silently becoming the study — the right call for this question.

- Threats to validity (§10) go beyond a token list. I particularly endorse items 2, 6 and 7: tokenizer-dependent interaction with the dedent-stop rule is a real scoring-path asymmetry for indentation-sensitive Python, and treating pretraining contamination and prompt near-leakage as reported diagnostics rather than pretending to correct them is the intellectually honest framing given that prompts must be used unmodified.

Two accepted-with-note items, neither requiring rework in a design-only deliverable: (i) the EM strip semantics and the ~1.7k instance count are pinned-at-staging steps from a dataset that is absent here — the design already commits to recording both in a run manifest before any comparison, which is the right handling rather than asserting them as verified; (ii) the 8,192-token cap on B1/B3 is a cost-motivated choice, and the pre-committed >20%-capped trigger for a 32k sensitivity is sufficient governance.

Scope boundaries are stated, not hidden: retrieval fixed by official prompts, single dataset and language, no scale-matched comparison, no compute-matched curves, no execution. payload.answer:
Proposed approach (design-only; nothing executed or claimed as run).

REPOSITORY OBSERVATIONS FIRST. /workspace contains only task.json (the question, context, and the one-line track.md: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"). There is no FuseLLM code, no Llama-2 weights, no datasets, no copy of the ICLR 2024 paper #18013 sections (setup_2/setup_9 are referenced as topics but their text is not present in the workspace). Environment checks: python 3.14.4 without torch/transformers, no GPU (nvidia-smi fails), network disabled, ~2 TB RAM / 224 CPU cores. So any real evaluation would run outside this sandbox; this deliverable is a protocol design only.

(1) EVALUATION PROTOCOL — FuseLLM vs Llama-2, Commonsense (CS), zero-shot.
Paired within-model-harness comparison: run both checkpoints through one fixed evaluation harness, one fixed per-dataset prompt template, deterministic likelihood-based scoring of multiple-choice letters, few_shot=0. Primary comparison: identical parameter scale and lineage control — e.g., FuseLLM-13B (merged model) vs Llama-2-13B, plus (if applicable to the paper's fusion recipe) the component models as intermediate controls, so any gain is attributable to fusion rather than size or instruction tuning. Primary endpoint: mean accuracy across the CS suite; secondary: per-task accuracies. Statistical comparison over per-example predictions (paired), not just point accuracy.

(2) BENCHMARKS, METRICS, SETTINGS, CONTROLS (proposed standard configuration).
- Benchmarks (standard CS suite as used by Alpaca/OpenLLaMA-style evaluations): PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OBQA (validation splits, test labels withheld by harness). 
- Metric: zero-shot exact-match accuracy per task; normalization: raw token log-likelihood of each answer continuation (report a length-normalized variant as a control because model/tokenizer pairs differ in length bias only if tokenizers differ — here both are Llama-tokenizer, reducing that risk). Mean over 7 tasks as headline.
- Prompting: one template per dataset shared verbatim between models, few_shot=0; explicit chat/instruct-wrapping decision must match the model variant compared (see uncertainties).
- Decoding: none needed for likelihood scoring (deterministic argmax over {A,B,C,D}); therefore seeds are not a variance source. If a generate-based scoring variant is used as control, use greedy decoding plus 3 seeds with temperature sampling as a robustness check only.

FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment was run or claimed)

TITLE: Zero-shot Commonsense (CS) evaluation of FuseLLM vs same-size Llama-2.

1. OBJECTIVE AND HYPOTHESIS
- Question (source, setup_2): "Evaluate whether FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 in zero-shot scenarios on the Common Sense (CS) benchmark." The only other fixed requirement is the model name "FuseLLM" (setup_9). Everything else below is an explicitly labeled assumption.
- H1: FuseLLM's mean zero-shot accuracy over the CS suite exceeds that of the comparator Llama-2 checkpoint. H0: no difference. Direction and success criterion defined in §6.

2. SYSTEMS UNDER TEST (assumption-labeled)
- Target: FuseLLM merged checkpoint (ASSUMPTION: model-merging fusion over Llama-2-lineage models; exact size/merge recipe not source-supported).
- Comparator: Llama-2 checkpoint of identical parameter scale, same tokenizer family (ASSUMPTION: base-vs-chat pairing must match FuseLLM's training regime; unresolved — see Uncertainties U1).
- Optional intermediate control: the component models used in the merge, to attribute any gain to fusion itself.
- Integrity: record weight repo IDs, revisions/commit hashes, and file SHA256 for every checkpoint before any run.

3. BENCHMARKS AND DATA (assumption-labeled; U2)
CS suite (ASSUMPTION — standard Alpaca/OpenLLaMA-style commonsense set; not confirmed by supplied sources): PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OBQA. Splits: validation sets scored (test labels publicly withheld). Pin each dataset's exact name+version in the harness config (e.g., lm-eval task IDs and commit). Record per-task N and chance level (1/#options) in the report header.

4. EVALUATION PROTOCOL
- Harness: one single harness for both models (lm-evaluation-harness preferred, or the paper's own scripts if the researcher later supplies them) so scoring code is a constant.
- Setting: few_shot=0 (zero-shot), one shared prompt template per dataset applied verbatim to both models (ASSUMPTION: Alpaca-style templates; template text printed verbatim in the appendix). If the comparator is a chat variant, the same chat-wrapping policy applies to both models (paired-design invariant).
- Scoring: for each example, compute raw summed token log-likelihood of each answer continuation conditioned on the shared prompt; predict = argmax over options; accuracy = exact match. Deterministic — no sampling, hence no seed variance; report determinism check (rerun 1% random subsample, expect bit-identical likelihoods up to float tolerance).
- Truncation/padding: identical max-length policy for both models; log count of truncated examples per task (must be equal-by-construction and near zero).
- Permutation control: repeat scoring with a fixed pseudorandom permutation of option order per example; final per-example prediction = permutation-averaged (report both raw-order and permuted accuracies to expose positional bias).

5. CONTROLS AND WHY EACH IS NECESSARY
- Same harness/template/scoring function: isolates model weights as the only differing factor — the entire fairness claim of the comparison rests on this.
- Same parameter scale + same tokenizer family: prevents size or tokenization artifacts explaining the gap.
- Answer-order permutation: Llama-tokenizer letter-prior and position bias differ across checkpoints; uncontrolled, this can flip small gaps.
- Version pinning (weights, code, datasets): makes the result auditable and reproducible; guards against silent model/data drift.
- Chance baseline + random-prediction negative control: harness sanity; catches template/scoring bugs before conclusions.
- Length/bias diagnostics: report mean continuation log-length and per-letter prediction distribution; raw vs length-normalized likelihood gap as secondary check.
- Leakage check: verify no eval examples appear in FuseLLM merge/instruction sources (dedup by exact match + near-dup MinHash on val sets) — merged models inherit their components' training data, so this is the main confound specific to FuseLLM.

6. ANALYSIS PLAN AND SUCCESS CRITERION
- Primary metric: per-task zero-shot accuracy (7 numbers per model) and unweighted mean across the 7 tasks = headline "CS score".
- Paired statistics: because both models score the identical example set, build the per-example correctness matrix and (a) McNemar test per task; (b) stratified bootstrap (10,000 resamples, resampled within task) 95% CI for the mean-accuracy gap.
- Success criterion: claim "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on zero-shot CS" ONLY IF mean gap > 0 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0, AND per-task table reported in full (no task-level cherry-picking), AND permutation-averaged results agree in sign with raw-order results. Otherwise report "no demonstrated outperformance" with effect sizes.
- Secondary robustness (not part of the claim): generate-and-match scoring variant with greedy decoding, plus 3-seed temperature-sampled variant as a sensitivity check only.

7. REPORT DELIVERABLES
Per-task accuracy table (FuseLLM, Llama-2, delta, chance level), CS mean ± bootstrap CI, McNemar p-values, permutation sensitivity table, bias diagnostics, leakage-check report, full config dump (templates, versions, hashes, harness commit).

8. FEASIBILITY / EXECUTION PREREQUISITES (not satisfied in this sandbox)
- This workspace: CPU-only, network disabled, no torch/transformers, no datasets, no weights → execution impossible here by construction; task.json itself states design-only, "repositories and compute are not required."
- External requirements: ≥1× A100-80GB (13B-class, fp16 likelihood scoring), gated Llama-2 access (researcher-license), FuseLLM checkpoint availability, public dataset downloads, lm-eval or equivalent. Rough cost: full 7-task zero-shot suite ≈ 1–2 GPU-hours per model; permutation control doubles it — modest, so the real risks are access (weights/data) and the assumption gaps below, not compute.

ASSUMPTIONS (not confirmed by supplied sources; every item except the two setup quotes is an assumption):
A1 CS = 7-task suite {PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-E, ARC-C, OBQA}, validation splits.
A2 Metric = zero-shot likelihood argmax accuracy; shared Alpaca-style prompt templates; few_shot=0.
A3 FuseLLM = merging-fusion checkpoint; fair comparator = same-size Llama-2, tokenizer-compatible.
A4 Deterministic scoring makes seeds irrelevant to the primary endpoint.
A5 Only source-fixed text: setup_2 sentence (objective) and setup_9 ("- FuseLLM"); no benchmark list, metric, size, base/chat, or merge recipe exists in provided sources.

UNCERTAINTIES TO RESOLVE (researcher-side, before any real run):
U1 Comparator variant: Llama-2 base vs chat must mirror FuseLLM's tuning regime — the single biggest fairness risk.
U2 Exact CS task list/split in paper #18013 (may include/exclude tasks; setup_2/setup_9 full text unavailable here).
U3 FuseLLM checkpoint availability, size, and component list (needed for leakage check and component control).
U4 Paper's original scoring implementation (generate-and-match vs loglikelihood; length normalization) — affects absolute numbers but not the paired design's validity.

RATIONALE FOR CONTROLS: each control neutralizes a specific confound — shared harness/templates (implementation asymmetry), same size/tokenizer (capacity and tokenization confounds), option permutation (positional/letter-prior bias known to inflate or deflate multiple-choice accuracy by several points), version pinning (reproducibility), chance/random baselines (harness-bug detection), leakage check (merge-inherited training data is the dominant confound unique to FuseLLM). Метрика:
- accuracy по задачам; итог по CS = тот же агрегат, что в источнике (пока неизвестно: макросреднее по списку задач или accuracy одной CSQA). Один и тот же сплит (val vs test) для обеих моделей.
Контроли честности:
- одинаковые промпт-шаблоны, один и тот же harness и его версия/конфиг; одинаковый лимит токенов и политика усечения; одинаковая точность (fp16) и устройство; greedy/temperature=0 либо чистый loglikelihood (без сэмплирования); одинаковая версия токенизатора (обе модели — Llama-2 tokenizer; отдельным чек-фактом проверить, что у fused-модели vocab/tokenizer идентичен Llama-2, т.к. FuseLLM трогает embedding-слой); проверка, что ни один пример из train не попадает в промпты; идентичный порядок/ID примеров для paired-тестов.
Вариативность и выборка (для дизайна без исполнения):
- greedy/likelihood эвал детерминирован по сути; единственный источник шума — численная недетерминированность → прогон 1 раз, но зафиксировать seed везде.
- Размер: полный dev/test-CS набор(ы) (для CSQA — 1221 dev-примеров), без подсемплирования; для утверждения «outperform» — paired-тест McNemar (пер-item совпадения правильностей FuseLLM vs Llama-2) + bootstrap 95% CI на разницу accuracy; порог значимости зафиксировать заранее.
- Power-оценку (какая минимальнаяDetectable разница видна на N примеров) включить в дизайн аналитически.

== 4. Допущения / открытые вопросы / что не проверяемо ==
Допущения (если ты не переопределишь):
- FuseLLM checkpoint = 7B fused (Llama-2-7B student + 13B teacher), base-версия, Llama-2 tokenizer;
- «outperform» = выше средний CS-accuracy, а не по каждой задачке;
- сравнение «FuseLLM vs Llama-2-7B», а не vs чат-версии;
- дизайн-only: исполнение не планируется, веса/данные будут доступныresearcher'у вне этой среды.
Открытые вопросы (нужен clarification, бюджет 6):
1) Точный состав CS-сплита и setting (zero vs few-shot) по setup_2/setup_9: одна CommonSenseQA или агрегат (какие задачи, какой сплит, какая метрика-колонка)?
2) Какой именно чекпойнт FuseLLM публикуется (repo/имя), base или instruction; какие размеры; какой eval-harness в их репо?
3) Формат промптов: их собственный скрипт или Llama-2 eval / lm-eval-harness? Как парсится ответ?
4) Будут ли веса/датасеты предоставлены локально (Llama-2 — gated), или остаёмся строго design-only?
5) Критерий успеха: средний балл CS или по-задачно; нужен ли 13B-референс?
6) Бюджет вычислений, если исполнение всё-таки планируется (CPU-only inference для 7B/13B здесь практически непригоден).
Не проверяемо в этой среде: текст FuseLLM-статьи/репо и определение CS; наличие/имена HF-чекпойнтов; поведение harness; любые численные результаты (их нет и не будет — исполнение не производилось).

Q1 (состав CS): фиксированная часть источника говорит только "zero-shot scenarios on the Common Sense (CS) benchmark" и не раскрывает список задач. Поэтому не выдумывай список как факт. Q2 (чекпойнт): принимается как допущение — FuseLLM fused 7B (student=Llama-2-7B, teacher=Llama-2-13B), base-версия, Llama-2-токенизатор. Оформить как assumption, не как факт, + проверка целостности: vocab/токенизатор идентичны Llama-2, т.к. fusion трогает embedding-слой.

Q3 (harness/промпты): фиксируем одинаковый для обеих сторон публичный harness (lm-eval-harness-стиль), likelihood-скрининг вариантов ответа, greedy, temperature=0, один шаблон промпта на задачу, одна версия harness на обе модели. Это наше методологическое решение, не утверждение про авторов FuseLLM — так и подпиши.

Q4 (веса/данные): строго design-only. Никакого исполнения, веса gated, сети нет. В разделе feasibility явно посчитай порядок стоимости внешнего прогона (7B+13B likelihood-эвал на CS-наборах, ориентировочно GPU-часы) как условие реализуемости, без假-запусков.

Q5 (критерий успеха): «outperform» = выше средний (macro) accuracy по CS + статистическая значимость. Определи a priori: primary — разница macro-accuracy и McNemar's test на paired per-item correctness с alpha=0.05, плюс bootstrap 95% CI на разницу; secondary — по-задачные сравнения с поправкой на множественность. Референс Llama-2-13B — optional upper bound, не primary.

Q6 (бюджет): не задан; впиши правдоподобный бюджет как часть feasibility-оценки, а не как ограничение от заказчика.

payload.answer:
ФИНАЛЬНЫЙ ЭКСПЕРИМЕНТАЛЬНЫЙ ДИЗАЙН (design-only; ни один эксперимент не выполнялся, направление эффекта не заявляется).
Вопрос: превзойдёт ли FuseLLM Llama-2 на commonsense-бенчмарке "Common Sense (CS)" в zero-shot?

=== 1. Гипотеза и операционализация «outperform» ===
H1 (primary): macro-average zero-shot accuracy модели FuseLLM (fused 7B; АССЕПШН A1) выше, чем у базовой Llama-2-7B, на CS-наборе, и разница статистически значима.
H0: разницы нет. Операционализация «outperform» (фиксировано а priori, per clarification Q5):
- Primary: Δ = macro-accuracy(FuseLLM) − macro-accuracy(Llama-2-7B) по всем задачам CS-сплита; значимость — McNemar exact/chi2 test на paired per-item correctness (объединённый по задачам, stratum = задача), α=0.05 two-sided; плюс bootstrap 95% CI (10k ресемплов по items внутри задач, one-seed-зафиксированный RNG) на Δ.
- Вердикт «outperform» только если Δ>0 И McNemar p<0.05 И нижняя граница CI > 0. Иначе — «not demonstrated» (не «равенство»).
- Secondary: по-задачные Δaccuracy с поправкой Holm-Bonferroni по числу задач; вывод secondary не меняет primary.
- Llama-2-13B — optional upper-bound референс, вне primary-критерия.

=== 2. Условия сравнения: варьируется vs фиксируется ===
Варьируется (единственный фактор — веса модели):
 (a) FuseLLM fused 7B; (b) Llama-2-7B base (главная контрольная); (c) опционально Llama-2-13B base.
Фиксируется идентичным для всех условий: набор задач и сплиты (val/dev, никогда hidden test); промпт-шаблон на задачу; число few-shot = 0; метод скоринга; ограничение длины и политика усечения; dtype=fp16; устройство/библиотеки/версии; порядок и ID примеров; парсер; RNG seed (заранее, для bootstrap). Никаких model-specific промптов, никакого early-stop по результатам, никаких подсетей, выбранных после взгляда на данные.

=== 3. Протокол zero-shot и скрининг ответов ===
Методологическое решение стороны дизайнера (НЕ утверждение о протоколе авторов FuseLLM): публичный lm-eval-harness-стиль, один общий конфиг на все модели.
- Шаблон: «[задача-specific instruction] {context/question}\n(A)..(E)\nAnswer:» — один шаблон на задачу, 0 демо-примеров.
- Скоринг: likelihood, не генерация. Для каждого варианта scoring logP(вариант | промпт) последним-токен суммированием log-likelihood токенов продолжения; нормировка по длине варианта (acc-norm style, выбор нормировки фиксируется до прогонов и одинаков); выбор argmax. Буквенные метки («A») как продолжения НЕ используются — только полный текст варианта (защита от length/letter bias), при этом длина варианта учтена нормировкой.
- Декодинга нет (greedy не нужен; temperature=0 тривиально выполняется). Все pass@k/сэмплирование исключены.
-sanity-парсер дляoptional генеративной версии (если исследователь потребует): regex первой литеры варианта; в основной протокол не входит.

=== 4. Controls (полный список) ===
C1. Идентичный harness, версия и конфиг конфига на обе модели (один git-commit harness, лог версии).
C2. Идентичный промпт-шаблон и 0-shot для всех моделей.
C3. Идентичная политика усечения и max_seq_len (4096; при переполнении — усечение left с логом числа усечённых примеров на модель; доля усечений не должна различаться между моделями).
C4. Идентичный токенизатор: чек-факт — vocab, special tokens, tokenizer config FuseLLM == Llama-2-7B byte-идентичны (критично, т.к. fusion трогает embedding-слой; рассинхрон vocab = валидностная ошибка, остановка).
C5. Одна dtype (fp16), одно устройство-класс, один batch-режим; batch не влияет на likelihood (проверка на подвыборке 100 примеров: batch=1 vs batch=8 → идентичные скоры с точностью 1e-4).
C6. Leak-check train-vs-prompt: пересечение входных строк eval-примеров с train-сплитами этих же задач (exact + near-dup hashing) — пусто; 0-shot ⇒ учебных примеров в промпте нет по построению.
C7. Идентичность ID-порядка: обе модели получают один и тот же manifest (task_id, item_id) в одном порядке; paired-тест сопоставляется по item_id, не по позиции.
C8. Контроль реализации: прогон «шам-модели» (Llama-2-7B дважды, два независимых рана) — расхождение только от числовой недетерминированности (см. §5), ожидаемо ~0; если больше — проблема harness.
C9. Фиксация артефактов до анализа: конфиги, манифесты, хэши весов и датасетов (SHA256) логируются до первого прогона.

=== 5. Анализ: primary/secondary, power/MDE, недетерминированность ===
- Primary/secondary как в §1 (McNemar на paired correctness по объединённым задачам + bootstrap CI на macro-Δ; Holm для по-задачных).
- MDE (аналитический расчёт, формула McNemar Δ=(z_{.975}+z_{.8})·√(p_disc/N); рассчитано в этой среде арифметически, без эксперимента):
  • CSQA-only, N=1221: при доле дискордантных 5%/10%/20% → MDE ≈ 1.8 / 2.5 / 3.6 п.п. (α=0.05, power 0.8).
  • Агрегат из ~8 задач (N≈15–20k, размеры сплитов проверить на исполнители, они ориентировочно: PIQA≈1838, WG≈1267, HellaSwag≈10042, ARC-e≈2288, ARC-c≈1172, SIQA≈1954, OBQA≈500): MDE ≈ 0.5–1.0 п.п. при той же дискордантности.
  Вывод дизайна: агрегат даёт приемлемую мощность на пороге ~1 п.п.; одиночная CSQA способна детектировать только эффекты ≳2–3 п.п. Это следует зафиксировать в протоколе интерпретации: «no significant difference» на CSQA-only ≠ равенство моделей.
- Числовая недетерминированность: greedy/likelihood детерминирован по построению, шум только от nondeterministic GPU kernels/batch shape. Обработка: фиксация seed везде; допуск |Δscore| ≤ 1e-4 по C5/C8; если accuracy-флипы между ранами > 0.2% items — удвоить раны и использовать мажоритарный/средний скор с протокольной пометкой.

=== 6. Feasibility (внешний прогон; в этой среде исполнение исключено) ===
Подтверждённые ограничения этой среды: сеть отключена (DNS-fail), GPU нет (нет /dev/nvidia*, драйвера нет; в metadata gpu_enabled:false), весов/датасетов нет, torch/transformers не установлены — факт, а не предположение.
Для внешнего прогона потребуются: (i) HF-доступ к gated Llama-2-7B/13B (соглашение Meta) — основной риск; (ii) чекпойнт FuseLLM 7B (публичность/имя — проверить по репо авторов); (iii) датасеты CS-задач (публичные, не gated); (iv) 1×A100-80GB (fp16 13B ≈ 26 ГБ весов — влезает), CUDA, transformers+lm-eval.
Оценка стоимости (аналитическая, ~2·P·tokens при 50 TFLOP/s eff; допущения: ~4 pass/пример × ~150 токенов):
 • CSQA-only: <0.1 GPU·ч на модель. Весь CS-агрегат (~20k примеров): ≈1.5 GPU·ч (7B), ≈2.6–3 GPU·ч (13B) чистого forward; с загрузками/отладкой/дублями реалистичный бюджет — 10–25 A100·часов на все условия. Правдоподобию бюджет (не требование заказчика, per Q6).
Риски: gated-веса (блокер доступа); нерепroducible промпты авторов FuseLLM (митигируется тем, что протокол — наше симметричное методологическое решение, а не репродукция их цифр); недетерминизм kernels (митигация C5/C8); embedding-surgery может дать non-Llama-2 vocab (митигация C4 — проверка до прогонов); расхождение с цифрами статьи не является фейлом дизайна (иное определение CS/prompts допустимо — см. §7).

=== 7. Assumptions vs Confirmed facts; чего дизайн НЕ доказывает ===
CONFIRMED (проверено в среде): /workspace содержит только task.json; сети нет (DNS failure); GPU нет; весов/датасетов/ML-библиотек нет; python 3.14.4, 224 CPU, 2 ТБ RAM; MDE-числа — арифметический расчёт.
ASSUMPTIONS (помечено, требует внешней сверки): A1 FuseLLM checkpoint = fused 7B (student 7B/teacher 13B), base, Llama-2-vocab — из непроверенной памяти о статье, НЕ подтверждено источником в этой среде.
