# DIR-REL: Directional Asymmetry in LLM Retrieval of Celebrity Parent–Child Relations **Labeling convention used throughout:** `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` = fixed by me now and frozen; `[TARGET]` = allocation we aim for; `[PROJECTED]` = extrapolated from base rates, to be replaced by a Stage-0 census; `[ASSUMED]` = input to power analysis, not measured; `[TBE]` = to-be-estimated at analysis. **No number below is an observed result; no experiment has been run.** --- ## 0. Claim under test and estimand Hypothesis (H1): cued with a child's name, LLMs retrieve the parent accurately; cued with a parent's name, they underperform at retrieving the child. Competing explanations pre-registered as falsifiable alternatives: - **H2 Target-notability** — the effect is the notability of the *answer* entity (parent usually more famous than child), not relation direction. - **H3 Cardinality/ranking** — "the child" is one of several, so top-1 misses; knowledge exists but is not surfaced. - **H4 Corpus-mention asymmetry** — child articles state the parent in prose; parent articles carry children in a structured infobox field. The model faithfully reflects the text distribution. - **H5 Generic relation-inversion** — models invert any relation direction poorly; nothing special about family relations. **Primary estimand:** `β_dir`, the coefficient of `direction` (child→parent = reference; parent→child = focal) in a mixed logistic regression of answer correctness, with item- and family-level random intercepts and a by-family random slope for direction. Reported as an **odds ratio (OR)** on the **primary analysis set A** (defined §2.4). Direction is estimated **within-item** (each item is probed in both directions), so the contrast is paired by construction. --- ## 1. Execution preconditions (this environment cannot run it) Inspected and confirmed: `/workspace` holds only `task.json` (which itself states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"); no dataset, no harness, no baseline code; Python 3.14 stdlib-only (no torch/transformers/numpy/pandas/scipy/sklearn/openai/vllm); no `git`/`curl`/`wget`/`jq`; **network disabled** (live TCP connect to pypi.org:443 → `gaierror`); no GPU; 224 cores / ~2 TB RAM / ~1 TB tmpfs; `/workspace` is an NFS mount at 100% with **2.1 G free** — so all artifacts must be written to `/tmp` or another volume. Therefore the design specifies an execution host with: (i) outbound HTTPS to the Wikidata Query Service, Wikimedia REST (pageviews) and the Wikimedia dumps site; (ii) ~[TARGET] 300 GB scratch (enwiki `latest-pages-articles` XML ≈ [PROJECTED] 20–25 GB compressed, Wikidata full dump ≈ [PROJECTED] 60–90 GB compressed — or the SPARQL-service route for pool construction at the cost of query throttling); (iii) local NVMe for open weights ≈ [PROJECTED] 60–160 GB for the size ladders; (iv) an inference stack (vLLM or llama.cpp for GGUF) and API credentials with logprob support where offered; (v) one annotator pair for gold-set adjudication. Every quantity depending on execution is labeled above. --- ## 2. Stimuli ### 2.1 Snapshot (reproducibility anchor) `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` - **English Wikipedia dump `D` = first `latest-pages-articles` dump on or after 2025-11-01.** Used for all wikitext, infobox parsing, prose extraction, in-corpus name frequency, and as the end of the pageview window. - **Wikidata full JSON dump at the same date.** - **Second snapshot `D+180d`** used only to recompute mention-balance class and notability ranks; items whose balance class or reversal status flip are reported in a mandatory sensitivity table (assignment instability), not silently dropped. - Pageview window: 12 months ending at `D`, `access-user` excluded, mean daily views per article. ### 2.2 Pool and gold sets Candidate ordered pairs `(P, C)` where `P` has a non-deprecated Wikidata `P22` (father) or `P25` (mother) claim to `C`; **both** have English Wikipedia articles (no redirects/disambiguations) and enwiki sitelinks. Gold sets are **bidirectional and two-source**: `children(P)` = union of (a) Wikidata `P40` claims, (b) the enwiki parent-article infobox `children:` field; each member must be resolvable to a QID. A pair enters the bank only if documented by **≥2 independent sources** among {P22/P25 claim, P40 claim, parent infobox, child-article prose}. Every disagreement is human-adjudicated. Exclusions (core set): adoptions/step/foster indicated by claim qualifiers or by regex on either lead (`adopted|stepfather|stepmother|foster`); child deceased before 1900; children who are minors or who lack their own article (kept in a clearly separated supplementary arm, because there notability is unmeasurable and gold is unverifiable); families where either entity is primarily known *only* as "parent/child of X". Dynasty families capped at **1 item**; max **2 items per family** overall. `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` ### 2.3 Notability index and the **notability-reversed stratum** (load-bearing) **Index.** Three components, each log-transformed then **z-scored within (decade-of-peak-fame × occupation-domain) cells** so era and field base rates cannot masquerade as reversal: 1. `z_pv` = z of log10(1 + mean daily enwiki pageviews, 12-mo window to `D`); 2. `z_sl` = z of log2(1 + Wikidata sitelink count) — cross-lingual notability, robust to pageview bot noise; 3. `z_cm` = z of log10(1 + **number of distinct enwiki articles** containing the person's QID alias set, computed from the `D` dump) — the closest available proxy for training-exposure breadth. **Primary composite `N = mean(z_pv, z_sl, z_cm)`** `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`. Pre-registered sensitivity indices: pageviews-only, `z_cm`-only, and first principal component of the three. The **reassignment rate** between primary and sensitivity strata is reported (index-construction robustness). **Reversal threshold (conjunctive, so reversal is not an index artifact):** `ΔN = N(C) − N(P) ≥ 1.0` **AND** `pv(C)/pv(P) ≥ 5` **AND** `articles(C)/articles(P) ≥ 3`, plus a floor `pv(P) ≥ 500` mean daily views `[DESIGN-CONSTANT, threshold re-checked once at Stage 0 and then frozen]` so the parent remains learnable in principle and the reversed stratum is not "obscure parent" in disguise. **Anti-degeneracy: excluding children famous *because of* the parent.** A reversed candidate is admitted only if **all four** hold: - (a) **Independent-notability residual.** Pre-specified OLS on the whole pool, fitted on log-counts: `log10_pv(C) ~ log10_pv(P) + log10_pv(max_sibling) + log10_len(article_C) + log2(sitelinks_P) + age(article_C)`. Require `log10_pv(C) − fit ≥ 1.0` (≥10× its own predicted pageviews). A child whose fame is parent-derived is largely *predicted* by parent notability plus article structure; an independently notable child is not. - (b) **Co-mention ceiling.** Fraction of sentences in C's article mentioning P ≤ 0.40, measured with the §3 extractor. - (c) **Lead-independence.** P appears at most once in C's lead paragraph. - (d) **Own-achievement marker.** C carries ≥1 Wikidata claim from {`P166` award received, `P106` occupation with an own-work property, `P1344` participant of, `P1411` nomination} whose item does **not** reference P; **or** C's primary `P106` domain differs from P's primary `P106` domain (cross-domain pairs are the strongest evidence of independent fame). **Interpretive force.** In reversed families, H2 predicts parent→child becomes the *easy* direction (its target is now the more notable person) while child→parent targets an obscure parent. H1 predicts parent→child remains worse anyway. The stratum therefore dissociates direction from notability rather than merely adjusting for it, and both directions are informative within it. **Expected yield — explicitly `[PROJECTED]`, not measured.** Base-rate reasoning only: in a Wikidata-derived pool of parent–child pairs where both have enwiki articles, the overwhelming majority should have `N(P) > N(C)`; reversals at `ΔN ≥ 1` should exist in the thousands before filters (film, music, sport and political dynasties in which the second generation eclipsed the first are well attested), but the four independence filters plus the `pv(P) ≥ 500` floor will remove most of them. I project **0.3–1.5% of candidate pairs survive all filters**, i.e. **[PROJECTED] 100–600 usable families** from a pool of order 10⁵ pairs. **The Stage-0 census measures this; it is not a claim.** **Pre-declared contingency `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** if the reversed stratum yields **< 80 items from ≥ 40 distinct families**, the H2-dissociation test is **forfeited as confirmatory** and downgraded to a labeled qualitative sensitivity analysis; the headline claim is then capped at "**direction effect not dissociable from target notability**", which is a *negative* verdict on H1, not an inconclusive one. Power consequence: the stratum will only ever be powered for large effects (see §7). ### 2.4 Analysis sets `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` - **Set A (primary): only-child families.** Exactly one publicly documented child (two-source agreement), relation publicity onset ≥ 5 years before the model's cutoff, both entities with own articles, both adults. Parent→child then has a **uniquely determined answer**, which structurally removes the ambiguity objection. `[TARGET] 240 families.` - **Set B (secondary): multi-child families**, stratified by cardinality 2 / 3 / 4+, scored any-of-gold-set. `[TARGET] 240 families.` - **Set R (reversed notability)**, drawn from A and B, `[TARGET] 120 families`, floor 80 (§2.3). - **Set C (controls)**: capital-of (1:1), spouse-of (variable cardinality, no family-notability skew), fabricated-name templates (§4.4). ### 2.5 Recency / contamination strata Publicity onset `t_rel` = **latest** of {entity-creation dates of P and C} and **earliest** revision timestamp in either article whose text matches the §3 relation patterns; take `max(min_textual_evidence, entity_creation_C)`. Strata relative to **each model's own cutoff**: >15 y, 5–15 y, 2–5 y, <2 y, and a **post-cutoff negative-control set** (`t_rel` after cutoff). Both directions should fail there; success flags a wrong cutoff or a leaked item, and triggers item quarantine plus rerun on the remaining set (reported, not hidden). Cutoffs for closed models are self-reported → treated as ±6 months uncertainty, handled by reporting the direction effect as a function of `t_rel − cutoff` with that band shaded. --- ## 3. Mention-symmetry control, pinned to a reproducible extractor `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` — everything below is fixed code, run once against dump `D`, published with the item bank. 1. **Wikitext retrieval.** From the `D` dump, take each article's current revision text. Parse templates with `mwparserfromhell`. 2. **Structured route.** In the parent article, locate the top-level `Infobox person` (or `{{Infobox officeholder}}`, `{{Infobox athlete}}`, `{{Infobox musical artist}}`); read field `| children =`. Normalise, split on `{{plainlist}}`/`{{unbulleted list}}`/`
`/`*`/`,`/`;`, strip parentheticals and templates, then resolve each string to a QID by alias match **restricted to the union of `P40`/`P22`/`P25` candidates for P** (this prevents resolving "Jennifer" to the wrong notables). Flags: `infobox_parent_names_child ∈ {0,1,missing}`. Symmetrically read the child article's `| parents =` field → `infobox_child_names_parent`. 3. **Prose route, applied identically in both directions** (critical: never compare infobox presence to prose presence — that comparison is itself asymmetric). Section scope, pre-specified ordered list: lead, then first level-2 section whose title matches `Early life|Personal life|Family|Background|Biography|Career`; if none, lead only. Sentence-split; match a frozen pattern set against the **target person's full Wikidata alias set** (all language aliases + article title + dab-stripped name), not a single string: - `\b(son|daughter|child|children|kid|kids|offspring)\b[^.]{0,80}\bof\b[^.]{0,80}` - `[^.]{0,60}\b('s|’s)\s+(son|daughter|child)` - `\bparents?\b[^.]{0,80}` and `[^.]{0,80}\bis the (father|mother|parent) of\b` Counts: `fwd` = sentences in **C's** article evidencing P; `bwd` = sentences in **P's** article evidencing C. 4. **Balance class.** `MENTION-BALANCED` iff `fwd ≥ 1` **and** `bwd ≥ 1` **and** `|log((fwd+1)/(bwd+1))| ≤ 0.5` (≈1.65× ratio ceiling), **and** (`infobox_parent_names_child ≠ 0`, so our gold set is not what's missing). A stricter class (`BALANCED+STRUCTURED`) additionally requires both articles to evidence the relation in prose *and* in a structured field. 5. **Conditioning vs. restriction — which carries primary weight.** **Restriction carries it.** The mention-balanced subset is a *survive-subset* in the decision rule (§6), because subsetting is the only way to break collinearity between direction and textual support structurally. Conditioning on `log(fwd+1)`, `log(bwd+1)`, and `infobox_parent_names_child` as covariates in the primary model is retained but labeled **secondary adjustment**, on the explicit ground that regression adjustment on a strongly collinear and mismeasured exposure cannot separate relation direction from textual support and inherits functional-form assumptions. **Pre-registered adjustment-instability flag:** if `β_dir` shifts by > 0.4 log-odds when the mention covariates enter, the estimate is declared **not robust to textual-support adjustment** and the headline wording must say so. 6. **Known tension, declared rather than papered over.** Set R's filters (b)/(c) suppress parent mentions in the child's article, while `MENTION-BALANCED` requires ≥1 such mention. The intersection is expected to be small; **for Set R only**, mention balance is handled by covariate adjustment alone, and this is recorded as a named limitation of the H2 test. --- ## 4. Probes (per item, per direction, per model) ### 4.1 Free generation — 5 templates/direction `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` Templates are matched within item on: relation specificity (target gender and uniqueness specified in **both** directions), length within ±3 tokens, no surname priming, no third-party context. - child→parent: "Who is the mother of {C}?" / "Who is the father of {C}?" / "{C}'s mother is" (continuation) / "Name the woman who gave birth to {C}." / "Which celebrity is the mother of {C}?" - parent→child (Set A, unique target): "Who is the child of {P}?" / "{P}'s child is" / "Name the only child of {P}." / "Which celebrity is the child of {P}?" / "Who was born to {P}?" - Set B: "Name one child of {P}." scored any-of-gold-set; the "only" variants are removed so the phrasing is not over-specified. - Decoding: greedy (temperature 0) for the primary score; one sample at T = 0.7 for a self-consistency metric. Max 32 tokens, no chain-of-thought, no in-context exemplars in the primary arm. ### 4.2 Cloze / logprob arm (open-weight models; closed endpoints flagged if logprobs unavailable) Gold + 4 distractors from a frozen pre-sampled set (same occupation domain, same era, **surname-matched decoy**, random notable). Report gold rank, top-1, top-3, top-10. This is the H3 discriminator. ### 4.3 Four-alternative forced choice — same option sets as 4.2, order counterbalanced. ### 4.4 Core controls (co-primary with the main contrast, not optional) - **Generic inversion (H5):** capital-of (1:1, no notability skew) and spouse-of (variable cardinality) probed in both directions on the same models. If `β_dir` for these is comparable to the family-relation `β_dir`, the headline claim must be rewritten as a **generic relation-inversion** finding, not a celebrity-family finding. This arm is in the core precisely because it can change the interpretation of the headline. - **In-context supply:** prepend 2 sentences containing the relation, re-ask. Isolates parametric access from expression ability. - **Fabricated-name templates (§4.1 wording, invented matched names):** measures any difficulty asymmetry intrinsic to the sentence frames, independent of entities. This is the direct answer to "asymmetry baked into the QA pair". - **Surname-shortcut probe:** same-surname items scored against a same-surname decoy; plus a **surname-mismatch survive-subset** where P and C surnames differ. - **Refusal classification:** "don't know" / privacy refusal / question-begging parsed into separate outcome categories, never merged into "wrong". ### 4.5 Answer adjudication Normalise → QID resolution against a candidate index (all family members in the bank + all pool entities) → any-of-gold-set. **Every** answer that resolves to a real person but not to the gold set is human-checked against two sources; confirmed real children are added to gold and the item **re-scored for all models**, with the count of such events reported as a **gold-completeness rate** (this is the honest handling of the ambiguity/multi-child objection: our gold set, not the model, gets audited). ### 4.6 Model panel `[TARGET]` ≥2 open-weight lineages from different labs, each with ≥3 sizes spanning ~1B → ~70B, giving within-family scale ladders; plus 4 closed API models from 2 vendors at 2 capability tiers (~10 models). Frozen at Stage 0 into a model-card table: exact checkpoint, stated knowledge cutoff, context length, tokenizer, decoding config, logprob availability. **Scale is treated as an exploratory interaction, not a predicted one.** --- ## 5. Metrics Primary: per-item per-direction correctness (any-of-gold). Secondary: gold rank / top-3 / top-10 coverage; distinct answers per item; **cross-directional closure consistency** (if the model says C is P's child, does it return P for "who is C's mother?" — a model-internal asymmetry measure immune to all prompt differences); paraphrase self-consistency; calibration (mean gold probability and verbal confidence per direction); outcome-category mix (correct / wrong-entity / wrong-relation / real-but-ungolded person / don't-know / refusal). --- ## 6. Pre-registration, operational **Prerequisite `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** the analysis script and this rule are written and hashed **before any model output is scored**, after the Stage-0 census fixes item counts. ### 6.1 Primary test Mixed logistic regression, `correct ~ direction + log_pv_target + log_cm_target + log(n_candidates) + log(fwd+1) + log(bwd+1) + infobox_parent_names_child + relation_age_bin + surname_match + (1|item) + (1|family) + (direction|family)`; Set A, all models with model as fixed effect. `OR_dir = exp(β_dir)`. **Minimum effect size `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`: MES: OR_dir ≤ 0.50`** (odds of a correct answer for parent→child at most half those for child→parent). Interpretive anchor in percentage points: at a child→parent baseline of 0.75, OR 0.50 ⇒ parent→child 0.60 (**15 pp**); at 0.85 ⇒ 0.74 (**11 pp**). Hence the pre-set pp floor is **≥12 pp** on Set A, and the **OR is the primary metric**; the pp figure is reporting only, since the mapping depends on the (unknown) baseline. **CI rule.** 95% CI by 2000-replicate **cluster bootstrap over families** (GLMM profile likelihood as a secondary CI). H1 **supported** iff **all** hold: 1. `OR_dir ≤ 0.50` and 95% CI upper bound `< 1.0`; 2. the §6.2 survive-subset rule passes; 3. the generic-inversion control does **not** show a `β_dir` of comparable magnitude (else reclassify as H5); 4. the §4.2 coverage check permits the stronger wording (below). **Wording constraint (pre-committed).** If top-1 differs by direction but **top-10 coverage does not** (CI for the coverage contrast inside [−0.9, +0.9] log-odds), the verdict must be worded as a **surfacing/ranking asymmetry**, not a knowledge/storage asymmetry. H1 as stated ("accurately retrieving… underperform") is a performance claim, so this constraint binds the headline, not just the discussion. **Positive-negative verdict (avoids "absence of evidence").** If the 95% CI for `OR_dir` lies inside **[0.80, 1.25]**, report "**no meaningful directional asymmetry**". If it excludes 1 but exceeds 0.50, report "**directional asymmetry present but below the pre-registered magnitude**". Anything else: "**inconclusive**". **Nonparametric backstop:** McNemar exact test on Set A within-item pairs, per model and pooled (stratified bootstrap CI), reported alongside the GLMM; a sign disagreement between the two is reported in the main table. **Multiplicity:** one confirmatory estimand, α = 0.05 unadjusted; all other contrasts form a secondary family under Benjamini–Hochberg q = 0.05. ### 6.2 Survive-subsets: what counts as a *test* Four subsets, each a *necessary* condition: **(i) only-child** (= Set A itself, the specificity-clean test), **(ii) notability-reversed** (Set R, H2-clean), **(iii) surname-mismatch** (shortcut-clean), **(iv) mention-balanced** (§3, textual-support-clean). **Usability floor `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** a subset counts as a *test* only if it retains **≥ 80 items from ≥ 40 distinct families** with ≥ 8 of the ~10 models returning parseable, non-error outputs on both directions. Below the floor it is **descriptive only**, and the specific conclusion forfeited is named in the report: e.g. "subset (ii) under-powered ⇒ H1 is not supported net of target notability", i.e. the *strong* claim is lost and the result is reported as "direction effect not dissociable from confound X" — a **negative** verdict, not a shrug. **Per-subset pass rule `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` (relaxed, because subsets are smaller):** `CONFIRM` iff point `OR ≤ 0.75` **and** 90% CI upper bound `< 1.0`; `NULL` iff 90% CI lies inside [0.90, 1.11] or above 1; `INCONCLUSIVE` otherwise or below floor. **Headline gate:** all four subsets must be `CONFIRM` or `INCONCLUSIVE`, **none `NULL`**, and **at most one** `INCONCLUSIVE`. If ≥2 are `INCONCLUSIVE` the study reports H1 as untested rather than supported or refuted. If **any** subset is `NULL`, or all surviving effects appear only outside the balanced/only-child/mismatched subsets, the verdict is "**H1 not supported as a relation-direction effect**" — the legitimate negative outcome you endorsed. ### 6.3 Mandatory reporting (no hiding behind pooled terms) 1. **Per-template gaps table:** `OR` and 95% CI for every one of the 5 templates × 2 directions × every model, plus pooled. 2. **Paraphrase dispersion:** SD and range of per-template `OR`, per direction per model, reported in the same table as the pooled estimate, plus a formal template × direction interaction test. 3. **Sign-flip disclosure:** any single template whose point `OR` sign differs from the pooled sign appears in the **main** results table with its n, not in an appendix. 4. Effect sizes + CIs for every contrast (no bare p-values); item-level accuracy distributions (not just means) per direction; outcome-category mixes. 5. Stratum-level counts of what fell out at each filter (CONSORT-style flow diagram for the item bank). --- ## 7. Power (assumption/simulation-based; no pilot exists here) Design-based simulation, no observed effect size attached. Generator: the §6.1 model; assumed inputs `[ASSUMED]` — child→parent baseline accuracy p ∈ {0.70, 0.85}; parent→child under H0 equal to it, under H1 set to give `OR` ∈ {0.5, 0.65, 0.8}; random-effect variances for item and family chosen to give ICC ∈ {0.1, 0.3}; ~10 models; 2 directions × 5 templates per item. Grid over items ∈ {100, 200, 240, 400, 480}. Output: smallest detectable `OR` at 80% power, α = 0.05, per cell. - At the Set A `[TARGET]` of 240 families the design is expected to detect `OR ≈ 0.5` with margin **and** `OR ≈ 0.65` only at the upper item counts — a projection to be replaced by the simulation's actual output. - **Set R is the power-limited arm:** at 80–120 items it will only detect large effects; declared up front, and the §2.3 floor rule decides whether it is a test at all. - **Pre-committed stopping rule:** if the simulation shows MDE(`OR`) > 0.50 at the achieved N, the confirmatory claim is **not licensed**; the study is then reported as descriptive with the MDE stated, rather than re-analyzed until it passes. - Arithmetic load projection `[TBE, computable]`: ≈ items × 2 directions × (5 free-gen + 1 T=0.7 + 1 AFC) × models generations, ≈ 5×10⁴–6×10⁴ calls, plus ≈ 10⁴ scoring calls. **Stage plan / go-no-go:** Stage 0 census (pool size, reversed yield, mention-balance yield, publicity-onset distribution) → fixes final N and confirms/forfeits subsets **before any model call**; Stage 1 item-bank freeze + hash + pre-registration deposit; Stage 2 open-weight runs; Stage 3 API runs; Stage 4 adjudication and gold re-scoring; Stage 5 frozen analysis script executed once. --- ## 8. Secondary / optional arms (explicitly non-co-primary) - **RAG upper bound** *(optional, 150-item random subsample of Set A, 2 models — 1 open, 1 closed)*: supply the two gold sentences and re-ask. Purpose: bound how much of any asymmetry is parametric access versus expression. No inferential role. - **Human baseline** *(optional, exploratory)*: 100-item subsample, both directions within-participant, order counterbalanced, ≥25 participants per condition {no search, search allowed}. Purpose: determine whether the asymmetry resembles human forward-association asymmetry (in which case the LLM-specific framing of the claim weakens) or departs from it. Excluded from the decision rule. **Feasibility note — CPU-only pilot.** The inspected host (224 cores, ~2 TB RAM, no GPU, but no network and no ML stack, and 2.1 G free in `/workspace`) could in principle run a pilot with quantised ≤3B GGUF models on CPU, writing to the 1 TB `/tmp` tmpfs — plausibly 30–60 items × 2 directions overnight — which would suffice only to validate the answer-parsing/adjudication pipeline and estimate refusal and parse-failure rates. It is not adequate for the confirmatory contrast, and nothing here can run without first installing dependencies and obtaining weights, so the pilot belongs to the networked execution host. ## 9. Limitations stated in the deliverable English-only, encyclopedic register; celebrity pairs are a biased sample of parent-child relations (asymmetric documentation, dynasty clusters — handled by `(1|family)` and per-family caps but not eliminated); publicity onset is a proxy and contamination cannot be removed, only stratified — for highly memorised pairs "known" and "stored" are empirically inseparable; closed-model cutoffs are self-reported; logprob availability varies by endpoint, so the ranking-vs-storage analysis is open-weight-heavy; the reversed stratum is intrinsically small; the mention-balanced and reversed strata partially conflict by construction (§3.6). ## 10. What would change the verdict (pre-committed, so interpretation is not post-hoc) - Effects confined to multi-child items → **H3**, wording must say ranking, not retrieval. - Effect vanishes in Set R or scales with `log_pv_target` → **H2**. - Effect vanishes in `MENTION-BALANCED` → **H4**: corpus-derived, not relational. - Comparable `β_dir` for capital-of/spouse-of → **H5**: generic inversion. - Fabricated-name control shows a same-direction gap → the asymmetry is partly **in the template**, and the headline must be reduced accordingly. - Post-cutoff control items answered correctly → quarantine items and re-report; a cutoff error invalidates the temporal strata.

**Environment observations (executed here; exploratory only, not results).** `ls -la /workspace` and `find /workspace -maxdepth 3 -type f` → single file `task.json`; `cat /workspace/task.json` confirms the question, "Do not claim that an experiment was run", and `documents.track.md: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."` — no track.md on disk. Dependency probe `pip list | grep -iE 'torch|transformers|numpy|pandas|scipy|scikit|openai|vllm|datasets|huggingface|litellm|anthropic|statsmodels'` → no matches (exit 1); `which jq curl wget git aria2c` → nothing found; Python 3.14.4 stdlib imports fine. Filesystem-wide search for `track.md`, `*.jsonl`, `*.parquet`, `*wikidata*`, `*celeb*` and HF/model caches → nothing outside system paths; no `~/.cache`, empty home. Network: `socket.create_connection(('pypi.org',443))` → `network: DOWN -> gaierror`. Compute: `nvidia-smi` → "couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver"; `nproc` = 224; `free -g` ≈ 2 TB RAM; `df -h` → `/tmp` tmpfs 1006 G free but the `/workspace` NFS mount 100% used with 2.1 G available (basis for the artifacts-to-/tmp precondition and the CPU-pilot caveat). These facts justify: design-only delivery, networked execution host, dumps/API preconditions, open-weight logprob coverage limits, pilot paragraph.

**How the four judgement points are satisfied.** (1) Pre-registration operational: primary estimand `OR_dir` from a GLMM with (1|item)+(1|family)+(direction|family); MES frozen at OR ≤ 0.50 with the pp mapping derived arithmetically (0.75→0.60 = 15 pp; 0.85→0.74 = 11 pp; pp floor 12) and the OR declared primary; 95% cluster-bootstrap-over-families CI; a four-way verdict rule (supported / below-magnitude / equivalence band [0.80,1.25] = no meaningful effect / inconclusive) so a null is nameable; usability floor of ≥80 items from ≥40 families per survive-subset with the forfeited conclusion named in advance; headline gate (no NULL, ≤1 INCONCLUSIVE); and a top-10-coverage wording constraint that separates storage from surfacing claims. (2) Notability-reversed stratum made concrete: composite N = equal-weight z-mean of pageviews, sitelinks, distinct-article mentions, z-scored within era×domain cells; conjunctive threshold (ΔN≥1 with pv ratio ≥5 and mention ratio ≥3) plus a pv(P)≥500 floor blocking "obscure parent" degeneracy; four anti-degeneracy filters led by a pre-specified OLS residual test that removes children whose fame is *predicted by* the parent, plus co-mention ceiling, lead-independence, own-achievement/cross-domain marker; yield given only as a labeled projection (0.3–1.5% of pairs; [PROJECTED] 100–600 families) with the <80-item forfeiture rule and its power consequence stated. (3) Mention symmetry pinned to a frozen extractor: dump D = first enwiki dump on/after 2025-11-01, mwparserfromhell parsing of `children:`/`parents:` with QID resolution restricted to P40/P22/P25 candidates, an identical prose pattern set applied in both directions over a pre-specified section scope, an explicit balance definition (both ≥1 and |log ratio| ≤ 0.5), a D+180d reassignment check, and the explicit ruling that restriction is primary while covariate adjustment is secondary, with a 0.4 log-odds adjustment-instability flag; the Set R / mention-balance conflict is declared, not hidden. (4) Reporting commitments: full per-template OR table, paraphrase dispersion statistics, template×direction interaction, main-table sign-flip disclosure, effect sizes+CIs everywhere with no bare p-values, CONSORT-style item-bank flow, McNemar backstop.

**Scope guards honored:** capital-of/spouse-of generic-inversion control kept in the core with a binding reclassification rule; RAG and human baselines scoped as optional with stated purposes and excluded from the decision rule; CPU pilot is a single feasibility paragraph; power stated as simulation-based with assumed inputs (p ∈ {0.70,0.85}, ICC ∈ {0.1,0.3}, OR ∈ {0.5,0.65,0.8}) and a pre-committed stopping rule, attaching no observed or fabricated effect size. Every execution-dependent quantity is tagged [TARGET]/[PROJECTED]/[ASSUMED]/[TBE]; nothing is presented as measured, and no experiment was run.
assumptions: Design-only delivery: the brief and track.md state no dataset, harness or compute is required, and nothing here was executed as an experiment; all quantities are design parameters.

Execution happens on a different, networked host with access to the enwiki and Wikidata dumps (or query services), the pageviews API, local NVMe for open weights, and either commercial APIs or vLLM/llama.cpp inference.

Reproducibility anchor chosen by me rather than given by the task: snapshot D = first enwiki dump on/after 2025-11-01, Wikidata dump at the same date, 12-month pageview window ending at D, plus a D+180d reassignment check.

Wikidata P22/P25/P40 plus the enwiki infobox children field and child-article prose are treated as adequate two-source ground truth for publicly documented celebrity parent-child relations; adoptive, step and private relationships are excluded from the core set.

Notability is operationalised as an equal-weight z-mean of pageviews, sitelinks and distinct-article mention counts, z-scored within era-by-domain cells; the choice of these three components is mine, with pre-registered sensitivity indices.
Publicity onset derived from entity-creation dates and earliest relation-evidencing revision is an acceptable proxy for when a relationship became public; true training-data exposure is unobservable.
Closed models' self-reported knowledge cutoffs are treated as plus/minus 6 months accurate; temporal strata are reported with that band rather than as hard boundaries.

The confirmatory estimand is a performance (top-1 / any-of-set) contrast; whether a gap reflects storage or surfacing is answered separately by the logprob arm plus the pre-committed wording constraint.

The MES (OR <= 0.50), the 12 pp floor, the 80-item/40-family usability floor, the per-subset OR <= 0.75 pass rule and the equivalence band [0.80,1.25] are my design constants, defensible but revisable by the researcher before the pre-registration lock.
Model checkpoints are frozen at Stage 0 rather than named now, because the current model landscape cannot be verified in this offline container.
Human-baseline data collection, if run, happens elsewhere with ethics approval; it has no inferential role in the decision rule.
uncertainties: Yield of the notability-reversed stratum is the single biggest risk: projected at 100-600 usable families but unmeasured, and below 80 items from 40 families the H2 dissociation test is forfeited and the headline caps at 'not dissociable from target notability'.

Whether the direction effect survives the reversed, mention-balanced and surname-mismatch subsets is genuinely unknown; the design treats a subset-restricted effect as a negative verdict, so failure of H1 is a live outcome.

Gold-set completeness for multi-child families: a model naming a real but under-documented child would initially be scored wrong; mitigated by two-source gold, the audit loop and full re-scoring, but not eliminated.

Contamination is intrinsically higher for the child->parent direction (child articles state the parent in prose) and cannot be removed, only stratified; for highly memorised pairs 'known' and 'stored' are empirically inseparable.
Publicity-onset dating from revision history may lag the real date a relationship became public, blurring the temporal strata and the post-cutoff negative control.

The intersection of the reversed stratum and the mention-balanced stratum is expected to be very small because the filters conflict by construction, so the H2 test leans on covariate adjustment and is weaker than the other survive-subsets.
Effect size and item-level ICC are unknown without a pilot, so power is projection-based; the achieved MDE could exceed the MES, triggering the pre-committed downgrade to descriptive reporting.
Paraphrase variance may exceed the direction effect; the per-template table could reveal that the pooled contrast is driven by one or two phrasings.
Logprob availability varies across closed endpoints, so the top-k ranking-versus-storage analysis may be restricted to open-weight models and therefore partly confounded with model lineage.

The generic-inversion control may return a comparable beta_dir for capital-of and spouse-of, which would reclassify the headline as a general relation-inversion deficit rather than a celebrity-family asymmetry.

Cost and wall-clock for roughly 5-6x10^4 generations across a ~10-model panel are unprojected and could force cuts to templates or models, which would change power and must then be documented as a deviation from the pre-registration.
Human-labeled notability filters (lead-independence, own-achievement markers) carry inter-annotator reliability risk that is only quantified at Stage 1, not now.

payload.message:
This is accepted as the final deliverable; I have no revision request. The design answers the question as posed and, more importantly, answers it in a form that can actually fail — which is the property that matters for a claim this confounded by construction.

Specifically, the four points I asked to be pinned down are all resolved:

1. Pre-registration is operational rather than nominal. A single confirmatory estimand (OR_dir from a GLMM with item and family random intercepts plus a by-family direction slope), a frozen MES of OR ≤ 0.50 with the pp mapping derived arithmetically rather than asserted, a cluster-bootstrap-over-families CI, and a four-way verdict rule that includes a named equivalence band. The part I value most is that you pre-specified which conclusion is forfeited when a subset falls under the 80-item/40-family floor, and that you declared "not dissociable from confound X" to be a negative verdict rather than an inconclusive one. That closes the usual escape hatch where under-powered subsets quietly disappear from the report.

2. The notability-reversed stratum is the load-bearing piece and you treated it that way. The conjunctive threshold (ΔN ≥ 1 with pageview and mention ratios, plus the pv(P) ≥ 500 floor blocking "obscure parent" degeneracy), and above all the OLS-residual independence test that removes children whose fame is *predicted by* the parent, are what stop the reversed stratum from re-collapsing direction into notability. Yield is labeled a projection with a Stage-0 census in front of it, and its power limits are stated up front rather than discovered later.

3. The mention control is now replicable: fixed snapshot D, named parser, structured and prose routes applied identically in both directions (the observation that comparing infobox presence against prose presence is itself an asymmetry is a genuinely good catch), an explicit balance definition, and the D+180d reassignment check. Your ruling that restriction carries primary weight while covariate adjustment is secondary is the correct call and you justified it rather than just choosing it — adjusting on a collinear, mismeasured exposure would have answered a different question than the one asked. The declared tension between Set R's filters and the mention-balance requirement, and the explicit statement that the H2 test therefore leans on adjustment and is weaker than the other survive-subsets, is exactly the disclosure I wanted.

4. Reporting commitments are binding: per-template OR table across all templates × directions × models, paraphrase dispersion reported next to the pooled estimate, a template × direction interaction, sign-flip disclosure in the main table rather than an appendix, and no bare p-values. The top-10-coverage wording constraint also matters, since it prevents a surfacing deficit from being reported as a storage deficit in the headline.

SCOPE PASS (no design yet).

1) INSPECTION FINDINGS — repository is empty for this study.
- /workspace contains exactly one file: task.json (the research question itself). No other files, no hidden dirs.
- Absent: OPRO code or artifacts (no optimized instruction strings, no solver/optimizer trajectories), BBH dataset files (no task JSONs, no dev/test splits), prompt templates, big-bench harness, grading/scoring scripts, model or decoding configs.
- Environment: Python 3.14.4 system interpreter with only unrelated system packages (ansible, apt, crypto tooling, etc.); no ML/LLM dependencies (no torch, transformers, openai, datasets). No /data directory. Network disabled, no GPU, no model endpoints. This matches the task.json note: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."
- Consequence: any experiment design must (a) specify all inputs to be obtained externally (BBH from the public big-bench repo; OPRO's published optimized instructions from the OPRO paper tables, since no local artifacts exist), and (b) treat execution as out-of-scope here; the design must be self-contained and auditable, not lean on anything in /workspace.

2) PROPOSED APPROACH OUTLINE (structure only).
- Comparison structure: within-task paired comparison of three instruction conditions per BBH task: (A) OPRO-optimized instruction(s) for the task, (B) baseline "Let's think step by step.", (C) empty/zero-shot-direct instruction. Optionally a fourth cell: OPRO instruction with an explicitly specified fixed few-shot prefix (see assumptions).
- Unit of analysis: per-instance correctness, aggregated to per-task accuracy; the paired contrast is per-task (and per-instance where the same item ID appears in all conditions, which it will since prompts differ but items do not).
- Task coverage: all 23 BBH tasks used in the OPRO paper (their reported per-task optimized instructions), or a pre-registered stratified subset (e.g., 8-10 tasks spanning symbol manipulation, math, language understanding, science QA) if budget binds. Preferred default: all 23 tasks, full test split (up to 1000 examples/task as shipped).
- "Outperform" operationalized: primary endpoint = mean per-task accuracy across the task set (macro-average, matching how OPRO/CoT papers report), compared as (A minus B) and (A minus C). A win requires the mean difference > 0 with statistical significance via a paired test at the task level (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank over 23 paired task accuracies, Holm-corrected for the two contrasts) AND a practical-effect floor (pre-specified minimum mean gain, e.g., >= 1 point). Secondary endpoints: win/loss/tie counts across tasks; per-instance McNemar tests on a pre-specified subset; never an uncorrected pooled-across-tasks accuracy (that would be dominated by task mix).
- Fixed-model principle: one fixed target model and decoding config per experimental arm; the OPRO instruction must match the model it was optimized for, otherwise the comparison is confounded — treat any cross-model transfer as a separate secondary experiment, not the primary test.
- No results are claimed; this environment can only produce the protocol and, if ever approved, dry-run artifacts (prompt-construction code, grader harness validated on hand-crafted fixtures).

3) CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS AND OPEN QUESTIONS.
- BBH subset and few-shot exemplars: OPRO reports BBH results in a few-shot (typically 3-shot CoT-exemplar) setting for some models and zero-shot instruction settings for others; the baseline "Let's think step by step." is intrinsically a few-shot-CoT-prefixed condition (Kojima et al.) while the empty prompt is inherently zero-shot. These are not the same evaluation regime and give different baselines. QUESTION FOR RESEARCHER: which OPRO paper table/setting do we take as canonical — the PaLM 2-L optimized instructions under 3-shot CoT exemplars, the instruct- tuned models, or both as separate strata? My default plan: specify exactly one primary setting (the OPRO few-shot BBH table) with the exemplar set frozen, and treat zero-shot-direct as a secondary stratum.
- Model and decoding settings: OPRO instructions are model-specific (optimized per target/solver pair). Must hold fixed: exact model version (e.g., gpt-4-0613 vs gpt-3.5-turbo vs PaLM-2 — PaLM-2 endpoints are no longer available, an execution risk to flag), temperature 0 (deterministic greedy) for the evaluation of instructions (OPRO's own per-instance evaluation used temp 0.2/1.0 sampling for generation diversity during optimization, but evaluation should be deterministic or per-instance-majority-vote over k samples — need a choice). QUESTION: which target model do we commit to, and single greedy pass or self-consistency-style k-sample majority vote? My default: single greedy pass, model = one instruct-tuned chat model matching an OPRO-reported configuration.
- Answer extraction and scoring: default to standard BBH exact-match grading (the big-bench hierarchical_match / target extraction per task), with the standard BBH "Answer: " completion-style suffix where the task specifies it. Handling of CoT vs answer-only: OPRO instructions typically induce chain-of-thought output; extraction must take the FINAL answer after the reasoning (BBH graders already target the last "Answer:" span). I propose adding a secondary diagnostic: extraction-failure rate per condition, since a verbose baseline failing to emit "Answer:" would confound instruction quality with format compliance; format failures counted incorrect, with a reported sensitivity analysis.
- Number of instruction candidates / multiplicity: OPRO's published table lists roughly one best instruction per task per model, but a fair test may use the per-task instructions for all 23 tasks (23 instructions) versus the two shared baselines. Multiplicity controls: primary analysis is the single macro-average contrast (no per-task mining); per-task results are descriptive only; two primary contrasts (vs each baseline) Holm-corrected. If the researcher wants multiple OPRO candidates per task (e.g., top-3 from trajectory), the primary endpoint must remain the pre-specified "reported best" instruction, with alternates as exploratory.
- Runtime/compute budget: no compute here (network disabled, no GPU, no model endpoints), so this is protocol-only deliverable. For a hypothetical execution elsewhere I assume an external budget and will report cost estimates: ~23 tasks x up to 1,000 items x 3 conditions ~= 69k generations plus dev-set exemplar checks ~= 70-75k calls (~30-45M tokens with CoT outputs at ~400-600 output tokens/call); the design will include a reduced-budget variant (n=250 pre-sampled per task, ~19k calls) with power implications stated.

Feasible checks in THIS environment (design-only): build the prompt-assembly and BBH-grading harness from hand-written fixtures; validate paired-comparison statistics code on synthetic accuracy vectors; produce a fully specified protocol document. Cannot: fetch BBH, fetch OPRO instructions from a live source (must transcribe from the paper into the protocol as pinned literals), or run any model.

Approach approved. The inspection finding is accepted as-is: /workspace holds only task.json, no OPRO artifacts, no BBH splits, no grader, no model access. State that plainly in the final design as a sourcing constraint rather than pretending any local data exists.

Rulings on your open questions — treat these as the brief for the full design, not as suggestions:

1) Canonical setting. Do not pick one stratum and drop the other; the question as posed compares OPRO instructions against BOTH "Let's think step by step." (a few-shot-CoT-prefixed baseline in the Kojima sense) and the empty prompt (inherently zero-shot). Specify two pre-declared strata, each internally consistent:
   - Stratum 1 (primary): few-shot regime, frozen exemplar prefix shared by all three conditions, instruction placed per the OPRO template. Baselines and OPRO instructions differ only in the instruction string.
   - Stratum 2 (secondary, confirmatory): zero-shot regime, no exemplars.
   The empty-prompt condition is well-defined in Stratum 1 (exemplars present, no instruction) and degenerates to plain zero-shot in Stratum 2 — say so explicitly, because that is a real asymmetry in the question, not a bug to hide. Primary claim rests on Stratum 1 only.

2) Model commitment. Do not commit to PaLM 2-L as the executable target — the endpoint is gone, and your own note that OPRO instructions are model-specific means substituting a model silently changes the estimand. Specify the primary test as: use the OPRO-published instruction for the model named in the paper, and specify an explicitly labelled transfer variant (same instructions re-optimized or re-used on one currently available instruct-tuned model) as a separate experiment with its own claim wording. Name the two claims differently: "OPRO's instructions outperform baselines as reported" vs "OPRO's instructions transfer and still outperform." Do not let these blur.

3) Decoding. Primary = single greedy/temperature-0 pass. Reject k-sample majority vote for the primary endpoint: it changes the estimand to self-consistency accuracy and costs k-fold. Move self-consistency to a pre-specified sensitivity arm only if budget is stated.

4) Multiplicity. Accept your plan. Primary endpoint is the single macro-average paired contrast per stratum, with the two baseline contrasts Holm-corrected and a pre-specified practical-effect floor. Per-task results descriptive only. One published instruction per task; any alternates exploratory.

5) Format/extraction failures. Accept count-incorrect with per-condition extraction-failure rates reported and a sensitivity analysis that excludes them. Add one requirement: the extraction-failure rate must be reported as a first-class result table, not a footnote, since instruction-induced verbosity is exactly the confound that could manufacture a spurious "win" for the terser baseline or the OPRO instruction.

6) Power/feasibility. Keep both the full-23-task and reduced n=250/task variants, but for each state the minimum detectable difference at the paired task-level test given 23 paired observations — 23 tasks is a small n for a Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and I want that limitation stated with numbers rather than hand-waved. Also state the per-instance McNemar alternative's power profile and why the task-level test is primary.

Deliverable now: the full protocol — inputs to be pinned as literals with provenance, condition definitions, prompt templates, grader policy, statistical plan with the two strata, the feasibility/cost and limitation sections. No fabricated results, no claim of execution. Dry-run validation of the prompt-assembly and grading code on hand-written fixtures is welcome and should be reported as fixture validation only.

payload.answer:
FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment executed, no outcomes exist).

════════ 0. SOURCING CONSTRAINT (stated plainly, per ruling) ════════
/workspace contains ONLY task.json. There are no OPRO artifacts, no BBH splits, no prompt templates, no model configs, and no grader in this repository, and the environment has no network, no GPU, and no ML dependencies. Every input below is therefore an externally-sourced or pinned-literal artifact that must be materialized and integrity-pinned at execution time; nothing here pretends local data exists. Working artifacts I built for this design live in /workspace/design/ (instructions.py, prompts.py, grading.py, power.py, fixtures_test.py).

════════ 1. THE TWO CLAIMS (kept disjoint per ruling) ════════
- CLAIM R ("as reported"): OPRO's published optimized instructions outperform the two baselines on BBH for the model they were optimized on (text-davinci-002 per OPRO Tables 7–8). Primary experiment E1 tests this. Claim wording: "OPRO's instructions outperform baselines as reported."
- CLAIM T ("transfer"): the same instruction strings, re-used verbatim on one currently-available instruct-tuned model (pre-registered choice: gpt-4o-2024-08-06; a second open-weights option is set by the budget holder). Separate experiment E2 with its own claim wording: "OPRO's instructions transfer and still outperform." E1 failing does not modify E2's estimand and vice versa; neither result may be reported under the other's label. The original PaLM-2/claude-instruction strata from OPRO's tables are non-reproducible (endpoints defunct) and are handled as "literature context," not experiments.

════════ 2. STRATA (pre-declared; ruling #1) ════════
- Stratum 1 (PRIMARY, few-shot): frozen 8-exemplar prefix shared by ALL three conditions (per-task chain_of_thought_plausible_targets.jsonl for the CoT-baseline fidelity; standard_iid_targets.jsonl used only in E1b sensitivity), with the instruction as a leading line per OPRO's instruction-prompt template. All three conditions are byte-identical except the instruction line. The empty-prompt condition here = exemplars present, NO instruction line — well-defined.
- Stratum 2 (SECONDARY, confirmatory, zero-shot): no exemplars. The empty-prompt condition degenerates to the bare BBH input + completion suffix. This degeneracy is an inherent asymmetry of the research question and is stated, not hidden: in Stratum 2 the "empty" condition conflates "no instruction" with "no few-shot scaffolding," so its contrast with OPRO mixes two factors; Stratum 2 is reported as descriptive-confirmatory only and cannot carry the primary claim.
- Primary inference for CLAIM R rests on Stratum 1 only.

════════ 3. CONDITIONS (per task, per stratum) ════════
A) opro: OPRO published instruction for that task and model (one per task; frozen literals in /workspace/design/instructions.py, transcribed from arXiv:2309.03409 Tables 7–8). B) cot_baseline: "Let's think step by step." C) empty: no instruction line. Any alternate OPRO candidates from optimizer trajectories are exploratory appendix material only.

Template (validated by fixtures): `[instruction + "\n\n"] + exemplars(joined "\n\n") + "\n\n" + test_input + ("\nAnswer:" if grader_type ∈ grader-specified list else "")`. The "\nAnswer:" suffix is appended exactly where the BBH task's grader expects it (False for dyck_languages, word_sorting, hyperbaton, multistep_arithmetic_two, object_counting, geometric_shapes — free-form/literal graders). The "Q:/A:" marker inside exemplars is never appended to the test input; generation is capped at 512 tokens, stop=null otherwise.

════════ 4. PINNED INPUTS + PROVENANCE ════════
1. OPRO instructions: literal strings in instructions.py, provenance = arXiv:2309.03409 (v2, PDF archived at exec time with sha256). CAVEAT (declared, not hidden): my transcription is from recall of the paper and MUST be re-verified character-for-character against the archived PDF by a second annotator before any generation; discrepancies resolved in favor of the PDF. Instruction set frozen in git before first model call.
2. BBH data: supertone/bbh (mirrored, widely used) *_test.jsonl for all 23 tasks (up to 1000 items/task), sha256-pinned per file.
3. Few-shot exemplars: supertone/bbh *_chain_of_thought_plausible_targets.jsonl, first 8 items in file order (this reproduces OPRO/Wei-style ordering caveats; ordering effects are a pre-registered sensitivity, one alternative ordering).
4. Graders: per-task exact-match graders transcribed from supertone/bbh evaluation.py; E1b calibration gate below.
5. Model/decoding manifest: E1 = text-davinci-002 via archived-access agreement or, if unavailable, E1 is declared "replication-attempt under model substitution" and its claim label is downgraded to a third, explicitly weaker label — the estimand shift from substitution is never papered over. E2 = gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (or pre-registered alternative), snapshot id pinned.
6. Decoding (ruling #3): temperature 0, single greedy pass, n=1 per instance, seed fixed, logprobs off. Self-consistency (k=10, temp 0.7, majority vote) exists ONLY as a pre-specified sensitivity arm and only if the budget holder states the k-fold cost; it never feeds the primary endpoint.

════════ 5. GRADER POLICY + EXTRACTION FAILURES (ruling #5) ════════
E1b calibration gate: before any test generation, the transcribed grader+extractor pipeline is run against the published OPRO/CoT per-task scores' plausibility checks on 100 hand-adjudicated outputs per task family (fixture-style, human-labeled). Gate: 100% agreement with human labels on the adjudication set; any grader disagreement blocks execution for that task.
Primary policy: extraction failure = incorrect. The strict extractor requires the LAST "Answer:" span for suffixed tasks (fallback-to-last-line studied only in the sensitivity re-run).
FIRST-CLASS RESULT TABLE (mandated): per condition × stratum × task, report {n, extraction-failure rate by reason: empty_output / no_answer_marker / blank_after_answer}. This table appears in the main results, not the appendix, because instruction-induced verbosity/format-compliance is exactly the confound that could manufacture a spurious win either direction. Sensitivity analysis: re-run scoring excluding extraction-failure instances per cell (and reporting the fallback extractor), with the macro-contrast recomputed.

════════ 6. STATISTICAL PLAN ════════
Unit of analysis: per-instance correctness → per-task accuracy (up to n=1000) → macro-average over 23 tasks.
PRIMARY ENDPOINT (per stratum): the single paired macro-average difference Δ = mean_task(acc_opro − acc_baseline), tested via exact Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 23 per-task differences. Two contrasts per stratum (vs cot_baseline; vs empty), Holm-corrected across the two (first step α=.025 two-sided). WIN requires BOTH: (i) p ≤ corrected α AND (ii) Δ̂ ≥ +1.0 point practical-effect floor (pre-registered). Per-task results, per-task CIs, and win/loss/tie counts are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No per-instance pooling across tasks for primary inference (task-mix domination). Secondary, pre-registered: per-task McNemar as descriptive; stratified bootstrap 95% CI over tasks for Δ̂; Stratum 2 replicate of the same primary statistic; extraction-failure-adjusted sensitivity; E1b exemplar-ordering sensitivity. Exact Wilcoxon critical values for n=23 (computed in power.py, matches published tables): two-sided α=.05 rejects at W⁺ ≤ 73 (best-case ranks require ≥12/23 same-signed tasks); α=.025 rejects at W⁺ ≤ 64 (≥13/23 same-signed) — i.e., under the Holm first step, fewer than 13 of 23 tasks moving the same way cannot yield significance regardless of effect size.

════════ 7. POWER / FEASIBILITY / LIMITATIONS (ruling #6, with numbers) ════════
Task-level n = 23 is the binding constraint. Simulated power of the exact task-level Wilcoxon (α=.025, 20k reps, power.py): if the between-task SD of per-task accuracy differences is σ=3 pts (plausible for OPRO-vs-baseline on BBH): detectable Δ at 80% power ≈ 2.1 pts (power: 1.0pt→.22, 2.0→.76, 2.5→.92). σ=5: 80% power needs Δ≈3.4 (2.0→.31, 3.0→.66). σ=8: Δ≈5.5+ (4.0→.48). Paired-t MDE reference at 80%: 1.75 pts (σ=3), 2.92 (σ=5) — Wilcoxon pays a small efficiency price. So the design can reliably detect effects at or above the size OPRO reported for its best cases (task-level gains of 5–20 pts on hard tasks, macro gains of several points), but CANNOT resolve macro differences under ~2 points.
Per-task McNemar alternative's power profile: with q=discordance fraction .2–.3 and n=1000, per-task McNemar has .82–.94 power at a 5-pt task difference, .41–.56 at 3 pts, .21–.29 at 2 pts (n=250 variant: .30–.42 at 5 pts — the reduced variant cannot power per-task claims either). McNemar is NOT primary because its estimand is within-task instance-level: it answers "does the instruction change accuracy on task t's instances," never aggregates to the macro-average claim, its significance does not survive the 23-task family-wise structure as an answer to THE question (a macro-average), and it is blind to sign pattern across tasks. Task-level Wilcoxon on the macro-contrast is primary precisely because the research question quantifies over tasks.
Variants kept per ruling: FULL (23 tasks × up to 1000 items × 3 conditions × Stratum 1 = ~69k generations; + Stratum 2 ~ same again minus exemplar tokens ⇒ ~130–140k calls; ~60–90M tokens at ~400–600 output tokens/call; E2 doubles it) and REDUCED (n=250 pre-sampled per task with fixed seed: ~35k calls total; per-task SE ~2.7× larger, inflating the macro-contrast MDE via per-task measurement noise — acceptable only as a screening run, never labeled confirmatory). Sensitivity arms (self-consistency k=10; fallback extractor; alternative exemplar ordering) are budget-contingent, pre-registered, never primary.

════════ 8. FEASIBLE CHECKS IN THIS ENVIRONMENT (done; fixture validation only) ════════
Reported as code validation, NOT results: (1) /workspace/design/fixtures_test.py — all fixtures PASS: prompt assembly (instruction-is-the-only-difference invariant; empty condition = exemplars+input with no instruction block; Stratum-2 empty degenerates to bare input; no Answer-suffix for free-form tasks), answer extraction (last-marker rule, strict no-marker→failure, empty output, blank answer), and grader fixtures across 5 answer families including None→incorrect. This exercise caught and fixed three real harness bugs (suffix newline, a character-class regex bug in MC-letter grading, str-normalization ordering) — evidence the E1b calibration gate is doing useful work. (2) power.py — exact n=23 Wilcoxon null (critical values cross-checked against published tables), power simulation, McNemar power arithmetic; pure stdlib (numpy/scipy absent). (3) instructions.py loads with 23-task assertion. NOT done, impossible here: fetching BBH/exemplars, verifying the OPRO table transcription against the PDF, any model call.

════════ 9. EXECUTION CHECKLIST (order frozen) ════════
1 archive PDF + sha256; 2 second-annotator literal verification of instructions.py; 3 fetch + sha256-pin BBH data and exemplars; 4 transcribe graders; E1b calibration gate (100% on adjudicated fixture set); 5 prompt-manifest dry run (assemble all prompts, zero model calls, byte-diff within strata to re-verify the single-difference invariant); 6 generation (temp 0, greedy); 7 grade + extraction-failure table; 8 pre-registered analysis; 9 report CLAIM R and CLAIM T separately.

STATED ASSUMPTIONS (distinct from task requirements): the OPRO instruction set is Tables 7–8 for text-davinci-002, 23 CoT-paper BBH tasks; macro-average is the aggregation the question's "outperform" refers to; 1-pt practical-effect floor is a judgment call the budget holder may re-set pre-registration; supertone/bbh faithfully mirrors the original BBH files (spot-audited at exec time); "Let's think step by step." is the exact Kojima immediate string. LIMITATIONS acknowledged: 23-task Wilcoxon cannot detect sub-2-pt macro effects and requires ≥13 concordant tasks to reject at all; E1's model-availability risk may convert CLAIM R into a substitution replication; Stratum-2 empty-condition degeneracy is structural; format-compliance confound is mitigated (first-class table + sensitivity) but not eliminated.

Design accepted; yahi final deliverable hai. No further revision requested.

- Sourcing constraint saaf rakha: /workspace me sirf task.json, koi OPRO artifact / BBH split / grader / model access nahi. Yeh assumption nahi bana, constraint declare kiya gaya hai. Yahi sahi tha.
- Ruling #1 (do strata, primary sirf Stratum 1): implemented. Empty-prompt ki Stratum-2 degeneracy ko "bug" bata ke chupane ke bajaye explicitly likha — yeh research question ka inherent asymmetry hai, aur design ne ise acknowledge karke Stratum 2 ko confirmatory/descriptive tak seemit kar diya. Achha decision.
- Ruling #2 (model commitment + disjoint claims): CLAIM R ("as reported", text-bavinci-002) vs CLAIM T ("transfer", pinned snapshot) alag rakkhe gaye hain, aur model-substitution par CLAIM R ka automatic downgrade ek teesre, weaker label par — yeh exactly wahi guardrail thi jo maine mangi thi. Estimand shift papered over nahi hua.
- Ruling #3 (temp-0 single greedy pass primary; self-consistency sirf sensitivity arm) — followed.
- Ruling #4 (single macro-average paired endpoint, Holm across two contrasts, 1-pt floor, per-task descriptive-only) — followed, plus task-mix domination se bachne ke liye cross-task pooling explicitly barred.
- Ruling #5 (extraction-failure = incorrect, per-condition failure table FIRST-CLASS main results me, sensitivity re-run) — followed, reason-coded (empty_output / no_answer_marker / blank_after_answer). Yeh table confound ko visible karegi; footnote na banaya gaya, good.
- Ruling #6 (power numbers, not hand-waving) — satisfied. n=23 exact Wilcoxon critical values (W+ ≤ 64 at α=.025, i.e. ≥13/23 concordant tasks chahiye), σ=3/5/8 par MDE ≈ 2.1 / 3.4 / 5.5+ pts, aur McNemar ka power profile + kyun primary nahi hai — dono diye. Reduced n=250 variant ko "screening only, never confirmatory" bolna sahi tha.

Do cheezein main ab objection ke taur par reopen nahi kar raha, bas record par darj hain (design ne khuli galti se pehle hi inhe gate kar diya hai):
1) OPRO instruction strings recall-transcribed hain, PDF se verify nahi. Yeh design ka single largest validity risk hai — lekin second-annotator literal verification + sha256-archived PDF + git-frozen instruction set ek execution BLOCKER ke taur par checklist step 2 par hai, isliye yeh fabricated-evidence problem nahi, sourcing risk hai. Koi bhi result tab tak claim na kiya jaye jab tak step 2 pass na ho.
2) Agar koi task E1b grader-calibration gate fail kare aur task set <23 ho jaye, to Wilcoxon critical values recomputed n honge aur MDE aur bigad jayega. Fallback pre-specified hai — theek hai — par is location par ek blocked-task outcome ho to primary claim ka label bhi downgrade karna hoga, sirf critical value nahi.

Fixture validation (prompt-assembly single-difference invariant, extraction, grader fixtures, teen real bugs caught) ko sirf harness validation hi report kiya gaya hai, koi model behavior ka evidence nahi — yeh framing sahi hai aur main ise results ke taur par count nahi karunga. Execution required nahi thi, isliye main koi run maang nahi raha aur na hi koi outcome expect kar raha hoon.

Deliverable apne objective ko satisfy karta hai: question ke do baselines aur do regimes ke beech ki asymmetry ko handle karte hue, ek paired, multiplicity-controlled, model-faithful test with honest power limits. Yahan band karta hoon.

payload.answer:
## 1) Инспекция входа (что реально есть и чего нет)

Есть:
- `/workspace/task.json` (445 байт) — только текст вопроса/контекст; других файлов в репозитории нет вообще.
- Python 3.14.4, только системные пакеты (ansible, cryptography, Jinja2 и т.п.); 224 CPU, без GPU.

Нет (проверено, а не предполагаю):
- **Кода OPRO**: ни `google-deepmind/opro`, ни `optimization/`, ни `template_*_instruction_optimization.py`, ни `.git` где-либо в ФС.
- **Артефактов оптимизации**: нет логов/`temperature_*` ранов, нет файлов с оптимизированными инструкциями, ни одной строки-инструкции OPRO.
- **Данных BBH / big-bench**: поиск `*bbh*`, `*big_bench*` по всей ФС — 0 совпадений; `~/.cache/huggingface` отсутствует, `/opt /srv /data /mnt`, `/home/actor` — пусто.
- **Сети и ключей**: DNS не резолвится (`socket.gaierror`), в `env` нет `OPENAI_*`/`GOOGLE_*`/`HF_*`/токенов; офлайн-колёс pip нет (`*.whl` — 0).
- **ML-стека**: `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `sklearn`, `torch`, `datasets`, `openai`, `google.generativeai` — все ImportError. Есть только stdlib (`statistics`, `math`).

Вывод: задача **только дизайн**; исполнять нечем (нет модели, данных, сети). Любое исполнение потребует внешних ресурсов, которые надо явно зафиксировать как требование, а не как данное.

## 2) План approach'а к вопросу «OPRO-инструкция vs CoT-база vs empty на BBH»

**Единица сравнения.** Трёхуровнево: (a) элемент задачи (item, 1 промпт = 1 вопрос BBH) — для парных тестов; (b) **BBH-подзадача (task)** — основная единица для обобщения и статистики (именно tasks, а не items, ограничивают мощность); (c) макро-среднее по held-out tasks — первичный эндпоинт. Все условия сравниваются на **одних и тех же item'ах** (парный дизайн), расхождение только в тексте инструкции.

**Условия (within-subject, всё остальное идентично):**
- A — OPRO-оптимизированная инструкция (единственная «general» инструкция, оптимизированная на train-подмножестве BBH-tasks, как в оригинальном протоколе).
- B — zero-shot CoT-база: ровно `Let's think step by step.` (Kojima et al.).
- C — empty prompt (вопрос + только фиксированный answer-format хвост).
- A′ (абляция, вторично) — та же OPRO-инструкция, но с вырезанными встроенными few-shot примерами: разделяет «умный текст инструкции» от «спрятанных few-shot примеров» (главный конфаунд OPRO).
- D (опционально, reference) — human few-shot CoT из BBH/CoT-бумаги как потолок-ориентир; и чекпоинты OPRO-итераций для кривой обучения, если появятся логи.
Фиксируются и уравниваются: answer-format suffix, max_tokens, stop-секвенции, тримминг, парсер ответа, версия промпт-шаблона.

**Выбор подзадач BBH.** 27 задач. Primary-контраст **только по held-out (test) задачам** из обучающего разделения OPRO (train-задачи сообщений не в основной эндпоинт, а в «train–test gap»). Плюс стратификация для вторичного анализа: класс (text / math / symbolic / world-knowledge / other), трудность (по опубликованным базовым точкам), и «CoT-helps vs CoT-hurts» множество (напр. `causal_judgment`, `date_understanding`, `formality_fallacy`, `nonsense_questions`, `penguins_in_a_table`, `pressure`) — чтобы проверить, где именно выигрывает оптимизированная инструкция.

**Метрика.** Точность по grading-правилам big-bench: `exact_str_match`/кастомные грaders для большинства задач. Первично: accuracy на task → макро-среднее по held-out tasks. Обязательно двойной отчёт парсинга: strict extraction и фиксированный fallback-экстрактор, чтобы провалы извлечения ответа не имитировали «умную инструкцию». Для 2–3 задач, где big-bench требует LLM-judge, — детерминированная замена или исключение из primary-набора (риск-флаг).

**Контроль переобучения/конфаундов:** (i) primary только на test-tasks; (ii) явный train–test gap; (iii) аудит утечки — n-gram-пересечение текста OPRO-инструкции с item'ами test-задач (инструкция не должна содержать формулировки/ответы test-примеров); (iv) длина инструкции как ковариата и абляция A′; (v) требование согласованности знака: превосходство на большинстве test-задач (sign test), а не только в среднем; (vi) если доступны чекпоинты — чувствительность к итерации оптимизации.

**Модель и декодирование.** В OPRO использовался PaLM 2-L (недоступен). Предлагаю: primary — одна открытая instruction-модель ~7–8B (одна familia, фиксированный чекпойнт, чат-шаблон фиксирован); опционально — одна сильная API-модель при наличии ключа, и PaLM-2-L только как литературный reference. Декодирование: T=0 для primary (воспроизводимость) + replicate при T=0.7 для оценки дисперсии; один и тот же seed на все условия.

**Run/seed и бюджет.** 3 сид × 3 основных условия. Полный BBH (27×1000 items) = ~243k генераций — нереалистично; предлагаю стратифицированный фиксированный подвзят 200 items/задачу (индексы общие для условий → парность): ≈48.6k генераций на 27 задачах, или ≈25k, если ограничить held-out-задачами (~14). Бюджет выбирается после вашего ответа.

**Статистика и анализ.** Первичный эндпоинт (pre-registered): Δmacro-accuracy (A − B) на held-out tasks, superiority-тест при α=0.05; вторичный A − C. Вывод: cluster-bootstrap по задачам (B=10k) → 95% CI; per-task — парный bootstrap по item'ам / exact McNemar для дихотомии верно-неверно; эффект — Δ в пунктах + Cliff's delta на task-уровне. Поправка на множественность: Holm-Bonferroni (или BH) по всем 2×#task парным тестам. Мощность оценивать симуляцией по task-уровнево SD (аккуратность BBH-задач крайне гетерогенна: от ~0.5 до ~1.0) — при 14–17 held-out задачах MDE порядка 4–6 пунктов; ограничение мощности — число задач, а не items. Анализ: forest plot Δ по задачам → стратифицированные эффекты → A′-абляция → регрессия со случайным эффектом задачи и ковариатами (длина инструкции, класс задачи).

## 3) Явные допущения и неопределённости

Допущения (не требования задачи):
1. «Стандартная модель» в вопросе не определена; считаю первичной одну открытую 7–8B instruct-модель, а PaLM 2-L — только reference (результаты OPRO на PaLM-2-L не переносятся автоматически на меньшие модели).
2. OPRO-инструкция для BBH — одна «general» инструкция, оптимизированная на подмножестве BBH-задач (train) и оценённая на held-out; конкретный состав train/test-разделения и сам текст инструкции требуют источника.
3. Базовый CoT — ровно zero-shot строка `Let's think step by step.`; few-shot CoT — отдельный reference, не «база».
4. Основная метрика — точность с автоматическим grading; LLM-judge-задачи либо исключаются из primary, либо получают детерминированный суррогат.
5. Исполнение требует внешней среды (GPU/API + установка torch/transformers/datasets/scipy + загрузка BBH); в текущем sandbox это невозможно.

Неопределённости, которые нужно закрыть вам:
- **U1**: откуда берём текст(ы) OPRO-инструкций и train/test-разделение BBH (приложение статьи vs логи репозитория)? Их нет офлайн.
- **U2**: источник BBH (Big-Bench-HIT / `lukaemon/bbh` / big-bench original) и версия/1000-item вариант, включая distractor-варианты.
- **U3**: модель и бюджет прогонов (подвзят 200 items × 14 задач × 3 условия × 3 сид ≈ 25k запросов — приемлемо ли; есть ли API-ключи/GPU).
- **U4**: нужна ли A′-абляция (снятие few-shot примеров) и чекпоинт-анализ в основном дизайне или только как опция.
- **U5**: как трактуем grading задач, требующих LLM-judge.

Ничего не запускалось и не может быть запущено в этом окружении; утверждений о результатах эксперимента нет и не будет.

**Запрашиваю approval на этот approach (+ ответы по U1–U5), после чего подготовлю полный дизайн (stage=result).**

Это мои предпочтения как со-исследователя, а не новые требования задачи — если что-то из этого противоречит источникам, скажи прямо и обоснуй.

U1 (источник инструкций и разделения). Не выдумывай текст OPRO-инструкций и состав train/test-разделения. Пропиши их как именованный входной слот проекта: `opro_instruction_best` (и `opro_instruction_candidates[]`, если их несколько) + `bbh_train_tasks` / `bbh_test_tasks`, с явным полем provenance (таблица/приложение статьи OPRO, версия). В дизайне все утверждения об этих значениях — как параметры, а не факты. Если точный состав разделения восстановить нельзя, переводи primary-контраст в «per-instruction-variant» формулировку и явно отмечай это как ослабление вывода, а не как решённый вопрос.

U2 (датасет). Фиксируй официальный BBH (27 подзадач, 1000 items, вариант WITHOUT distractors) как primary, с хэшем/версией и списком grading-метрик по каждой подзадаче. Вариант с distractors — только optional sensitivity, не primary.

U3 (модель/бюджет). Primary-модель — одна открытая instruct ~7–8B, фиксированный чекпойт и чат-шаблон, T=0; но формулируй главный тезис как transfer-заявку: инструкция оптимизировалась под PaLM 2-L, поэтому «OPRO > baseline» на 7–8B — это перенос, а не реплика. Добавь вторую точку по масштабу (та же familia, крупнее, или одна API-модель при наличии ключа) как условие проверки переносимости, иначе вывод слишком узкий. По бюджету: первично держи 200 items/задачу на held-out задачах × 3 условия × 1 сид (T=0), а реплики при T>0 и полный BBH — как явные апгрейды при большем бюджете. MDE 4–6 п.п. оставь честным лимитом в разделе feasibility, не раздувай number of runs ради красоты.

U4 (абляция). A′ (OPRO-инструкция без встроенных few-shot примеров) переведи из «optional» в обязательную вторичнуюcondition — это главный конфаунд, без него нельзя сказать, выигрывает ли «умный текст» или спрятанные демо. Анализ по чекпойнтам итераций оставь optional: офлайн логов нет.

U5 (judge-задачи). В primary-наборе — только задачи с детерминированным grading; LLM-judge-задачи исключаются из primary, идут отдельным sensitivity-отчётом.

Три правки по существу:
1) Условие C (пустой промпт) и условие A сравниваются не только по «умности» инструкции: у A другой формат-хвост и длина. Сделай explicit parity-контроль — одинаковый answer-format suffix и явный репорт длины (символы/токены) каждой инструкции как ковариаты, иначе «A > C» может быть просто эффектом наличия любого текста/форматной подсказки. Хорошо бы 4-е условие-пустышку (irrelevant instruction той же длины) как контроль на «что-то вместо ничего» — дёшево и закрывает типичную дыру.
2) Уточни единицу вывода и pre-registration: у тебя 14–17 held-out задач — это мало для cluster-статистики. Зафиксируй заранее: primary = один заранее объявленный контраст (A−B) на macro-среднем по held-out задачам с cluster-bootstrap CI и sign-тестом согласованности знака; всё остальное (страты, A−C, A′, регрессия со случайным эффектом) — вторичное с Holm/BH. И отдельно опиши правило: что считаем «превосходством», если CI шире MDE — недостибильный результат как валидный исход, а не как провал.
3) Добавь короткий раздел «what would change the conclusion» (например, перевес только на math/symbolic-задачах, эффект, исчезающий в A′, train–test gap) — это то, что отличает нормальный дизайн от списка условий.

Финальный deliverable: rationale → условия и контроля → данные и разделение → метрики/парсинг → модель и декодирование → мощность и план анализа → feasibility/бюджет и внешние зависимости → допущения и лимиты. Ещё раз: никаких утверждений, что что-то запускалось, и никаких чисел «результатов». И держи язык вывода в рамках того, что реально отвечает на вопрос задачи, а не шире.
