payload.answer:
# Diseño experimental: impacto de la cuantización completa 4 bits de QuaRot en el rendimiento de prefill y decoding de LLaMA-2

**Estado**: diseño solo. No se ejecutó ningún experimento (el entorno no tiene GPU, repo de QuaRot, checkpoints ni datasets). Todas las referencias de hardware/E/S son de diseño; todo detalle de QuaRot proviene de memoria paramétrica y va etiquetado como supuesto a reconciliar con el paper (arXiv:2404.00456) y el repo oficial.

## 1. Objetivo e hipótesis
Cuantificar el efecto del pipeline end-to-end W4A4KV4 de QuaRot (pesos INT4 + activaciones INT4 + KV cache INT4, con rotaciones de Hadamard offline fusionadas y rotación Hadamard online) sobre la velocidad de prefill y de decoding de LLaMA-2 7B/13B, con la calidad como control de validez.
- **H1 (prefill)**: QuaRot acelera el prefill por GEMMs INT4 (vía emulación INT8 en A100), atenuado por el costo de cuantizar activaciones y aplicar Hadamard online; speedup esperado de diseño: ~1.4–1.8×.
- **H2 (decoding)**: decoding (limitado por ancho de banda) se beneficia ~4× del reducido de pesos+KV; speedup de diseño: ~2.5–3.5× (techo roofline ~3.5×).
- **H3 (régimen)**: la ventaja de decode se mantiene hasta batches donde la KV cache dominada en FP16 hace el paso aún más memory-bound; la cuantización ensancha el régimen memory-bound y posterga el crossover a cómputo (batch alto).
- **H4 (atribución)**: la mayor parte de la ganancia viene de pesos+KV de 4 bits; la rotación de Hadamard online impone un overhead medible en batches pequeños, y sin rotación (W4A4KV4 directo) la calidad se degrada fuera de tolerancia.

## 2. Alcance
- **Modelos**: LLaMA-2 **base** (no chat — supuesto declarado) 7B y 13B, un checkpoint por modelo, una sola **A100-80GB** como referencia.
- **Fuera de alcance (limitación/extensión futura)**: LLaMA-2 70B y tensor-parallel (requiere multi-GPU y cambiaría los cuellos de botella medidos); variantes chat; modelos no-LLaMA; CPU/otros aceleradores.

## 3. Condiciones de tratamiento (6, cerradas por el brief)
| # | Condición | Rol |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | FP16 (ruta FP16 del mismo harness de QuaRot) | Referencia obligatoria |
| C2 | W4A16 (GPTQ, pesos INT4, act. FP16) | Contexto industrial |
| C3 | W8A8 (SmoothQuant) | Contexto industrial |
| C4 | **QuaRot W4A4KV4** | Tratamiento principal |
| C5 | QuaRot W4A4 + KV16 | Ablación: contribución de KV4 |
| C6 | W4A4KV4 **sin rotación** (GPTQ/RNTN directo) | Ablación: valor de la rotación + costo del Hadamard online |

Equidad: misma infraestructura de serving/benchmark para todas las condiciones (harness del repo QuaRot con kernels Triton/CUTLASS para todas las rutas cuantizadas y para FP16), misma versión, mismos kernels de attention salvo lo impuesto por la precisión de KV.

## 4. Factores y grid
- Modelo: {7B, 13B}
- Batch: {1, 4, 8, 16, 32} (C1/C2/C3 pueden OOM en B=32+S=4096 para 13B en KV16 → registrar "no cabe" como resultado de capacidad, no descartar)
- Prefill: prompt S ∈ {128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096}
- Decoding: contexto inicial S ∈ {512, 2048, 4096} × generación G ∈ {32, 128, 512}
- Régimen: batch=1 (latencia interactiva, TTFT/ITL) y batching alto (throughput), ambos por diseño del brief.
- Celdas de rendimiento: 6 cond × 2 modelos × (5×5 prefill + 4×3×3 decode) ≈ 1 440 celdas + barrido de capacidad máxima de batch por (cond, modelo, S).

## 5. Métricas
**Primarias (velocidad, reportadas por separado y end-to-end):**
- Prefill: latencia (mediana, p95) y throughput de prompt (tokens/s); TTFT end-to-end.
- Decoding: latencia por token ITL (mediana, p95) y throughput de salida (tokens/s).
- End-to-end: tokens/s totales por solicitud y por unidad de tiempo; tiempo total por solicitud.
- Memoria: pico de GPU (pesos / KV cache por separado), máximo batch×contexto viable.

**Control de validez (calidad)**: perplexity WikiText-2 y exactitud LAMBADA como mínimos; batería zero-shot amplia (PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, GSM8K, MMLU) solo si el presupuesto lo permite.
**Criterio de éxito numérico (fijado aquí)**: un speedup se reporta como **válido** solo si, para el mismo modelo: |ΔPPL WikiText-2| ≤ **+0.5** absoluto (y ≤ +8% relativo) y Δexactitud LAMBADA ≥ **−3.0 pp** vs C1 FP16. Condiciones que excedan la tolerancia se reportan igualmente pero etiquetadas "speedup con pérdida de calidad fuera de tolerancia". Semillas: 3 para la calibración; se reporta media±rango de calidad.

## 6. Protocolo
1. **Cuantización**: calibración C4 (512 muestras × 2048 tokens), GPTQ por grupo (grupo 128) para pesos; rotaciones Hadamard offline fusionadas en pesos (R1, R2); Hadamard online donde la arquitectura lo exija (p. ej. entrada de down_proj); KV4 por-token (esquema exacto = supuesto a reconciliar con el repo). Cada cuantización se fija con semillas registradas y se reutiliza para todas las corridas de rendimiento.
2. **Medición**: GPU exclusiva, clocks bloqueados, temperatura monitoreada; 5 warmup + 30 iteraciones cronometradas por celda de prefill (CUDA events, sin sincronizaciones dentro de la región); decoding: 6 generaciones completas por celda, ITL por token registrada y agregada; orden de condiciones aleatorizado por bloque (modelo); reinicio de proceso y memoria entre condiciones; 3 repeticiones de todo el bloque para estimar varianza de sistema.
3. **Reporte de capacidad**: búsqueda binaria del mayor batch que quepa por (cond, S); la KV4 debe predecir ~4× más cabida — verificación cruzada con la memoria medida.
4. **Integridad**: hashes de checkpoints y artefactos cuantizados; logging de versión de kernels; misma secuencia de tokens de entrada para todas las condiciones (mismos prompts sintéticos de longitud exacta + un conjunto de prompts reales de ShareGPT-style para reportar ITL en distribución realista).

## 7. Plan de análisis
- Efecto principal: speedup = métrica(C1)/métrica(C4) por celda (modelo × batch × longitud); resumen con intervalos bootstrap (10k remuestreos) sobre repeticiones; regresión de log-latencia con factores condición × log(batch) × log(S) para curvas de escalamiento.
- Atribución (H4): C4−C5 = contribución de KV4; C4−C6 = valor/overhead de la rotación (velocidad y calidad por separado); C2/C3 sitúan a C4 en el frente industrial.
- H3: curva throughput-vs-batch por condición; estimar el punto donde el paso de decode se vuelve compute-bound (regresión por segmentos o cambio de pendiente).
- Entrega: tablas prefill y decode por separado, figuras TTFT/ITL vs batch en los dos regímenes, frente Pareto calidad-latencia (PPL vs ITL), y veredicto explícito de tolerancia por condición.

## 8. Sanity-check analítico CPU-only (calculado en este entorno, no es medición del modelo)
Modelo roofline A100-80GB (BW 2.04 TB/s, FP16 TC 312 TFLOPS, INT8 624 TOPS como proxy de GEMM INT4 emulado; ridge ≈ 153 FLOP/byte):
- **Footprint**: 7B: pesos 13.5 GB→3.9 GB (INT4 c/ overhead); KV 128→40 KB/tok. 13B: 26 GB→7.5 GB; KV 160→50 KB/tok. → habilita batches/longitudes inviables en FP16 (p. ej. 13B FP16 con B=32×S=4096 necesita 26 GB de pesos + 24 GB de KV).
- **Arithmetic intensity de decode**: AI ≈ 1 (B=1) a ~60-70 (B=32, S=4096) — casi siempre ≪ ridge → memory-bound en ambas rutas; techo de speedup de decode ≈ 3.3–3.5× en todo el grid (dominado por el ratio de bytes), decreciendo levemente con batch por el peso relativo de KV.
- **Prefill**: compute-bound → techo ≈ 2× (tasa INT8) menos overhead de rotación/cuantización ⇒ predicción de diseño 1.4–1.8×. Estas predicciones acotan lo observable: un resultado fuera de estos órdenes (p. ej. decode >4× sostenido) indicaría artefacto de medición.

## 9. Presupuesto de tiempo/cómputo (referencia, 1× A100-80GB)
- Límite inferior roofline del barrido completo: prefill ~6 GPU-h, decode ~2 GPU-h, calidad mínima ~5 GPU-h (este cálculo ignora overheads reales).
- Estimación realista (×3–5 por launch-overhead en batch=1, carga/descarga, arranques, OOM-retries): **rendimiento ~60–100 GPU-h + calidad ~15–25 GPU-h + cuantizaciones ~20–30 GPU-h ≈ 100–160 GPU-h ⇒ 1–2 semanas en una A100** (o ~3–5 días con 2–3 GPUs en paralelo por condición). Batería zero-shot amplia: +15–30 GPU-h (opcional).

## 10. Tabla de riesgos
| Riesgo | Impacto | Mitigación |
|---|---|---|
| Gteo de checkpoints de Meta (LLaMA-2) | Bloqueante | Solicitar acceso con antelación; alternativa LLaMA-1/Pythia solo como fallback declarado (cambia la comparabilidad con el paper) |
| Madurez de kernels INT4 (Triton/CUTLASS; A100 sin tensor cores INT4 nativos → emulación INT8) | Subestima speedup real si los kernels son lentos | Reportar eficiencia de GEMM aislado (µ-benchmark) junto al end-to-end; separar "costo de QuaRot en este stack" de "costo de QuaRot en teoría" |
| Overhead del Hadamard online domina batches pequeños | Anula la ganancia de decode en B=1 | Medir la transformación online aislada; reportar descomposición del paso de decode |
| Inestabilidad de GPTQ a 4 bits en 7B | C4/C6 fuera de tolerancia de calidad | Verificar con el criterio de tolerancia antes de atribuir speedups; reportar calidad por semilla |
| Implementación de SmoothQuant/W8A8 no idéntica al paper | Baselines injustos | Usar implementación estándar (p. ej. la ruta del repo base) y declararla; µ-benchmark de GEMM W8A8 |
| Ruido de sistema (clocks, vecino en el nodo, allocador) | Varianza de ITL | GPU exclusiva, clocks fijos, bloques aleatorizados, 3 repeticiones, intervalos bootstrap |
| Datasets no disponibles offline (red deshabilitada aquí) | Fallo logístico | Preparar caché de WikiText-2/LAMBADA/C4 junto con los artefactos |

## 11. Verificado vs supuesto (separación explícita)
**Verificado en este entorno**: repo solo con task.json ("design-only; repositories and compute are not required"); sin torch/transformers; sin GPU accesible (nvidia-smi sin driver); 224 CPUs; red off; los números de la sección 8 y el presupuesto de la 9 son cálculos analíticos CPU ejecutados aquí.
**Supuestos (a reconciliar)**: detalles de QuaRot (R1/R2 fusionadas, Hadamard online solo en ciertas entradas, esquema exacto de KV4, kernels INT8-emulados); especificaciones de A100 usadas (2.04 TB/s, 312 TFLOPS); overhead de empaquetado INT4 15–25%; uso de checkpoints base LLaMA-2; parámetros del protocolo (512×2048 de calibración, grupo 128).
**Requisitos del brief (fijos, no supuestos)**: alcance 7B/13B 1 GPU, 70B fuera; prefill y decode separados + end-to-end; ambos regímenes de batch; los 6 baselines/condiciones; WikiText-2+LAMBADA mínimos y cero-shot amplio opcional; entregable solo-diseño sin ejecutar ni citar cifras del paper como medidas.

【最终交付：完整实验设计（设计文档 + 解析推演，无任何实测数字）】
交付物已落盘：/workspace/DESIGN.md（主文档）、/workspace/skeletons/{run_prefill_decode.py, run_quality_eval.py}（标注"未运行"的脚本骨架）、/workspace/skeletons/config/experiment_config.yaml（预注册配置与判读阈值）、/workspace/skeletons/analytical_estimate{,_batch}.py（纯算术 roofline 估算器，仅标准库，已在 CPU 上运行生成表内数字——属算术运算而非模型实验）。六项裁定全部固化：

1) 条件与因子：主集合 LLaMa-2-7B/13B @ 单卡 A100-80GB；70B 仅在假设 8×A100-80GB 下作条件性次要条件，不入主结论。精度条件=①同代码路径 FP16 基线 ②QuaRot W4A4KV4；KV4-only 消融与 SmoothQuant/OmniQuant 对照均为可选。网格：batch=1（主）+ {4,8}（次要，检验 H5 衰减趋势）；输入 {512,1024,2048}；输出固定 128。

2) 加速比定义（关键裁定）：主加速比 = 同一定制 CUDA 代码路径内 QuaRot-4bit/FP16 自配对（论文口径）。跨实现比较（HF transformers FP16 为分母）单列小节，仅说明其混入实现效率差异，不进主结论。

3) 指标：主=（预填充 tokens/s 与时延、decode TPOT 与 tokens/s、端到端时延、峰值显存含权重/KV/激活分解）；必要护栏=WikiText-2 PPL 增量 + PiQA/WinoGrande 准确率增量。

4) 协议与统计（预注册）：锁定内核库 commit/CUDA 版本/锁频/旋转种子（seed 0 与 1 稳健性）；每单元格 warmup 3 + 正式 10，全部原始值入库；汇报中位数+IQR，加速比 95% CI 用 bootstrap。判读标准（先于数据固定）：CI 下界>1.1 判显著增益；[0.95,1.1] 无实质差异；上界<0.95 显著回退。护栏：PPL 增量≤+0.25 且平均准确率变化≥−1.0 pt。

5) 解析式可行性推演（roofline/内存流量，[估算，非实测]）：decode 每步 T≈max(权重字节/BW, b×flops/算力)+KV字节/BW+Hadamard 在线变换额外流量/BW；QuaRot 有效位宽 4.25 bit（含 g=128 fp16 scale）；参数[假设]：有效 BW 1.55 TB/s、FP16 有效 187 TFLOPS、INT4 有效 400 TOPS。结果[估算]：7B decode FP16 115→108 t/s（S=512→2048）vs Q4 432→407 t/s，上界≈3.76x（权重主导、几乎不随 S 变）；7B prefill 14.2 vs 30.3 kt/s，≈2.14x（compute-bound）；13B 同比例（59→57 vs 223→213 t/s）。batch 敏感性[估算]：理论上界 crossover≈121 token，roofline 在 b≤8 预测衰减<1%（3.76→≈3.75x），但真实 GEMV→GEMM 效率差会使衰减远早出现——正是 b∈{4,8} 次要条件要检验的 H5。显存[估算]：权重+KV 16→4.25 bit ⇒ ~3.76x，计入 FP16 例外层后整体 ~3.0–3.5x。

6) 先验对照表：论文口径（arXiv:2404.00456 转引）70B ≤2.4x prefill / ≤3.1x decode / ~3.5x 内存 vs 本设计估算上界 2.14x（prefill，略低于论文 70B 多卡值，量级一致）/ 3.76x（decode 上界高于实测，符合"上界"预期，差值即内核融合不完全+量化/旋转开销，方向可解释）。7B 论文值（约 1.7x/2.6x）标注为待复核转引。

7) 局限与可行性结论（单列）：本环境无 GPU（nvidia-smi 失败）、网络禁用（pip 失败）、site-packages 为空、全盘无权重/仓库/数据集、/workspace 仅剩 ~14 GB——物理上无法执行端到端 4-bit 推理；执行本设计至少需 1×A100-80GB + CUDA 工具链 + QuaRot 官方实现 + 权重与数据集。

【假设（单列，非任务硬性要求）】有效带宽/算力比例常数如上；分组量化 g=128/fp16 scale；lm_head 与 embedding 保 FP16（执行前以 QuaRot 官方实现实际配置核对）；decode 平均上下文≈S+输出/2；论文转引数字未复核原文 PDF。
【未定项（单列）】70B 与可选消融/扩展是否最终启用；PiQA/WinoGrande few-shot 数（建议沿用论文 harness 默认）。
【边界声明（单列）】本交付为设计而非实测；全部数值已逐处标注 [论文口径]/[估算]/[假设]，不含任何实测数字，不声称运行过实验。

payload.answer:
**1. Inspection findings (what exists vs. absent)**

Exists in /workspace: only `task.json` (the task spec itself; it explicitly states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"). No QuaRot code, no LLaMA-2 weights or tokenizer, no eval scripts, no datasets, no prior notes.

Runtime constraints confirmed empirically:
- No GPU: `nvidia-smi` fails ("couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver"); environment declares gpu_enabled=false.
- No network: DNS resolution fails for pypi.org (consistent with network=disabled).
- CPU-only: 224 CPU cores, ~2 TB RAM, but Python 3.14.4 with no project dependencies (torch not installed, and pip install impossible without network). Note Python 3.14 is far newer than the 3.8–3.10 toolchain QuaRot's official repo (PyTorch ~2.1, CUTLASS kernels, Triton) requires — even with network, porting would be nontrivial.

Conclusion: this is unambiguously a **design-only deliverable**. The design will specify an experiment feasible on a standard GPU-class host, not on this machine.

**2. High-level approach skeleton**

*a) Models.* LLaMA-2 7B, 13B, 70B (HF checkpoints; LLaMA-2's published QuaRot results cover these). 7B primary for full sweep; 13B for trend confirmation; 70B for one representative config per phase to test scaling of the effect (70B W4A4 is what actually fits a single 80GB GPU in 4-bit).

*b) Quantization configurations.*
- BF16 baseline (HuggingFace / non-quantized reference).
- QuaRot full W4A4 end-to-end (all linear layers 4-bit weights + 4-bit activations, Hadamard rotations: online Hadamard on activations, fused Hadamard into weights, including the down-proj online Hadamard trick).
- Ablations isolating QuaRot components: (i) W4A16 (weight-only 4-bit, same rotation) — separates weight-quant vs activation-quant cost/benefit; (ii) Hadamard-averaging vs Hadamard-multiplication for the V/O-proj + residual handling (paper's "Ave" vs "Mul/Hadamard" variant — the paper recommends Ave for speed; measure both); (iii) skip-rotation W4A4 (RTN-style) to attribute quality deltas to the rotation vs to bit-width alone.
- Optional context: a strong baseline competitor (e.g., SmoothQuant/OmniQuant W8A8 or weight-only GPTQ W4) only if researcher wants external comparison; otherwise keep scope to QuaRot vs BF16.

*c) Phase separation (the core of the question).*
- **Prefill**: single forward pass on prompt-only inputs, measured via CUDA-event timing, excluding model load and quantization/rotation application (those are reported separately as one-time offline/one-time-online costs: rotation-fusion time, weight-quant time, calibration time). Sweep prompt lengths {128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} at batch size 1 and a few batch-8 points (prefill is compute-bound; 4-bit GEMM speedup depends on whether the CUTLASS kernels give compute or only memory-bound gains).
- **Decode**: step-wise generation, measuring time-per-output-token (TPOT) and tokens/s with fused-quantization fused-GEMM kernel path, output lengths {32, 128, 512}, batch sizes {1, 8, 32, 64} (decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; this is where W4A4 should shine). Use a fixed prompt+generate harness (e.g., model.generate with static prompt batches) and measure steady-state (discard warmup tokens).
- Report prefill throughput (tokens/s processed) and decode throughput (tokens/s generated) separately; never a blended e2e number alone.

*d) Quality metrics.* Perplexity on WikiText2 (seq len 2048, standard non-overlapping evaluation) and C4; zero-shot accuracy (AI2 Benchmark lm-eval suite: PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-e, WinoGrande, LAMBADA); optionally LongBench/AIME-free subset to show 4K-context behavior. Quality gates: report perplexity degradation vs BF16 and task-accuracy deltas.

*e) Performance metrics.* Latency (prefill latency per sequence, per-decode-step latency), throughput (prefill tokens/s, decode tokens/s at each batch size), peak GPU memory (model weights + activations + KV cache; note KV cache kept BF16/FP16 — also track memory reduction attributable to weights/activations vs KV), and one-time overheads (rotation fusion, quantization, calibration).

*f) Essential controls.* BF16 same-harness baseline (identical prompt batching, same kernel library where possible); W4A16 to attribute activation-quant effects; no-rotation W4A4 to attribute rotation effects; identical seeds/calibration set across configs; kernel-overhead sanity check (microbenchmark the 4-bit GEMM vs BF16 GEMM at the batch/shape grid actually used, since end-to-end speedups can vanish at large batch where BF16 tensor cores saturate); warmup + median-of-N timing, locked clocks where possible; same software stack version pinned for all runs; a fused-GEMM vs separate-kernel decode path toggle to test whether QuaRot's fused quantization is the deciding factor at large batch (the paper's known large-batch regression regime).

**3. Assumptions / uncertainties (design-only caveats)**
- Deliverable is a written design; nothing executed here (no GPU, no weights, no deps, no network — verified above). No results are claimed.
- Assumed feasibility hardware: single NVIDIA A100-80GB per run for 7B/13B; 70B W4A4 on one A100 (weights ~35GB + KV/activations), BF16 70B on 4×A100 with tensor parallel — feasibility section will state this hardware class explicitly.
- Assume QuaRot official repo's CUTLASS 4-bit kernels + their fused quantization kernel; assume KV cache remains BF16 (QuaRot quantizes linear layers, not KV).
- Assume standard paper setup: C4-based calibration (128×2048 samples), Hadamard rotations, 1/2 group size 128 for weight quant (per QuaRot), WikiText2 + C4 perplexity, lm-eval zero-shot suite.
- Assume batch-1 and batch>1 both matter (the key open question is where 4-bit helps vs hurts at larger batch; the design covers the crossover rather than assuming a direction).
- Uncertainty: exact kernel availability/build on the assumed CUDA/toolchain; if repo kernels won't build, fallback is a simulated-quantization path with fake-quant for quality and kernel microbenchmarks for performance, with the limitation stated.
- Uncertainty: whether LLaMA-2 access-gated weights are obtainable in the target execution environment (HF license gate); fallback: use already-downloaded copies if the executor has them.

The approach is approved. Environment findings are sufficient to justify a design-only deliverable, and the phase-separation logic (compute-bound prefill vs bandwidth-bound decode, with an explicitly measured crossover rather than an assumed direction) is the right way to answer the question. Please now produce the full experiment design. Before you write it, I am resolving four open choices from your list, and adding three structural requirements.

Resolutions of your open questions (these are my preferences, not source-verified requirements — flag any that conflict with what the source supports):
1. External baselines: include exactly one — weight-only W4 (GPTQ-style, W4A16) — because it is the most informative contrast for attributing prefill/decode cost specifically to activation quantization and the online Hadamard. Drop SmoothQuant/OmniQuant W8A8 to keep scope tight; mention them only as untested alternatives in limitations.
2. Keep 70B, but scope it as a scaling check only: one representative W4A4 config per phase, and treat BF16 70B as a memory/serving-feasibility reference with the tensor-parallel communication caveat stated inline rather than as a like-for-like speed baseline. Make explicit that cross-hardware or cross-parallelism comparisons are not speed claims.
3. Use Ave as the primary V/O-proj + residual handling and Mul/Hadamard as an ablation, as you proposed — and state it as a design choice with the reason (fewer online ops in the decode path), not as a fact about what the source mandates.
4. Keep the fallback path (fake-quant for quality, GEMM microbenchmarks for performance if the kernels will not build), but make clear it changes what the performance numbers can mean: fake-quant gives no speedup evidence, so the design must say which conclusions are lost under that fallback rather than reporting them anyway.

Structural requirements for the deliverable:
- State a per-cell experiment matrix (config x model size x phase x sequence length x batch size) with an estimated run count, so the feasibility section can be critiqued against the assumed A100-80GB budget. Identify which cells are load-bearing for the question and which are optional.
- Specify how you avoid conflating one-time costs (calibration, rotation fusion, weight quantization) with steady-state serving cost, and how the "end-to-end" framing in the question is honored: I want a stated convention for how one-time overheads are reported (amortized over N tokens at a given prompt/output mix, plus reported unamortized), since "end-to-end effect" is ambiguous otherwise.
- For quality, define the decision threshold or reporting convention for "acceptable degradation" (e.g., report deltas with a stated per-task noise floor and a repeated-seed or repeated-eval variance estimate), so the design yields an interpretable conclusion rather than a table of deltas.

Also be explicit wherever a number is an assumption (group size, calibration set size, sequence-length and batch grids) versus something read from the source, since I cannot verify source details you have not quoted. No results should be claimed or implied.

The proposed skeleton covers the question's two phases separately, includes the attributive controls I would require (W4A16, no-rotation W4A4, fused-vs-separate kernel toggle, GEMM microbenchmark sanity check), and lists assumptions and uncertainties explicitly. Four scope choices were left to me; approving now with those resolved and structural requirements added avoids unnecessary rework.

# Experiment Design: Effect of QuaRot End-to-End 4-bit Quantization on Prefill and Decoding Performance of LLaMA-2

**Status: design-only.** Nothing here was executed or observed on GPU; no performance or quality outcomes are claimed or implied. The current workspace has no QuaRot code, no LLaMA-2 weights, no GPU, and no network (verified in the scoping pass), so this document is the deliverable.

**Provenance tags used throughout:** `[A]` = assumption/design choice (not source-verified — I could not read the QuaRot paper or repo from this environment); `[S?]` = recollection of the QuaRot paper's setup that should be source-verified before execution. No number in this design is quoted from the source.

---

## 1. Question and answer structure

Primary question: for LLaMA-2, how does QuaRot's W4A4 end-to-end quantization change (a) prefill (prompt processing) and (b) decode (token generation) performance, relative to BF16 and to weight-only W4, and with what quality cost?

The design answers it in three parts, kept separable:
1. **Quality effect** — is W4A4 quality acceptable, and how much of any degradation is attributable to activation quantization vs to the absence of rotation?
2. **Performance effect, phase-separated** — prefill (compute-bound) and decode (bandwidth-bound) are measured as distinct workloads; the batch size at which 4-bit stops winning is **measured, not assumed**.
3. **One-time cost accounting** — calibration, rotation fusion, weight quantization, with a stated amortization convention (§6) so "end-to-end effect" is unambiguous.

## 2. Configurations

| ID | Config | Role |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | BF16 (no quantization) | Baseline |
| C1 | QuaRot W4A4, **Ave** V/O-proj + residual handling | Primary treatment. Choice of Ave as primary is a design choice (fewer online Hadamard ops in the decode path), not a source mandate `[A]` |
| C2 | QuaRot W4A4, **Mul/Hadamard** variant | Ablation: cost of extra online rotation ops |
| C3 | W4A4, **no rotation** (RTN weights + direct activation quant) | Ablation: attributes quality/perf deltas to the rotation itself |
| C4 | **GPTQ-style W4A16** (weight-only 4-bit) | Single external baseline (researcher-approved): isolates the cost/benefit of *activation* quantization + online Hadamard by differing from C1 in exactly that dimension |

SmoothQuant/OmniQuant W8A8 are excluded and appear only in Limitations as untested alternatives.
Assumed quantization details, all `[S?]`: weights group-128 asymmetric INT4; activations per-token INT4; Hadamard rotations (random Hadamard, fused into weights where possible; online Hadamard before down_proj); KV cache left in BF16 (QuaRot quantizes linear layers, not the KV cache) `[A]`. Calibration: 128 samples × 2048 tokens from C4 `[S?]`; one fixed calibration set and seed shared across all quantized configs.

## 3. Models and hardware (feasibility assumption `[A]`)

- **LLaMA-2-7B** — primary; full matrix.
- **LLaMA-2-13B** — trend confirmation; reduced grid.
- **LLaMA-2-70B** — scaling check only: C1, one representative cell per phase. BF16 70B (4×A100 tensor-parallel) is a **memory/serving-feasibility reference only**; its timings carry an inline tensor-parallel communication caveat and are **not** like-for-like speed comparisons. No cross-hardware or cross-parallelism speed claim is made anywhere.
- Assumed hardware: 1× A100-80GB for all 7B/13B work and 70B W4A4 (weights ≈35 GB `[A]`); 4× A100-80GB only for BF16-70B feasibility check.

## 4. Phase-separated performance protocol

**Timing method (all cells) `[A]`:** CUDA-event timing; ≥5 warmup iterations discarded; median over 15 repeats with per-repeat spread reported; clocks locked if permitted; identical harness for C0/C1/C2/C3 except the quantization kernel path. Model load, weight quantization, rotation fusion, calibration, and JIT/compile time are **excluded** from steady-state numbers and reported separately (§6).

**Prefill (compute-bound):** prompt-only forward pass, generation disabled.
- Grid: prompt lengths {128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096}; batch {1, 8} on 7B; padding with attention masks; batched prefill throughput reported both per-sequence and per-batch.
- Metrics: prefill latency per batch; prefill tokens/s; peak activation memory.

**Decode (bandwidth-bound):** fixed prompts, generate N new tokens, per-step latency in steady state (first 8 tokens discarded).
- Grid: batch {1, 8, 32, 64}; context length {512, 4096} (prompt sized to hit each context); output length 128 `[A]`.
- Metrics: time-per-output-token (TPOT), decode tokens/s, peak memory (weights + activations + BF16 KV cache reported as separate components where the profiler allows).
- Both QuaRot's **fused** (quantization fused into the GEMM epilogue/prologue) and unfused kernel paths are timed at each decode cell, since the fused path is where large-batch behavior is decided `[S?]`.

**Crossover measurement:** prefill and decode each get a speedup-vs-batch curve (4-bit over BF16, and 4-bit over GPTQ). The batch at which the curve crosses 1.0× is the reported deliverable; the design deliberately does not presuppose its direction or location.

**Kernel microbenchmark (supporting evidence):** 4-bit GEMM vs BF16 GEMM vs W4A16 GEMM over LLaMA-7B layer shapes × M ∈ {1, 8, 32, 64, 256, 1024, 4096} `[A]` (~168 short runs, minutes each). This contextualizes any end-to-end regression as kernel-shape-bound rather than method-bound.

**One-time overhead cells:** calibration time, rotation-fusion time, weight-quantization time, kernel warm-up — measured once per config × model (~15 cheap measurement points).

## 5. Quality protocol

- **Perplexity:** WikiText2 and C4, non-overlapping 2048-token evaluation `[S?]`, all of C0–C4 on 7B and 13B; 70B limited to {C0, C1, C4} × WikiText2 (feasibility, `[A]`).
- **Zero-shot:** lm-eval-harness suite {PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-easy, WinoGrande, LAMBADA} on 7B for {C0, C1, C4} primary; C2/C3 optional extension.
- **Variance/noise floor `[A]`:** 3 seeds per quantized config (calibration shuffling and rotation-matrix RNG are the stochastic stages) and 2 repeated eval runs on C0. Noise floor σ_noise = max(seed spread, rerun spread) per metric.
- **Interpretability convention `[A]` (the "acceptable degradation" rule):** every delta is reported with σ_noise and classified — *no measurable degradation* if |Δ| ≤ 2·σ_noise; *within-tolerance* if 2·σ_noise < |Δ| ≤ assumed acceptance gate (design gate: +0.5 ppl WikiText2 absolute and −1.0 pt mean-suite accuracy zero-shot, stated up front as a conventional serving tolerance, not a source value); *degraded* beyond the gate. The conclusion section must state the classification per config, not just raw deltas.

## 6. One-time costs and the "end-to-end" convention

Ambiguity resolution: "end-to-end" in the question is read as *all linear layers quantized* (the QuaRot method property), while the *end-to-end effect on serving* is reported with this convention `[A]`:
1. **Unamortized:** each one-time overhead reported raw (seconds, per model, per config).
2. **Amortized:** over a declared serving workload mix — prompt 512 / output 128 tokens — at two horizons: 10⁴ and 10⁶ served tokens, giving an "effective per-token cost including preparation" as a supplement.
3. **Primary tables use steady-state numbers**; amortized figures appear in a clearly labeled supplementary table. No conclusion flips between the two views without being called out.

## 7. Per-cell experiment matrix and run-count

A *cell* = config × model × phase × seq × batch, each cell = one median-of-15 measurement block.

**7B (primary), C0/C1/C4 primary set:**
- Prefill: 3 configs × 2 batches × 5 seq = **30**
- Decode: 3 configs × 4 batches × 2 contexts = **24**
- C2 ablation (prefill + decode, same grids): 10 + 8 = **18 (optional)**
- C3 ablation (quality-focused; performance spot-check at batch 1, seq 2048, both phases): **2**
- 7B subtotal: 56 primary + 18 optional

**13B (trend confirmation, reduced grid) `[A]`:**
- Prefill: 3 × batch {1} × seq {512, 2048, 4096} = **9**
- Decode: 3 × batch {1, 32} × context {512} = **6**
- 13B subtotal: 15

**70B (scaling check):**
- C1 speed: prefill {512, 4096}×batch1 + decode batch {1, 32} = **4**
- C0 BF16-TP4 feasibility/memory only: **2** (flagged non-comparable for speed)
- 70B subtotal: 6

**Quality:** ppl 10 (models×corpora×5 configs) + 70B ppl 3 + zero-shot 15 primary (+10 optional for C2/C3) = **28 primary + 10 optional**
**Microbenchmarks:** ~168 short GEMM runs. **Overhead cells:** ~15.

**Estimated totals `[A]`:** ~105 primary measurement cells + ~38 optional; rough budget ≈ 80–140 A100-hours for 7B/13B (quality dominates), + ~20–40 hours for 70B — critique the feasibility section against this.

**Load-bearing cells (answer the question directly):** 7B prefill crossover curves (batch 1→8), 7B decode crossover curves (batch 1→64), quality deltas C1-vs-C0 with noise floors, attribution set {C0, C1, C3, C4}, one-time overhead accounting. **Optional:** C2 performance cells, 13B beyond batch-1, 70B beyond the 6 listed cells, C2/C3 zero-shot, batch-8 prefill on 13B.

## 8. Fallback semantics (kernels will not build)

If the QuaRot CUTLASS/fused kernels cannot be built on the executor's toolchain:
- **Survives under fallback:** all quality conclusions (fake-quant / simulated-quantization reproduces the numeric method; C1–C4 quality comparisons remain valid, modulo noting RTN-vs-GPTQ fine-grained sensitivity), one-time overhead timings for calibration/fusion, and GEMM microbenchmark data.
- **Lost under fallback (must be explicitly retracted, not reported anyway):** all end-to-end prefill/decode speedup claims, both crossover batch locations, and the fused-vs-unfused comparison. Microbenchmark + roofline reasoning may be included as *indicative mechanism analysis only*, labeled as insufficient for speed claims. The design's headline question would then be answerable only for quality, with the performance half marked "not established under fallback."

## 9. Assumptions vs source-read — consolidated

**Nothing in this design is quoted from the source** (no repository, paper, or network access in this environment). Treated as assumptions requiring pre-execution source verification `[S?]`: group size 128 for weight quantization; per-token activation quantization; calibration = 128 C4 samples × 2048 tokens; Hadamard placement (fusion into weights, online Hadamard before down_proj, Ave vs Mul variants); fused quantization GEMM kernels; KV cache kept BF16; 2048-token non-overlapping perplexity evaluation. Pure design choices `[A]`: model set and grids; Ave-as-primary; batch/context/output grids; noise-floor convention and acceptance gates; amortization mix and horizons; timing protocol; the 70B feasibility-only framing; GPTQ as the single external baseline (researcher preference).

## 10. Limitations

Untested alternatives (W8A8 SmoothQuant/OmniQuant, FP8) noted but excluded; single-hardware-class result; LLaMA-2-only; tensor-parallel caveat on BF16-70B; kernel-availability contingency (§8) may restrict the answer to the quality half; padding effects on batched prefill throughput acknowledged via reporting both padded and effective token counts.

Section 4 says both the fused and unfused decode paths are timed at each decode cell, but the Section 7 decode counts (24 on 7B, 6 on 13B) appear to assume one path per cell. # Revised sections only — all other sections of the approved design are unchanged (design-only; no results claimed or implied)

## Rev. 1 — Kernel-path toggle folded into the matrix arithmetic

**§4 Decode (revised sentence):** All decode cells use the **fused** quantization-GEMM path by default. The **unfused** path is restricted to a budgeted subset: **C1 only, on 7B, batch {32, 64} × context {512, 4096} = 4 added cells.** What is lost by this restriction, stated explicitly: (a) the fused-vs-unfused delta for C4-analogous or C2/C3 paths is unmeasured — but those configs either don't use the QuaRot fused kernel (C4) or are ablations where the path-interaction question is secondary (C2/C3); (b) the unfused crossover batch is localized only to the ±1 grid step around the fused crossover (batches 32–64), not resolved across the full batch sweep. If the fused decode shows no regression anywhere in the sweep, item (b) loss is immaterial; if it regresses, the unfused subset is the diagnostic, which is why batch {32, 64} was chosen.

**§4 Prefill (revised, new sentence):** The fused/unfused distinction is **declared out of scope for prefill**. Rationale: prefill runs whole-matrix activation quantization that is already compute-dominated, and the fusion question is specific to the per-step decode kernel; the crossover sweep itself (batch {1,8}) is path-agnostic evidence. Concession noted in Limitations: any prefill regression attributable specifically to kernel fusion structure would not be separable from general 4-bit GEMM slowness.

**§7 Decode counts restated explicitly:**
- 7B decode primary: configs(3) × batch(4) × context(2) × {fused only} = **24**, **plus 4 unfused-subset cells (C1, batch {32,64} × context {512,4096}) = 28**.
- 7B decode optional (C2): 8 cells, fused path only.
- 13B decode: **6**, fused only; unfused out of scope for 13B.
- 70B decode: 2, fused only.
- Prefill counts unchanged (no path multiplier).

**§7 revised totals:** 7B primary = 30 prefill + 28 decode + 2 (C3 spot-check) = **60**, plus 9 harness-parity cells (Rev. 2) = **69**; optional 18. 13B = 15; 70B = 6; quality primary 28 (+10 optional). **New grand total ≈ 118 primary cells + 28 optional** (was ~105), plus the same ~168 microbenchmark runs and ~15 overhead measurement points. Rough GPU-hour budget increases by ~5–10 A100-hours → ≈ 85–150 hours for 7B/13B + ~20–40 for 70B `[A]`, unchanged in character.

## Rev. 2 — Harness-parity control as first-class cells (§7 additions; §10 uncertainty retained but now backed by cells)

**Primary denominator for speedup curves:** C1/C2/C3 speedups are divided by **BF16 on the QuaRot repo's unquantized path** (same harness as the treatments, isolating quantization rather than harness differences). C4 (GPTQ) ratios use BF16 on the HF harness (its native comparison harness); C4 ratios are therefore always reported harness-labeled and are never mixed into the C1 crossover curves.

**Added cells (7B, C0 on both harnesses, small parity grid):** prefill seq {512, 2048, 4096} × batch {1, 8} = 6, plus decode batch {1, 32, 64} × context {512} = 3 → 9 cells per harness. The HF side (9 runs) is already inside the existing C0 primary cells, so the **added count is +9** (QuaRot-harness C0), included in the §7 totals above.

**Decision rule (stated in the design, applied at analysis time):** if, at any parity cell, the two BF16 harness medians disagree by more than max(3% `[A]`, 2× within-cell repeat spread), then **all 7B speedup curves are reported as ratios against both BF16 harnesses** — no picking one after seeing treatment results; the rule is fixed pre-run and the classification of each parity cell is reported. If all cells agree within threshold, the single QuaRot-harness denominator is used and the parity check is reported as passing.

## Rev. 3 — New §7b: Attribution decision table (pattern → licensed claim wording)

All speed claims below are relative to the §7 Rev. 2 denominator and confined to the measured grids (batch ≤ 8 prefill, ≤ 64 decode; seq ≤ 4096); no extrapolation beyond the grid is licensed in any row. Quality classifications use the §5 noise-floor rule.

| Observed pattern | Licensed conclusion wording |
|---|---|
| C1−C0 quality within tolerance; decode speedup at batch 1; decode crossover at batch B* | "W4A4 improves decode throughput for batch ≤ B* on this hardware/kernel stack, with quality within the stated tolerance; beyond B* it is at parity or regresses (measured range)." |
| Prefill crossover lands below batch 8 (only batch-8 cells regress) | "W4A4 prefill wins at batch 1 (and short prompts) and regresses at batch 8 **within the measured grid**; the crossover lies in (1, 8) — location not resolved." Do not claim the regression extends beyond batch 8 or beyond 4096 tokens; a prefill regression is stated only if it exceeds 2× repeat spread (2×σ) at both batch-8 sequence points, else the prefill effect is classified as **not detected** and claimed as "within-noise across the measured grid." |
| C1−C3 quality delta significant, C1−C4 decode delta ≈ 0 (within noise) | "The quality benefit at W4A4 is attributable to the rotation (C3 collapses without it); the decode speed benefit is attributable to memory-footprint reduction, shared with weight-only W4 — activation quantization and the online Hadamard add quality capability at no measured decode-speed advantage." |
| C1−C3 quality delta within noise | "No measurable quality contribution from the rotation at W4A4 on this model set; W4A4 quality ≈ weight-only 4-bit quality." (This would be a surprising result and triggers the §8/source-verification check before being published, but the licensed wording is stated in advance.) |
| C1−C0 decode within noise at every batch | "No measurable decode benefit for W4A4 on this kernel stack" — claim permitted only after the §4 GEMM microbenchmarks classify it as kernel-bound vs method-bound; mechanism attribution stays conditional on the microbenchmarks. |
| C1−C0 prefill regresses at batch 1 (both short and long seq, beyond 2×σ) | "4-bit GEMMs are slower for large-M compute-bound shapes on this stack; QuaRot's value is confined to the decode regime (measured)." |
| Conflict rule: speed benefit exists but C1−C0 quality classified *degraded* (beyond acceptance gates) | Only the conditional wording is licensed: "the speed benefit is available at the cost of quality beyond the stated tolerance and is not claimable as an acceptable serving configuration under the §5 gates." Never "acceptable." |
| C1−C0 quality *degraded* and decode within noise | "No benefit observed and measurable quality cost" — a negative result stated directly; no softening language. |
| Multiple cells of the same config conflict with 13B trend | 7B-only claim wording with the model qualifier "for LLaMA-2-7B"; the 13B disagreement is reported, not averaged away. |

## Confirmation line (13B/70B independence from batch-8 prefill reclassification)

Confirmed: the 13B prefill grid is batch {1} only and the 70B prefill cells are batch {1} only, so neither model depends on the batch-8 prefill points, and the load-bearing/optional split in §7 is unchanged by Rev. 1.

payload.message:
All three requested revisions are satisfied, and they were the last items I had open. Closing this out.

1. Kernel-path toggle: the unfused path is now budgeted explicitly (C1, 7B, batch {32,64} x context {512,4096} = +4 cells) rather than multiplied across every decode cell, the decode arithmetic is restated as config x batch x context x {fused} plus the named unfused subset, and the two stated losses from restricting it are honest — in particular the admission that the unfused crossover is localized only around batches 32–64. The prefill fused/unfused distinction being declared out of scope with a stated rationale (whole-matrix, compute-dominated activation quantization) plus the corresponding Limitations concession (a prefill regression caused by fusion structure would not be separable from general 4-bit GEMM slowness) is an acceptable scope decision, not a gap.

2. Harness parity: this is now a first-class control with a fixed pre-run denominator assignment (C1/C2/C3 against BF16 on the QuaRot repo's unquantized path; C4 against BF16 on the HF harness, always harness-labeled and never folded into the C1 crossover curves), 9 concrete added cells, and a disagreement rule fixed in advance (dual-ratio reporting rather than post-hoc denominator selection). That closes the confound I flagged, and fixing the rule before seeing treatment results is the right call.

3. Attribution decision table: the pattern-to-wording mapping does what I asked — it licenses claim wording per outcome pattern, including the awkward ones. I specifically note the row that keeps the crossover claim inside the measured grid when the prefill crossover lands below batch 8 (regression at batch 8 only, interval (1,8) unresolved, "not detected" classification if the delta is under 2x repeat spread), the row requiring microbenchmark-based mechanism attribution before a null decode result can be called kernel-bound, and the conflict rule that forbids the word "acceptable" when quality exceeds the gates. - Paper ka weight-only recipe (mujhe yaad hai): **per-group asymmetric quantization, group size 128**, per-group scale + zero-point; embeddings / lm_head / norm layers aam taur par excluded.
- **W bits ∈ {4, 3, 2}**; baselines: **RTN** (koi calibration data nahin, simple rounding/clipping) aur **GPTQ** (per-layer, Hessian-approximation `H = 2XXᵀ` par based error-minimizing rounding, calibration data use karta hai).

- Paper-level eval: LLaMA-2/LLaMA-3 families (7B/8B/13B/70B), WikiText-2 + C4 perplexity (seq len 2048), zero-shot tasks (PIQA, ARC-e/c, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, LAMBADA).

## 2) PROPOSED APPROACH (sirf outline — vistaar approval ke baad)

**Tier 0 — mechanism probe (isi environment mein chalane-yogya, zero deps, pure stdlib):**
Synthetic outlier-heavy matrices + fast Walsh–Hadamard + per-group uniform quantization ka MSE, bits ∈ {4,3,2} par. Ye *mechanism* aur *metric/ablation logic* ko validate karta hai; real LLM ke baare mein kuch claim nahin karta. (Maine feasibility confirm kar li — numbers §Evidence mein.)

**Tier 1 — main experiment (design-only; GPU+deps+models maan lena hoga):**
- **Models (proposed choice):** LLaMA-2 7B + 13B primary (paper-comparability), LLaMA-3 8B secondary (jahan outliers zyanaatar), LLaMA-2 70B optional/stretch. TinyLlama-1.1B jaisa ek chhota "smoke-test" model jiska full 4×3 grid sasta padhe.
- **Precision points:** W ∈ {4, 3, 2} + FP16/BF16 reference. **Arms (4×3 grid):** RTN, GPTQ, RTN+Hadamard, GPTQ+Hadamard.
- **Primary metrics:** WikiText-2 aur C4 perplexity (seq len 2048, sliding-window eval); zero-shot accuracy battery (PIQA, ARC-e, ARC-c, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, LAMBADA) + unka average.
- **Mechanism metrics (causal chain ke liye zaroori):** per-layer weight-quant MSE; dynamic-range ratio `max|w|/σ` before/after rotation; per-layer ΔPPL (ek layer block ko quant karke); rotation-invariance bit-check.
- **Controls/ablations (proposed):** (a) Hadamard **weights-only** vs **weights+activations/KV** — weight-only claim ko alag karne ke liye, plus "folded-Had vs online-Had = identical FP16 ppl" equivalence control; (b) deterministic vs **randomized** Hadamard (random sign flip) → seed variance; (c) **group size** 128 vs 64 vs 32 (benefit kis par nirbhar hai); (d) layer-class leave-one-out ablation (attention vs MLP projections) — benefit kahan concentrated hai; (e) GPTQ ke Hessian damping/act-order same across rot/no-rot arms; (f) ≥3 seeds, mean ± std.
- **Pre-registered decision rule:** "QuaRot 2-bit ko stabilize karta hai" tabhi成立, jab GPTQ+Had W2 ka PPL FP16 se ek pre-declared factor (e.g., ≤2×) ke andar ho jabki GPTQ-W2 orders-of-magnitude kharab ho; aur benefit bits kam hone par **monotone badhe** (trend test), na ki ek single point par claim.

1. **Kuch bhi "chalaya" hua claim nahin karunga.** Aaj tak sirf environment inspection aur ek synthetic stdlib probe chala hai. Real-model perplexity/zero-shot par koi numeric claim meri taraf se nahin aayega; design ke numbers sirf *targets* hain.

Aap `setup_*` topics se inhe pin kar dein to design design-only-reproducible ho jaayega.
3. **Ye design is environment mein executable nahin hai** (no GPU, no deps, no network, no dataset). Feasibility ka argument external/paper-level compute par based hoga, is machine par nahin.
4. **Storage reality:** /workspace par sirf ~11.3 GB free — 70B (ya 13B bhi fp16 mein) yahin store nahin ho sakta; ek real run ko bade volume ya RAM-backed `/tmp` (~1 TB) ki zaroorat padegi, aur `/tmp` observation se pata chala ki calls ke beech reset hota hai → design ko artifacts /workspace ya persistent volume par rakhna chahiye (proposed requirement).
5. **Python 3.14** par us era ka pinned ML stack (torch/transformers versions) install ho payega, ye anishchit hai → reproduction risk, design mein version-flexibility rakhni padegi.
6. **Quantizer details ka sign tak badal sakta hai** — meri synthetic probe mein symmetric 2-bit quantizer par Hadamard ne MSE *badha* diya (ratio 5.2×), jabki asymmetric (zero-point) grid par wahi rotation 8–12× MSE *kam* kar deta hai. # FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Does QuaRot's Hadamard transformation improve/stabilize weight-only quantized LLMs at W2–W4?"

**Status: DESIGN ONLY.** No LLM experiment has been run. Every number below tagged `[SYN]` is a pure-Python *synthetic* matrix study I ran in this sandbox to sanity-check the mechanism and the metric implementation; it is **not** evidence about any language model.

---

## A. FIXED requirements vs PROPOSED choices

| Item | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Quantization scope | **Weight-only**: only linear-layer weights quantized; activations, KV cache and all norms stay FP16 in every primary arm | **FIXED (task)** |
| Precision points | **W ∈ {4, 3, 2} bits** | **FIXED (task)** |
| Baseline 1 | **RTN** — round-to-nearest, **no calibration data** | **FIXED (task)** |
| Baseline 2 | **GPTQ** — layer-wise error-minimizing rounding from a Hessian approximation H = (2/n)Σxxᵀ + damping | **FIXED (task)** |
| Deliverable | Experiment design; **no claim that an experiment was run** | **FIXED (task)** |
| Model family/sizes | LLaMA-2 7B, LLaMA-2 13B, LLaMA-3 8B (primary) + TinyLlama-1.1B (smoke) + LLaMA-2 70B (top-line only) | proposed |
| Group size (primary) | **g\* = 128** | proposed (to-confirm vs paper) |
| Grid type (primary) | per-group **asymmetric** uniform, scale + zero-point, groups along input dim, per output row | proposed (to-confirm) |
| Excluded tensors | embeddings, lm_head, RMSNorm/scale params, rotary params | proposed (to-confirm) |
| Hadamard variant | **randomized Hadamard** (random ±1 diagonal then Sylvester H), folded **offline** into weights; no online Hadamard in primary arms | proposed |
| GPTQ hyper-params | act-order on, percdamp 0.01, blocksize 128, calibration = C4, 128×2048 tokens | proposed |
| Eval harness | WikiText-2 + C4 PPL at seq len 2048; zero-shot PIQA/ARC-e/ARC-c/HellaSwag/WinoGrande/LAMBADA | proposed |
| Seeds | 3 random-sign seeds for the two "+Hadamard" arms; deterministic single run for RTN/GPTQ | proposed |
| Decision thresholds (§F) | ×3 stability, ×10 collapse, monotone-trend floor | proposed (pre-registered) |

Everything except the first five rows is a choice, tunable or replaceable, and is labeled as such throughout.

---

## B. Frozen primary configuration (design-level resolution of my biggest uncertainty)

My probe showed the *sign* of the Hadamard effect can flip with quantizer choice (symmetric 2-bit: rotation **worse** 3.3–5.2×; asymmetric 2-bit: rotation **better** ~12×). Therefore:

**Pre-registration rule.** All four arms × three bit-widths × all models use **one identical quantizer config C\***; primary conclusions come *only* from C\*. Grid type (sym vs asym) and group size {g\*, 64, 32} are demoted to a **formal mechanism ablation** (§D-A1/A2) whose results may explain, but never establish, the answer.

**C\* = {** per-group asymmetric min/max+zero-point uniform quantizer; groups contiguous along the input dimension; g\*=128; quantize q,k,v,o,gate,up,down of every block; exclude embed/lm_head/norms; rotation = randomized Hadamard of matching order folded offline (X W = (XH)(HᵀW)) with the inverse applied to the preceding linear/norm so the FP function is mathematically unchanged; RTN = plain nearest rounding on C\* grid (no clipping search); GPTQ = C\* grid + Hessian above, **identical** whether or not rotation is applied; FP16 reference run; identical eval split/seed for every arm. **}**

Why asymmetric is the primary: at 2 bits a symmetric grid has only 3 usable levels and wastes one on zero, so the outlier-clipping effect dominates and the rotation's contribution is confounded — exactly what `[SYN]` showed.

---

## C. Primary grid (arms)

Per model: **4 methods × 3 precisions = 12 arms + 1 FP16 reference**, with 3 sign-seeds on the two Had arms → 12 + (2 Had arms × 3 bits × 2 extra seeds) = **19 quantization artifacts per model**.

| | RTN (no calib) | GPTQ (Hessian) |
|---|---|---|
| **no rotation** | A1 · 4/3/2 | A2 · 4/3/2 |
| **+ randomized Hadamard (folded)** | A3 · 4/3/2 | A4 · 4/3/2 |

This 2×2 (rotation × compensation-method) × 3-bit design is what lets us answer *how* (interaction/mediation) and not just *whether*.

## D. Controls and ablations

**Correctness controls (gates — must pass before any result is read)**
- **C1 Equivalence gate (the one you asked for):** FP16 + folded-Hadamard vs FP16 original must give **identical PPL** (target: ΔPPL within FP numerical noise, e.g. <0.1%); and "online Hadamard" vs "offline folded" must agree bit-for-bit. This proves any later ΔPPL is a quantization effect, not a transformation artifact. `[SYN]` support: round-trip error 4.4e-16, norm ratio 1.000000000000; quantizer MSE monotone in bits (16b 9.5e-9 → 8b 6.0e-4 → 4b 1.8e-1); group-quant MSE exactly permutation-equivariant (311.5729 = 311.5729).
- **C2 Activation/KV control:** one extra arm per model, QuaRot-style W4+FP activations vs W4A4KV4. Kept *outside* the primary grid — the question is weight-only quality — its only role is to show that the weight-only claim does not secretly depend on the activation/KV rotations.

**Pre-registered negative controls (cheap outlier-mediator tests)**
- **N1 outlier-free condition (your suggestion, adopted):** repeat C\* pipeline on outlier-free weights. Prediction: ratio ∈ **[0.95, 1.05]** (no benefit). `[SYN]`: ratio 1.000 at outlier-frac 0, and 1.004–1.009 in the outlier-free matrix control. *If N1 is not null, the harness is buggy and no conclusion is drawn.*
- **N2 permutation control:** permute input channels only (same group layout). Prediction: exact no-op. `[SYN]` 1.00× at all bits → benefit must come from *mixing*, not reordering.
- **N3 diagonal-sign control:** random ±1 signs without Hadamard. Prediction: no benefit / slight harm. `[SYN]` 1.09–1.19× (worse).
- **N4 non-Hadamard orthogonal control:** dense random orthogonal rotation of the same order. `[SYN]` was intermediate (0.34× at 4b vs Had 0.17×) → "any rotation" is *not* equivalent to Hadamard; a flat-spectrum/Hadamard-specific claim requires this control.
- **N5 alternative-mechanism control (most important discriminator):** RTN + MSE-optimal clipping search, and per-channel (SmoothQuant-style) scaling, both unrotated. If these match GPTQ+Hadamard within CI, the effect must be attributed to **dynamic-range/outlier suppression in general**, not to Hadamard specifically.

**Mechanism ablations (explanatory only, 1 model — 7B — to bound cost)**
- **A1 group size** {128, 64, 32} × 4 arms × W{2,4}: `[SYN]` benefit shrinks monotonically (2b ratio 0.071 → 0.152 → 0.315 → 0.686 as g falls to 16) → prediction: QuaRot's advantage is largest at coarse groups and fades as fine-grained scaling already absorbs outliers.
- **A2 grid type** symmetric vs asymmetric at each bit (the sign-flip axis).
- **A3 rotation scope / dose-response:** rotate 0/25/50/75/100% of layers, plus leave-one-class-out (attention-only, MLP-only, gate/up-only, down-only). `[SYN]` dose curve 1.000/0.706/0.495/0.297/0.159 → near-log-linear accumulation to be compared against the real cumulative curve.
- **A4 randomized vs deterministic Hadamard** (separates outlier suppression from sign-randomization/aliasing effects).

## E. Metrics

**Primary (quality):** WikiText-2 PPL (decision metric) and C4 PPL, seq len 2048, identical windows across arms; reported as **PPL and ratio r = PPL/PPL_FP16**.
**Secondary (quality):** 6-task zero-shot accuracy + mean; **Δ from FP16 in points** and % accuracy retained.

**Mechanism metrics (what makes the "how" question answerable):**
- M1 per-tensor relative weight error ‖W−Ŵ‖²/‖W‖² (rotation is Frobenius-invariant, so it is directly comparable across arms; measured after un-rotation, i.e. in the *original* basis).
- M2 **outlier/dynamic-range mediators**: max|w|/σ, kurtosis, and the fraction of group MSE contributed by the top-1% weights, before vs after rotation.
- M3 **curvature-weighted layer error** ‖X(W−Ŵ)ᵀ‖²/‖XWᵀ‖² — GPTQ's *own* objective, tested under rotation (implemented and validated in `[SYN]`).
- M4 **curvature diagonal non-uniformity** max(diag H)/mean(diag H): `[SYN]` 34.5 → 1.19 after Hadamard. Design-level prediction: rotation *flattens the curvature spectrum*, so GPTQ's error-feedback has little left to exploit → **RTN+Had ≈ or > GPTQ+Had**. Testing this redundancy prediction is the sharpest part of the "how".
- M5 **per-block ΔPPL curves**: quantize only block i (and only ¼-depth spans) → where damage accumulates.
- M6 overhead sanity: folded rotation adds **zero** online FLOPs; verify measured latency of FP16-original vs FP16-rotated ≈ identical.

## F. Analysis plan + pre-registered decision rule

Operational definitions: **r = PPL(arm)/PPL_FP16** on WikiText-2. "Traditional method fails" ⇒ **r ≥ 5** at that bit (with zero-shot mean drop ≥ 10 points as corroboration); "collapse" ⇒ **r ≥ 100** or non-finite.

Statistics: paired bootstrap over WikiText-2 document windows (arms share the eval set → paired resampling, 10k replicates) for CI on Δ log-PPL; per-model results reported separately (models are replicates, not pooled CIs); Holm–Bonferroni over the 3 pre-declared primary hypotheses; everything else exploratory.

1. **Main effect + interaction.** Two-way 2×2 (Hadamard × compensation) per bit-width on Δlog-PPL. Report (i) Hadamard main effect per bit, (ii) the interaction: if Hadamard helps RTN more than GPTQ, the two mechanisms are redundant (see M4 prediction) — an answer to *how* it works, not just *that* it works.
2. **2-bit stability (headline claim).** "QuaRot stabilizes 2-bit weight-only" is supported **iff GPTQ+Hadamard at W2 has PPL ≤ 3× FP16 on both WikiText-2 and C4 AND zero-shot mean within 5 points of FP16**, while at least one traditional arm at W2 satisfies the "fails" definition (r ≥ 5).
3. **Monotone trend test.** Benefit B(b) = log r_no-Had(b) − log r_Had(b) over b ∈ {4,3,2}. Require B non-decreasing as bits shrink (Jonckheere–Terpstra / bootstrap-permutation, and Spearman ρ = 1.0) **and** B(2) ≥ 2·B(4) as a pre-declared effect floor. A headline of "helps more at lower precision" without monotonicity is not claimed.
4. **Falsification conditions (explicit).**
 - If **GPTQ+Hadamard also collapses at W2** (r > 10 or non-finite), the stabilization claim **fails**, *no matter how much better it is than GPTQ alone*. The honest report becomes "improves, does not stabilize".
 - If the equivalence gate C1 fails, all results are void (transformation bug).
 - If N5 (clipping/per-channel scaling) matches GPTQ+Hadamard, the claim is downgraded to "outlier/dynamic-range suppression helps", not "Hadamard specifically".
 - If N1's ratio is outside [0.95, 1.05], the harness is declared invalid.
5. **Secondary hypothesis to report either way:** redundancy of Hadamard with Hessian-based compensation (M4/A-curve + interaction sign), and the group-size fade-out (A1).

## G. Feasibility

**Cost model (arm-count × model-size × pass).** Per model: 19 quantization artifacts + 19 PPL evals + 19×6 zero-shot evals; GPTQ artifacts (12/model) dominate quantization cost, zero-shot dominates eval cost.
- Mid models (1.1B/7B/8B/13B): 3 primary × 19 artifacts ≈ 57 GPTQ/RTN passes ≈ **120–200 GPU-h** + PPL/zero-shot ≈ **150 GPU-h**; per-block ΔPPL curves ≈ 40 GPU-h; ablations on 7B (A1–A4) ≈ 60 GPU-h → **≈ 400 GPU-h, ~1 week on 4×80 GB**.
- 70B optional top-line (4 arms × W2 only + FP16 ref ≈ 5 artifacts) ≈ **300–500 GPU-h** (2–3 weeks on 8×80 GB).
- Tier-0 `[SYN]`: 0.6–2.2 s per probe on CPU, no deps.

**Can / cannot run in *this* workspace (measured).**
- ✅ Can: Tier-0 synthetic mechanism + metric-implementation validation (pure stdlib, seconds) — done.
- ❌ Cannot: nothing LLM-related runs here. No GPU; `torch`, `transformers`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `datasets`, `tqdm` all absent; network **disabled** (DNS fails for pypi/HF; `pip install numpy` errors) so deps cannot be added; no checkpoints, no calibration corpora.
- ❌ Storage: **/workspace has only 10.87 GB free** — cannot hold even one 7B FP16 checkpoint (~13.5 GB); 70B would need ~140 GB.
- ⚠️ `/tmp` is ~1 TB tmpfs but **did not persist between sandbox invocations** (observed twice) → any real run must write artifacts to a persistent volume, and scripts must be self-contained per invocation.
- ⚠️ Python **3.14**: wheels for the torch/transformers/lm-eval stack of the QuaRot era do not exist for it → a real run needs a rebuilt 3.10/3.11 environment.

**External resources a real run needs:** 4–8 × 80 GB GPUs; ≥2 TB persistent scratch; gated LLaMA-2/3 weights; C4 + WikiText-2; torch/transformers/accelerate/lm-eval-harness; a QuaRot-compatible rotation implementation validated by C1–C2 and N1–N3 before any headline number.

## H. Synthetic illustration vs empirical LLM results — kept strictly apart
`[SYN]` summary table (asymmetric, g = full group, 3 seeds): MSE ratio Had/no-rot = 0.12 / 0.09 / 0.08 at 4/3/2 bits; symmetric 2-bit = **3.3 (worse)**; dose-response to outlier magnitude scale 0→100 gives ratio 1.000 → 0.035; curvature-weighted output error at 2 bits RTN 0.550, RTN+Had 0.126; curvature diag non-uniformity 34.5 → 1.19.
**These numbers exist to (i) prove the metric code behaves as intended, (ii) fix the direction/sign of the hypotheses and controls, and (iii) justify freezing C\*. They carry no magnitude information about any LLM, and no expected PPL is claimed anywhere in this design.**

## I. Requirements-to-confirm (not verifiable from local source — the workspace contains only `task.json`)
g\* value; symmetric-vs-asymmetric and zero-point conventions; exact excluded-tensor list (esp. whether lm_head is quantized in the weight-only tables); whether paper's W2/W3 weight-only arms use randomized Had and whether any online Hadamard remains; GPTQ calibration corpus/size and default act-order/damping; PPL seq-len/window/stride convention; zero-shot task list and few-shot counts; whether the paper tabulates RTN+Had and GPTQ+Had separately (my grid assumes it should). These map to the `setup_5/7/11/16/17` topics; until confirmed they are **assumptions, not facts**.

The QuaRot setup facts I recited (offline folding, randomized Hadamard, group-128 weight-only recipe, reported W2 degradation of GPTQ/RTN) come from prior knowledge of the paper, NOT from any file in this workspace.

Model set (LLaMA-2 7B/13B, LLaMA-3 8B, TinyLlama smoke, optional 70B), 3 seeds for Had arms, thresholds (x3 stability, x5 fail, x10 collapse, B(2)>=2*B(4)) are proposed pre-registered choices, not task requirements.

A real execution is assumed to occur on another machine (GPUs, persistent storage, model weights, calibration corpora, 3.10/3.11 Python environment); this workspace cannot host it.
uncertainties: Quantizer configuration can reverse the direction of the Hadamard effect (measured: 3.3x worse under symmetric 2-bit vs 12x better under asymmetric). Freezing C* removes this ambiguity for the primary claim but means the primary claim is config-conditional by construction.

Group-size fade-out: whether Hadamard's advantage survives at g=32/64 on real weights is untested; if it fades, the paper-level headline becomes 'rotation substitutes for fine-grained scaling', a different claim.

Whether the reported weight-only benefit depends on residual/activation-side rotations cannot be fully excluded by any weight-only arm; the C2 control bounds but does not eliminate it.
External feasibility only: my GPU-hour estimates are order-of-magnitude planning numbers derived from arm counts and model sizes, not from any measurement in this environment.

Design deliverable accept kar liya gaya hai — ye agreed approach aur submission contract (rationale, arms, controls, analysis plan, feasibility; no executed experiment) ko poora karta hai, isliye main yahi conclude kar raha hoon.

Jo mujhe sabse sahi laga aur main explicitly endorse karta hoon:
1) FIXED vs PROPOSED ka tabular separation (A): weight-only scope, W bits ∈ {4,3,2}, aur RTN (bina calibration) / GPTQ (Hessian-approximation) baselines ko task-fixed mana gaya, baaki sab (models, g*=128, asymmetric grid, excluded tensors, seeds, thresholds) proposed choices — bilkul wahi, jo maine pin karne ko kaha tha.
2) Frozen C* + "primary conclusion sirf C* se, ablation sirf explain karegi" — ye meri sabse badi chintka (symmetric vs asymmetric se effect ka sign palat sakta hai) ka sahi design-level nivaaran hai. Symmetric ko ablation axis (A2) mein demote karna correct call hai.
3) C1 equivalence gate (folded-Had vs online-Had = identical FP16 PPL) aur pure weight-only primary arms with activations FP — sawal ke scope ke anusaar. C2 (W4A4KV4) ko grid se baahar rakhna bhi sahi hai.
4) Negative controls N1–N5, khaaskar N1 (outlier-free par ratio ≈ 1) aur N5 (MSE-clipping / per-channel scaling equivalence se "Hadamard-specific" claim ka downgrade) — ye "how" wale hisse ko ek sasti, falsifiable roop deta hai.
5) Pre-registered decision rule: r = PPL/PPL_FP16 par operational "fails" (r ≥ 5) / "collapse", monotone trend test with B(2) ≥ 2·B(4) floor, aur explicit falsification ("GPTQ+Had bhi W2 par collapse kare to claim 'improves, does not stabilize'"). Paired bootstrap + Holm–Bonferroni + models-as-replicates (pooled CI nahin) statistics bhi theek hain.
6) M1–M6 mechanism metrics, khaaskar M3 (GPTQ ka apna curvature-weighted objective rotation ke neeche) aur M4 (curvature diagonal non-uniformity 34.5 → 1.19) jo redundancy hypothesis ko testable banate hain — ye design ka sabse strong hissa hai.
7) [SYN] vs empirical LLM ka strict separation, aur §I requirements-to-confirm ko assumption hi rakha gaya hai; koi "chalaya gaya" LLM experiment claim nahin. Environment/feasibility observations (no GPU, no deps, DNS blocked, /workspace ~10.9 GB free, /tmp non-persistent, Python 3.14 wheel risk) bhi measured aur honest hain.

Do chhoti editorial baatein (revision zaroori nahin, bas final record ke liye): (i) §F.4 mein falsification threshold "r > 10" likha hai jabki upar "fail" = r ≥ 5 aur "collapse" = r ≥ 100 define kiya hai — ek hi threshold use karna better hoga; (ii) §H ka dense-orthogonal result Hadamard-specificity ka synthetic illustration hai, aapne khud §J/uncertainties mein ise real-weight control maana hai — wahi framing kaayam rakhiye.

Ek baat dohra doon: maine aapke synthetic numbers ko independently verify nahin kiya hai, ve aapke report kiye diagnostics hain; design ke liye ve directional justification ke liye kaafi hain, kisi bhi LLM magnitude ke liye nahin — jaisa aapne label kiya hai. Is point par design adequately reported hai; mera koi outstanding objection nahin.

## 1) Инспекция вводов (факты окружения)

- `/workspace` содержит **только** `task.json` (579 B). Никаких `track.md`-файлов, репозиториев, конфигов, скриптов, весов, датасетов. Текст `track.md` доступен лишь как виртуальный документ внутри task.json: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."
- Артефактов QuaRot / GPTQ / квантизации нигде в ФС нет (`find / -iname '*qurot*' -o -iname '*gptq*'` → пусто). `/opt`, `/data`, `~` — пусты/нет.
- Python 3.14.4; **нет ни torch, ни transformers, ни numpy/scipy/pandas** (grep по pip list пуст). Устанавливать нечего и нечем: **сеть отключена** (DNS: "Temporary failure in name resolution"), pip-установка невозможна.
- **GPU нет**: `nvidia-smi` → "couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver". Есть 224 CPU, ~2 TB RAM, /tmp tmpfs 1 TB — но без框架 это неприменимо.

Вывод: работаем **чисто на бумаге**, это фиксированное свойство среды, а не ограничение дизайна. Ничего не устанавливал, тяжёлого не запускал.

## 2) Skeleton подхода к дизайну

**Модели (предположение, не из брифа).** Core: LLaMA-3-8B, LLaMA-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.1; small-N для полноты факторизации: OPT-1.3B, Pythia-2.8B. Опционально-стретч: LLaMA-3-70B (только при доступном 8×A100; иначе исключить явно). Логика: ≥2 семейства × ≥2 порядков размера, чтобы вывод не был артефактом одной модели.

**Калибровка.** C4, 128 последовательностей × 2048 токенов, фиксированный seed выборки; один и тот же файл калибровки для RTN/GPTQ/QuaRot во всех условиях (альтернатива для чувствительности: WikiText-2 train).

**Метрики.** (а) Перплексия: WikiText-2 (seq 2048, sequential) + C4 held-out; (б) zero-shot accuracy (lm-eval-harness, acc_norm): LAMBADA, PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-e, ARC-c, WinoGrande (+ средний average); (в) механизм-метрики: per-channel max/mean ratio, эксцесс (kurtosis) весов и активаций до/после ротации, число каналов > μ+4σ; (г) MSE квантизационного шума по слоям.

**Основные условия (главный контракт сравнения).** FP16 reference; RTN W∈{4,3,2}; GPTQ W∈{4,3,2}; QuaRot+RTN W∈{4,3,2}; QuaRot+GPTQ W∈{4,3,2}. Group size по умолчанию 128, симметричное/асимметричное per-group — единое во всех.

**Abilations.**
- A. Размещение ротации (факторно): {identity | weight-side offline Hadamard | activation-side online Hadamard | both} × {attention-only | MLP-only | all linear}. Это напрямую отвечает "входы/выходы против весов".
- B. Group size: g ∈ {per-channel(-1), 128, 64, 32} при W=3 и W=2 — разделить выигрыш от ротации и от измельчения групп.
- C. Тип "перемешивания" как control: random Hadamard vs deterministic H₂^⊗k vs random channel permutation vs identity (perm = не-унитарный control той же стоимости). Плюс 3 seed'а ротации → разброс от выбора ротации.
- D. Пропуски слоёв: embeddings/lm_head и последний блок — не ротируются (как в QuaRot), фиксируем как протокол и проверяем отдельно.

**Управление переменными.** Одна calibration-выборка и один seed на все методы; один harness (lm-eval-harness, фиксированная версия), один context length, одна схема групп/округления; детерминированный eval; GPTQ damping 0.01 и act-order фиксированы во всех GPTQ-ветках; единственное различие между клетками — метод и наличие ротации. Отчёт: mean ± std по 3 seed'ам ротации (RTN безротационный — 1 прогон).

**Что считаем успехом (пре-регистрируемо).** W4: QuaRot+GPTQ не хуже GPTQ (ΔPPL ≤ +0.1) — проверка "не ломает". W3: закрытие ≥50% разрыва GPTQ-vs-FP16 по PPL и +≥1 п.п. среднего zero-shot против GPTQ. W2: решaющий тест — RTN/GPTQ ожидаемо коллапсируют (PPL на порядки выше FP16, accuracy ≈ chance ≈ 25–30%), успех QuaRot = PPL остаётся ограниченным (< 100 и < 10× FP16) и accuracy ≥ chance + 5 п.п., строго лучше обоих baseline. Механизм: ранговая корреляция (Spearman) между снижением outlier-статистик и ΔPPL по слоям/моделям.

**Budget/feasibility (дизайн оценивается по стоимости).** Оценка: квантизация 7–8B GPTQ ≈ 0.5–2 ч, eval (PPL + 6 задач) ≈ 1–3 ч → ~4 GPU·ч на чекпойнт (1×A100-80GB). Core-сетка 13 условий × 3 модели ≈ 150 GPU·ч; полный ablation-контур (A–D, 3 seed) ещё ~150–200 GPU·ч ⇒ **итог ~300–350 A100·ч** — в данной среде недостижимо (0 GPU, 0 сеть). Выполнимые здесь проверки: только аналитические/бумажные (стоимость раундинга Hadamard O(n log n), инвариантность A(H Hᵀ x) = Ax, рассуждение об outlier-статистике) — без ссылок на "мы посчитали". Пропорциональный scale-down при дефиците GPU: 2 модели (LLaMA-3-8B + OPT-1.3B) × W∈{3,2} × {RTN, GPTQ, QuaRot+GPTQ} + ablation A/B ⇒ ~60–80 GPU·ч.

## 3) Assumptions vs Unknowns

Домысливаю (не зафиксировано брифом, готов поменять по темам источников):
- Набор/размеры моделей и отсутствие 70B в core-сетке.
- A16KV16: активации и KV остаются FP16 (weight-only) — из брифа зафиксировано только "weight-only, W∈{4,3,2}, baselines RTN/GPTQ".
- Калибровка = C4 128×2048; group-wise quantization; g=128 как primary; асимметричный min-max per group; GPTQ damping 0.01, act-order off.
- Eval-набор: WikiText-2 + C4 PPL и 6 zero-shot задач; метрика acc_norm; lm-eval-harness.
- Что online-ротации активаций в weight-only сценарии всё равно применяются (и добавляют инференс-оверхед) — это влияет на учёт стоимости, а не только на качество.
- Успех-пороги (ΔPPL, % закрытия разрыва, chance+5 п.п.) заданы мной до эксперимента, а не взяты из источника.

Unknowns / нужно от тебя по темам `setup_5/7/11/16/17`:
1. Точный список моделей и bit-конфигурации **weight-only** из источника (есть ли там W2 g=32 как отдельная конфигурация?).
2. Калибровочный датасет/число последовательностей и ctx len в source setup.
3. Group size по умолчанию для сравнения и симметрия/асимметрия шкалы.
4. Полный eval-контур источника (PPL-датасеты, список zero-shot задач, acc vs acc_norm) — чтобы не подменять своими.
5. Входит ли 70B в scope и считается ли inference-overhead от online-Hadamard частью результата.
6. Сообщает ли источник численные ориентиры для Δ при W4 (чтобы не приписывать ему ожидание "QuaRot лучше на 4 битах").

Ничего из источников я пока не цитировал числами: их тексты мне недоступны, только topic-идентификаторы.

**Что правлю при написании полного дизайна:**

1) Раздели явно offline vs online часть QuaRot и последствия для веса-онли сценария. В W-only weight-side Hadamard — это бесплатная предобработка весов (входит в чекпойнт), а activation-side — рантайм-оверхед на инференсе, за который приходится платить без квантизации активаций. Мне нужна отдельная строка в дизайне: какой из двух вкладов отвечает за выигрыш, и как ты это разводишь через ablation A. Не сваливай "QuaRot" в один чёрный ящик.

И заранее реши, что является operational-определением коллапса (PPL > X×FP16 ИЛИ accuracy в пределах chance±), иначе потом начнётся подгонка порога под результат. Тот же режим — для успеха QuaRot: твои пороги (ΔPPL ≤ 0.1 на W4, ≥50% закрытия разрыва на W3, chance+5 п.п. на W2) оставляю, но они должны быть подписаны как pre-registered и явно помечены "не из источника".
